4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.name: Archaeological and topographic map of the Carthaginian ruins
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.short_description: Having been invaded and destroyed many times, the city of Carthage was then subject to various sackings, and its ruins served as a quarry for nearby towns. The site was rediscovered in the 19th century and became fashionable following the publication of Flaubert's novel *Salammbô*. Archaeologists soon felt the need for the different sites to be mapped, and in 1833 a Danish marine, Falbe, put forward a proposal for the *Recherches sur l'Emplacement de Carthage*. Thanks to the maps drawn up by the army's geographical service and military engineers, by the end of the 19th century archaeologists were able to conduct more detailed work, particularly with regards to the division of land.
keywords: Phoenician, punic, roman ruins; archaeological excavations; Tunisia

4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.name: Carlo de Rossetti (consul of the Grand Duke of Tuscany) gives notice of a new ferry boat service between Alexandria (Egypt) and Constantinople operated by a Tuscan steamship
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.short_description: The steamboat Il Generoso had three classes of service: the first-class ticket cost 42.5 Thalers and the second class one 30 Thalers; they both included meals. By contrast, the third-class ticket (12 Thalers) did not entitle one to meals. The trip lasted five days. According to the poster, the steamboat Il Generoso was equipped with “very confortable cabins and living rooms, including a special living room for ladies”.
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.author: Cristina Francioli

4bf6a5a2-2ef7-5efd-930f-e900942ddaa6.name: *La Péri: thirteen costume sketches*
4bf6a5a2-2ef7-5efd-930f-e900942ddaa6.short_description: *La Péri* is a fantastical ballet in two acts with the scenario written by Theophile Gautier and the music by Burgmüller. This ballet, first performed in 1843, brought the audience to a grand Egyptian palace. Théophile Gautier dreamt of visiting Egypt, where his friend Gerard de Nerval had been living and sending him details to help him make the ballet more realistic.

4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.name: Map of the Network of Caravans
4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.short_description: This sketch shows the network of caravans in Egypt, North Eastern Africa and Western Arabia.
keywords: Egypt; North Eastern Africa; Western Arabia; Caravans

4c6c73fd-b2b8-5169-9f5b-defe03f3bbce.name: *Bilder aus Mekka von C. Snouck Hurgronje*, published Leiden, 1889
4c6c73fd-b2b8-5169-9f5b-defe03f3bbce.short_description:
*Bilder aus Mekka* was published in 1889 by the Dutch orientalist Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje. Consisting of 20 collotype prints mounted on 18 leaves, it is one of the earliest photographic records of the Hajj, preceded only by photographs taken in 1881 by Muhammed Sadiq Bey. *Bilder aus Mekka*came one year after *Bilder-Atlas zu Mekka*. This was a collection of lithographs including images predominantly of Mecca and portraits of pilgrims, taken by Snouck himself on his research trip to Jidda and Mecca between August 1884–August 1885. Alongside this he published *Mekka*a work that focussed on the history of Mecca and the origins of Islam. Following on from the publication of these two volumes, and having not been able to photograph the hajj himself, Snouck used images taken by a Meccan physician named ‘Abd al-Ghaffar of the Hajj of August 1888 to publish *Bilder aus Mekka*.  
Snouck met ‘Abd al-Ghaffar during his stay in Mecca in 1885, and although ‘Abd al-Ghaffar was already familiar with photography, Snouck is supposed to have helped refine his skills and he became Snouck’s photographic assistant during the six months he was in Mecca.  
The photographs include views of Mecca, Mina and Arafat, and depict the various stages of Hajj. Although traces of ‘Abd al-Ghaffar’s signature are still visible on the photographs, there is clear evidence of an attempt to erase them by Snouck. A summary text written by Snouck opens the volume and a list of plates precedes the images.
4c6c73fd-b2b8-5169-9f5b-defe03f3bbce.holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
4c6c73fd-b2b8-5169-9f5b-defe03f3bbce.method_for_datation: The date and publication details are included within the book.
4c6c73fd-b2b8-5169-9f5b-defe03f3bbce.bibliography: Sheehi, S., *The Arab Imago: A Social History of Portrait Photography, 1860–1910*, Princeton: Princeton University Press, 2016.
4c6c73fd-b2b8-5169-9f5b-defe03f3bbce.author: Qaisra Khan
keywords: Book; Hajj; Hijaz; Holy place; Ka'ba; Medina; Mosque; Paper; Pilgrimage; Prayer; Prophet Muhammad; Religion; Mecca; photograph

4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.name: Original sheet music of 'The Portugueza'
4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.short_description: Original sheet music of “The Portugueza”, initially a contest song against the British Ultimatum. It became the national anthem after the Republican Revolution.
4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.dates: Published in the supplement of the *Ocidente*, n. 405, 21 March 1890
4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.artist: Henrique Lopes de Mendonça; Alfredo Keil
4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.author: DGPC

4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.name: *The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia, Volume 1, title page*
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.short_description: This vignette depicts the façade of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, located on the spot where it is bellieved both the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his burial took place. David Roberts, the prominent Scottish Orientalist painter(1796-1864) visited at Easter time, when the square in front of the church was crowded with pilgrims and traders selling their wares. Nevertheless, he shows the scene not with contemporary life milling around the church, but enlivened only with his usual repertoire of carefully staged, oriental types. Originally, the church was accessed by a flight of steps from the main street of Jerusalem, but in the 11th century, the entrance was moved its south side, where it remains to this day, including he double-doorway, its right section walled up since 1187. Only the original, carved lintels still recorded by Roberts had to be removed after an earthquake in 1927.
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis

4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.name: Declaration by the Bey of Tunis assuring that in future wars with any European power prisoners will not be enslaved
4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.short_description:
This declaration was an annex to a treaty between the King of Sardinia (who ruled over Piedmont, Genoa and Sardinia) and the Bey (who ruled Tunis), concluded by British Admiral Baron Exmouth, who lead a military expedition against the Berber states in 1816. The Bey declared that in case of future wars with any European power, “none of the prisoners made on either side shall be consigned to slavery, but treated with all humanity as prisoners of war, until regularly exchanged according to European practice”.  
The Exmouth expedition was aimed at stopping Barbary corsairs from raiding European shipping in the Mediterranean. At the time, privateering was considered a legitimate form of warfare by European and North African countries alike. Only in 1856 did France, the United Kingdom and other European powers (except from Spain) declare privateering illegal.
4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.author: Edoardo Garis, Giulia Barrera

4ceec2b5-7808-56c2-b795-ced282fa861d.name: *24 hour optical telegraphy presented to the minister by a marine officer and used by the coast signalling services* (1802)
4ceec2b5-7808-56c2-b795-ced282fa861d.short_description: The telegraph was an important piece of technology for Napoléon I, as it allowed him to send information quickly from both land and sea during the War of the First Coalition. A huge network of telegraph lines was created during his reign.

4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.short_description: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.

4e04768a-5d14-5f0c-94df-814f2d4400f7.name: *The Exhibition!! The triumph of industry*
4e04768a-5d14-5f0c-94df-814f2d4400f7.short_description: Alfred Rodiba (1848–1926) was the artist of many dystopian works, a very fashionable theme at the time. Although he appreciated the 1889 Exposition Universelle (world fair), the cartoonist inside him also noticed a "universal" worship of industry which made everyone unaware of the pollution these inventions were producing.

4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.name: *The First Train in Spain: Inaugurated 28 October 1848*
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.description: The railway connecting Barcelona and Mataró was the first one to be inaugurated in Spain. This train connected two important industrial hubs of Catalonia, as an example of the industrial development of this area in the middle of the 19th century.
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.author: Ana Cabrera

4e2c253d-3f40-5817-ad41-b7fde8b9f4b8.name: Confidential report related to the Iraqi State Railways and the Trans-Iranian Railway
4e2c253d-3f40-5817-ad41-b7fde8b9f4b8.description: Report surveying the state of the railways and the gauges used by the Iraqi State Railways and the Trans-Iranian Railway between 1942 and 1944. The report is incomplete; 11 pages are related to Iraq (pp. 54-85), while 16 pages cover Iran (pp. 73-160). The typewritten text is accompanied by photomechanical prints and technical drawings of locomotives. The report might have been produced both by the British or the American intelligence. It includes The Second World War-era British military map showing regional railway networks (established or under construction) in the (ex) Ottoman Empire. Manuscript annotations highlight the geopolitical interests of various nations involved in their construction. The piece also has the stamp of the Survey Directorate, GHQ Middle East.
4e2c253d-3f40-5817-ad41-b7fde8b9f4b8.author: Moez Dridi

50134a0e-a943-5f25-a36c-43032ad0dd5e.name: Bob Walter [veiled dancer]
50134a0e-a943-5f25-a36c-43032ad0dd5e.short_description: The "serpentine dance", invented by Mary Louise Fuller, was copied by many dancers, and even parodied. Like Fuller, these dancers also used veils and lighting effects, characteristics typical of the Art Nouveau movement.

51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.name: Tramway
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.short_description: This railway carraige from the French Bône-Guelma company inaugurated, in April 1879, the opening of the first section of a 100 km long line which connected Tunis to Algeria. In 1800 it also acquired the Tuni-Sousse and Tunis-Bizerte lines, and thus gained a monopoly over the construction of railway lines in Tunisia, while the Italians bought the small Tunis-La Goulette-La Marsa (TGM) railway track.
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar

523087c9-9a15-54a0-b37b-745c43c2cb51.name: An olive oil factory run by an Italian migrant in Monastir (Tunisia)
523087c9-9a15-54a0-b37b-745c43c2cb51.short_description: According to a 1895 survey by the Italian Chamber of Commerce of Tunisia, 82 modern olive-oil industries operated in the country; 34 (41 per cent) were run by Italians, 24 by French nationals, 19 by Tunisians and the remaining five by persons of other nationalities.
523087c9-9a15-54a0-b37b-745c43c2cb51.author: Giulia Barrera

52e912d6-db07-5f7b-a1e2-6593559e25f6.name: Illustrated guide and timetable for travelling in the Orient. Featuring description of Constantinople and the most important cities in Turkey, Egypt, Greece, etc.
52e912d6-db07-5f7b-a1e2-6593559e25f6.short_description: The growth of tourism entailed the production of travel guides, such as this one, which gave the potential tourist advice for travelling in "the Orient" - here meaning Greece, Turkey and Egypt.  This page provides a timetable for steam boats with timings which coincide with the international train lines, such as the Orient Express.

52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.short_description: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt

5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.name: *Illustrated dictionary of Tunisia: the people and things of Tunisia*
5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.short_description: Italian immigration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. This is evident from advertisements such as this one, where the headquarters, names and addresses of a Tunis-based firm are Italian.

5426a620-cbfc-5b20-bed9-14fa1801de7d.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)
5426a620-cbfc-5b20-bed9-14fa1801de7d.short_description: Popular postcard from Turkey showing the costume worn by various people, according to occupation, activity, etc. At this time Turkish financial officials worked under European management.
keywords: costume; diplomacy; fashion; court life; economy; finance; Ottoman; Tercüman; travel; traveller; Orientalism

544117f8-c7fb-5075-b36e-315986c47bec.name: Transport plan of Beirut
544117f8-c7fb-5075-b36e-315986c47bec.short_description: This map shows a plan of transport terminals in Beirut in 1891.
544117f8-c7fb-5075-b36e-315986c47bec.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury

54f861aa-1d28-5c1b-b3c3-07e65ff10862.name: 'Picture of the Tents of the Turks'. Photographer: H. A. Mirza & Sons
54f861aa-1d28-5c1b-b3c3-07e65ff10862.description:
This image shows the tents of the Ottoman Turkish troops at their camp at Medina. Despite the apparently secular nature of the subject, and the fact that the camp does not depict a stopping-off point on the hadj, the laudatory poetry and prose makes clear the relevance of the image to the experience of the hadj – that is, that the Turks, as ‘military people of the highest rank’ serve Islam by defending and enabling the passage to Mecca and Medina for other Muslims.  
  
As with the other photographs in this album (Photo 174/1-13), whose subjects are architectural and landscape, the figures are not the subject of the image. However, a detailed examination of the image shows the soldiers going about their day-to-day activities, such as cooking and eating. The method by which the ground would have been prepared before a tent was erected is indicated by the empty low circular foundation in the lower left corner of the image. In the distance, in the right-hand background of the image, beyond the dry-stone wall delineating the camp, palm groves and permanent dwellings can be identified.
54f861aa-1d28-5c1b-b3c3-07e65ff10862.dimensions: Mount (external): 35 x 44,6 cm; Mount (internal): 20,2 x 27,3 cm [landscape]
materials: Mottled blue-tinted window mount, card, gelatin silver print, indigo ink (printed), red ink (hand-painted)

55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.name: A map of Tunisia (1:1,600,000) showing Italian agricultural settlements, mines, coral- and sponge-fishing areas and boat lines
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.short_description: The green rectangles on the map indicate Italian agricultural settlements; the number of settlers is indicated as well. In 1906 the majority of the Italian peasants had settled around Tunis and the Gulf of Hammamet. By contrast, few Italian peasants had settled in the South and in the interior of the country (the map indicated only 300 Italian peasants near Sfax and 400 near Kef).
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.author: Giulia Barrera

55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.name: *A Muslim man praying*
55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.short_description: One of the drawings by Fortuny, one of the most important European painters of the last quarter of the 19th century. He travelled to Morocco in 1863 and he was taken by the light, colour and characters of the country. He was an important collector of Islamic artworks, some of them depicted in his paintings.
55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.author: Ámparo López

562cd119-0bf1-544d-a90a-b4094899b356.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911)
562cd119-0bf1-544d-a90a-b4094899b356.short_description: Portrait of minister Sayed Ahmed Pasha Arabi (Urabi). In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

563af385-75b3-5cc2-a71e-50f89ce6f746.name: *Andalucía under Arab rule. Exposition of 1900*
563af385-75b3-5cc2-a71e-50f89ce6f746.short_description: This exhibition on the Arab presence in Andalucía was featured in the 1900 Exposition Universelle (world fair), reflecting a fashion for the rediscovery of Spain's North African past. Recently, for example, buildings in Granada and Córdoba had been rebuilt to host dances and fantasias. The artist of this poster, Eugène Grasset, has combined his two principal sources of inspiration - curiosity towards the Arab world, and japonese-inspired aesthetics.
keywords: World fairs; Orientalism; japan; north Africa

5686a4e1-e33b-5ad7-8f7a-20b3b101f2ca.name: Petar (Pezia) Petrovich (2nd half of the 19th century – 1900)
5686a4e1-e33b-5ad7-8f7a-20b3b101f2ca.short_description: Portrait of Petar (Pezia) Petrovic. He was Chief of the Albanian Mirdita tribes fighting against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.name: *Excavation of the Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel*
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.short_description:
An intrepid and versatile Frenchman, Linant came to Egypt in 1818. In Cairo he adopted the life of an Ottoman Turk, but was known and consulted by European residents and visitors as well as by the Pasha of Egypt, Muhammad Ali. At various times his talents were employed as a geographer, explorer, engineer, cartographer and draughtsman.  
His first adventure was an expedition to Upper Egypt that Henry Salt, British Consul-General in Egypt , took to Abu Simbel in 1818-19. Although there were other artists in the party it is likely that this watercolour is by Linant and that it depicts Salt's attempts to clear away the ever encroaching sand from the facade of the Great Temple. Linant took part in several subsequent expeditions up the Nile, and was one of the first Europeans to reach the Pharaonic sites of Meroe and Musawarat.
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum

574ec553-46f8-5bdf-871c-23a4e10a1779.name: Bellino copy
574ec553-46f8-5bdf-871c-23a4e10a1779.short_description: Hand drawing by Bellino of BM 22502. Bellino’s technique produced wonderfully accurate copies, despite the fact that cuneiform was not yet deciphered.
keywords: Cuneiform; drawing; archaeology; exploration; collection; collector; museums; travel; traveller; inscription

578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.name: Palais du Bardo
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.short_description: This postcard shows the throne room of the Palais du Bardo, with its rich furnishings and monumental chandeliers hanging from the ceiling. The bey's throne sits in the centre, surrounded by paintings of the princes of the Husainid dynasty, painted wooden ceilings, mirrors and console tables carved and painted with gold leaf, and with two great rooms on either side. From the 18th century onwards the Husainid beys continuously expanded and decorated the Palais du Bardo. The architecture and furniture all indicate a strong European, particularly Italian, influence.
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
keywords: Palais du Bardo; beylical throne; European influences; Italian influences

57ffa9ee-eaef-5f59-b4a3-2237ac46b63a.name: The ivory trade
57ffa9ee-eaef-5f59-b4a3-2237ac46b63a.short_description: Although banned in 1989, in the 19th century the ivory trade was flourishing. Many different objects, all marketed to a wealthy buyer, were made from this material: decorations, piano keys, knife handles, combs, fans, umbrella handles, and more.

58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.name: *The Royal Palace at Buda as a University*
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.description: At the end of the 18th century, the Hungarian aristocracy expressed a desire to turn the reconstructed Royal Palace at Buda back into a royal residence. Following reconstruction of 1750–1770, the palace was used only once by Queen Maria Theresia. From 1777, the University of Nagyszombat (Trnava) was located in Buda, and from this time up until 1784 the Royal Palace was used as the university. This is the only representation of the royal castle in Buda being used as the university during the 18th century.
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.short_description: The engraving and etching is an excellent example of a Baroque *veduta* representing the Royal Palace at Buda, a building of outstanding importance, being used as university at the end of the 18th century.
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.method_for_datation: On the basis of the signature
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.obtention: Transferred from the Capital’s collection in 1945.
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.bibliography: *Budapest az Újkorban* (*Budapest in the Modern Times*), (ed. G. Szvoboda Dománszky), Budapest, 1995, p.23.
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.artist: Johann Ernst Mansfeld (Mannsfeld) (1739, Prague – 1796, Vienna) and Ferdinand Pichler (18th century)
58863077-c5fb-5b7d-bc4c-25779a9e566e.author: Beatrix Basics
keywords: Engraving; etching; university; education; school;  Maria Theresia; Buda; Nagyszombat; Trnava; Tyrnau

58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.name: *Vue d'Alger*
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.short_description: These two original lithographs depict the city of al-Jaza'ir (Algiers) prior to the English bombardment led by Lord Exmouth on 26 August 1816. The regency was ruled first by the *Beylerbeys* (general governors) from 1518 to 1587, then by the Pashas from 1587 to 1659, the *Aghas* from 1659 to 1671 and the Deys from 1671 to 1830. The reign of the final Dey of Algiers, Hussein, lasted 12 years until the French conquest in 1830.
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.author: Dalila Orfali

59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.name: *The political refugee*
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.short_description: The cartoonist Honoré Daumier (1808–1879) was one of the first to be interested in the theme of migration, and drew many cartoon strips which dealt with the difficulties of exile. He did some more comic drawings on this theme, which are harder to understand. In this image, published in a series on the theme of the "Bohemian" (an artistic community attempting to live without restrictions), he highlights the gaze of his contemporaries on the "other" or the "stranger". The image also mocks the suspicious young woman just as much as the asylum seeker.

598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.name: *Mr Drovetti and his entourage measuring a fragment of the Colossus in Upper Egypt*
598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.short_description: Bernardino Drovetti (1776–1852) an Italian who joined the French army, was made a diplomat after having elicited Napoléon I's sympathy by saving his step-brother. Having been sent to Egypt as a consul, he then collected antiquities and thus portrayed himself as a defender of discovered treasures. He is pictured here with his team holding a plumb line in front of a colossus. Jean-Jacques Rifaud is leaning on the sculpture's head and dressed in an imitation of the local style. Dovretti later sold his collections to the Prince of Piedmont, to King Charles X of France and to the King of Prussia.

59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.name: Hydrographic map of Lower Egypt and part of the Suez isthmus, engraved at the Dépôt de la Guerre
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.short_description: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer passionate about Egypt, played a key role alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps in drawing and constructing the Suez Canal. He was given the title 'Bey' by the Egyptian viceroy, appointed director of Egyptian public works, and contributed to the irrigation of farmland. The map drawn in 1855 included the barriers; the outline of the Suez Canal and the railways were added in 1882.
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds

5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.name: *The Approach to Nablus (Shechem)*
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.short_description: This image shows the approach to Nablus (at the time believed to mark the biblical Shechem, according to the Bible first capital of the Kingdom of Israel and situated in the vicinity of several important Abrahamic sites). The caption further explains that the view is taken through the olive groves on the eastern side of the city, and that 'the gate is shown beneath the minaret'. The artist who created this work, Josiah Wood Whymper, was a British watercolour painter, engraver, and illustrator, who apparently never left Britain, but provided a prolific body of engravings to publishers, in particular the Society for the Promotion of Christian Knowledge. This print originally appeared in Vol. 1, page 243 of Charles William Wilson's  'Pituresque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt', published between 1881 and 1884.
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.artist: Josiah Wood Whymper (after a pencil drawing by Harry Fenn 1838–1911)
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis

5aea6a37-19f3-5c61-ac76-f38f3922c376.name: Fraser Album Artist: *The Bullock-Drawn Carriage of Prince Mirza Babur*
5aea6a37-19f3-5c61-ac76-f38f3922c376.short_description: 'The special chariot of the son of the spiritual preceptor of the horizons (Murshidzada-i afaq), Mirza Babur Bahadur'. Mirza Babur (b. 1796) was one of the sons of the penultimate Mughal emperor, Akbar II (reg. 1806–37), and the honorific title refers to the Emperor's role as a Sufi spiritual leader. Mirza Babur appears in a group portrait dated 1812 in the British Library, depicting Akbar II with three other sons (see J. P. Losty, M. Roy, *Mughal India: Art, Culture and Empire*, London 2012, pp. 209-10, fig. 150). 'Zana, bullock-cart driver, Ahir Jadubansi \[of the cowherd caste of the Yadava race, descendants of Shri Krishna\], inhabitant of Delhi'. The Fraser Album, which emerged from amongst the papers of the family of that name in Scotland in 1979, consists of more than ninety watercolours of high quality, and aside from their technical and aesthetic features provide an extraordinary portrait of life in and around Delhi in the early 19th century, an area which was relatively unknown to the British at that date, with Mughal control ceded to them only in 1803 and the Emperor nominally in power. James Baillie Fraser (1783–1856) and his brother William (1784–1835) came from Inverness. William went to India aged 16 as a trainee political officer in the East India Company; James arrived a year later in a commercial position in Calcutta. While James was a talented artist himself, publishing collections of views of the Himalayas and of Calcutta, when he joined William in Delhi in 1815 the two brothers commissioned local artists to depict servants, tradesmen and figures from the irregular military units, some of which were employed by the British, including Gurkha soldiers and the colourfully-attired troopers of bodies such as Skinner's Horse. More than one artist was employed on the paintings which go to make up the album: some are usually attributed to Ghulam ʽAli Khan, but it is likely that the rest were produced by other members of his family. The works date between 1815 and 1820. The three lots in the present sale capture the richness of ceremonial life in Delhi, and are also representative of the British fascination for types of transport and servants which appears in other more typical examples of Company School painting.
5aea6a37-19f3-5c61-ac76-f38f3922c376.bibliography: Archer, M., and T. Falk, *India Revealed: the Art and Adventures of James and William Fraser 1801-35*, London, 1989: 108.
materials: Pencil and watercolour, heightened with bodycolour and gold, on paper

5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.name: Official Bulletin establishing the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office (PTT.)
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.description: An Official Bulletin, signed by the Sultan of Morocco Mulay Yusuf ibn al-Hasan I, which concerns the creation of the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office. The establishment of this Office was part of an agreement between Morocco and the French authorities, to promote the telecommunications sector, and put a stop to attempts by Britain and Spain to capitalise from it. The text defined the functions and services of the Office and its organisation. After independence, the Office became the Ministry (*Makhzen*) of Post, Telegraph and Telephone.
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.holder: National Library of the Kingdom of Morocco
keywords: Postal service; post offices; Moroccan postal service; communication; routes; rakkas; delivery; French in Morocco; protectorate; postal network

5cada7e5-c863-5bd3-ae0b-41ec4765404d.name: *Grand Vizier*
5cada7e5-c863-5bd3-ae0b-41ec4765404d.short_description: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc.
keywords: costume; Orientalism; drawing; travel; traveller; fashion; court life

5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.name: Maronite Benevolent Catholic Society of New York rule book
5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.short_description: A copy of the book of regulations for the Maronite Benevolent Catholic Society of New York, a charitable society aimed at helping the needy within the Maronite community. It provided financial support for the poor and free medication for the sick, and financially supported burial of the deceased. The book outlines the objectives, rules and structure of the association.
5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.name: An open letter from the Tuscan community in Constantinople to the Chargé d’Affairs of Tuscany, protesting the detention of three Italian democrats exiled by Ottoman authorities
5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.short_description: Italian communities abroad actively supported the movement for Italian national unification known as “Risorgimento”. The Italian community in Constantinople raised funding to donate a cannon to the Kingdom of Sardinia, which in 1848 was at war with the Austrian Empire. After the Kingdom of Sardinia’s army was defeated, conflicts between the most moderate wing of the nationalist movement and the republicans (supporters of Giuseppe Mazzini) broke out and the Kingdom of Sardinia’s authorities started to persecute the latter.
5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.author: Massimo Sanacore

5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.name: Lake d'Orta. Villa Crespi
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.short_description:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near the lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), in order to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
He had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build a villa in the Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
The villa features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors, made with marbles of great value, imported from several different countries. It required 12 year of works to be completed. The estate comprises a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls, with valuable wrought iron gates.
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.author: Ignazio Galella

5dc7ada7-555b-5b55-b162-ac8e969fa698.name: *A Place for Breakfast in the Algerian Pavillion* \[Paris Exhibition 1878\]
5dc7ada7-555b-5b55-b162-ac8e969fa698.short_description: Within the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion This scene shows a refreshing small space that the author used to depict the tradition of sharing a couscous with friends or work colleagues. The recreation of an – even only hypothetically - typical setting had to include also works and related activities.
5dc7ada7-555b-5b55-b162-ac8e969fa698.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
5dc7ada7-555b-5b55-b162-ac8e969fa698.author: Marina Minozzi

5e2b03cb-5bee-5604-be76-35ecf0de0e45.name: *Valahian Caravan*
5e2b03cb-5bee-5604-be76-35ecf0de0e45.short_description: In Wallachia and Moldavia transportation of merchandise by land was done similarly to the Arab and Ottoman world, but using big carts pulled by horses instead of camel caravans. Both the vehicle and a group of carts travelling together for commercial purposes were called "chervan”, a term derived from the Turkish word "kervan", meaning "caravan". The lithograph, depicting a carriage drawn by 12 horses and followed by a second vehicle, was printed in Vienna and its legend (*Wallachian carriage*) is written below the image in German, Hungarian and French.

5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.name: Postal map
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.short_description: The network of routes for sending messages and transporting troops and supplies was carried out with a relay system, established in the 16th century in the Ottoman Empire. The messengers, who conveyed dispatches throughout the country, were identified as the Tatars. Private or personal correspondence was not a part of that relay system; it was built to fulfil governmental needs. Because of this reason the *reaya* (public) created an alternative postal method by using caravans, pilgrims, and private couriers called *ulaks*. The *Tanzimat* Decree, which was the declaration of process included reformation, modernization and westernization in 1839, proved that the Ottoman Empire was focused on its policy of changing governing to be more like modern Western European-style administrative practices.
keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication

5ec581f1-3f8e-5a5c-bdc5-c2d1b4b525e3.name: A postcard advertising the Singer sewing machine and at the same time supporting Italian colonial expansion in Libya
5ec581f1-3f8e-5a5c-bdc5-c2d1b4b525e3.short_description: This postcard sends the message that the Italian colonisers brought modernity to Libya. Both the sewing machine and the plane in the background epitomise modernity. The soldier is sewing an Italian flag. The postcard’s message is at the same time political and commercial.
5ec581f1-3f8e-5a5c-bdc5-c2d1b4b525e3.author: Giulia Barrera

5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.name: *Thebes. Hypogea. Pictures drawn after the covering of the mummies*
5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.short_description: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.name: Various hydraulic machines used in Egypt to water the land. The first method is constructed in a linear manner and provides the land with water whenever it is in need. Part of "Dyke A"
5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.short_description: The captain of the Danish Royal Marines Fréderic-Louis Norden (1708–1742) was sent to Egypt to draw monuments. His collection, *Voyage d’Égypte et de Nubie*, was published posthumously in 1755, and was added to in 1795 by the inclusion of scientific commentaries by Louis Langlès (1763–1824), founder of the École Spéciale des Langues Orientales and curator of oriental manuscripts at the Bibliothèque Impériale. This new edition, a product of Europen "Egyptomania", introduced some splendid new illustrations. In this particular page, the artist has focused on traditional hydraulic machinery.

5f7be233-5b3b-542f-9b15-c37a25a0932f.name: Plan of Jerusalem
5f7be233-5b3b-542f-9b15-c37a25a0932f.short_description: Plan of the area to the South of the Haram al-Sharif, Jerusalem, showing the location of the shafts dug by Lieut. Charles Warren, R.E., and his team to explore the topography of ancient Jerusalem. This work established the history of the development of the Old City of Jerusalem. While engaged in this work, Warren also carried out a major study of the economy of Jerusalem in the period 1867–1870, which was published in the SWP in 1884.

5f941ae8-9023-5935-99ef-eaae452485b9.name: Egyptian Pavilion of Chocolate and Cocoa Factories – Michele Talmone – Turin
5f941ae8-9023-5935-99ef-eaae452485b9.short_description: For the International Exhibition in Turin in 1911 the Talmone Company built an Egyptian Pavilion resembling an Egyptian temple. The architecture is a pastiche of ancient and oriental architectural elements. An interior stained-glass window shows a stunning view of the desert walked by a caravan.
5f941ae8-9023-5935-99ef-eaae452485b9.holder: The House of Antique Tin Boxes

5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.name: *Remains of the Garments of Prince Philip of Castile, son of Ferdinand III*
5fa7cbde-981a-5031-afe4-3cc242fd75c7.description: Drawing of part of the garment of Prince D. Felipe, son of the King of Castile Ferdinand III. These garments are a good example of the rich silk textile from the Arab workshops of the Al-Andalus.

601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.name: *Dar al-Baladiyya, Damascus*
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.short_description: Built between 1892 to 1894, the Dar al-Baladiyya was a prestigious edifice in stone. With its neo-classical elements and prominent middle projection, it was designed to display the power of the “new” state. The purpose of building the City Hall was functional, since the administrative workload, which rapidly increased after the reforms of the administrative system had to be accommodated.
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

60b297ce-03b5-5b81-8b64-abe6de2613c4.name: The Various Ages of Woman
60b297ce-03b5-5b81-8b64-abe6de2613c4.short_description: The National Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions in Rome was founded by Lamberto Loria (1855–1913), an Italian ethnologist passionate about the need to record the agro-pastoral Italian culture that was disappearing to industrialization and the consequent migration from the countryside towards the cities. In 1911, 50th anniversary of Italian unification, or Risorgimento, Loria organized the Italian Ethnographic Exhibition in Rome. Through the help of a group of coworkers, Loria gathered over three-thousand objects from exhibition of 1911, which today form the principal nucleus of the Museum’s collections.
60b297ce-03b5-5b81-8b64-abe6de2613c4.holder: Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions
60b297ce-03b5-5b81-8b64-abe6de2613c4.copyright: Copyright image: Roma, Istituto Centrale per la Demoetnoantropologia, ICDE, Archivio storico.
60b297ce-03b5-5b81-8b64-abe6de2613c4.author: Marina Minozzi
keywords: Popular traditions; ethnology; anthropology; post-unitarian Italian society; work; agriculture; pastoralism; ethnographic exhibition; exhibition; collection; collector; museum; woman; migration; internal migration; city; countriside; rural space

60b8885d-3137-5d4a-a32b-9222e6ec69cb.name: Two bills from Beirut port
60b8885d-3137-5d4a-a32b-9222e6ec69cb.short_description: Two bills from Beirut port, both for a value of 22 Ottoman pounds. The bill on the right is dated to 1 September 1895 and the bill on the left is dated to 24 July 1899.
60b8885d-3137-5d4a-a32b-9222e6ec69cb.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury

61490dc8-89a2-5eeb-adc6-a5f3b1bd62aa.name: *His Excellency Mirza Abulhassan Khan, Persian ambassador*
61490dc8-89a2-5eeb-adc6-a5f3b1bd62aa.short_description: Mirza Abulhassan Khan was sent to London by the Persian Shah in order to learn English. His visit, in the capacity of ambassador, attracted much attention from various European courts who did not know anything about Persia.

61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.name: Messageries Maritimes's Istanbul-themed posters
61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.short_description: *Messageries maritimes* was a French merchant shipping company. When it began, it operated on routes to the Middle East. Its ships were used as troop transports during the Crimean War, and were so helpful for the army that the Emperor gave the company the right to operate on the Bordeaux-Brazil route as thanks. This was the first French transatlantic line equipped with steamers. The following year, the *Société générale maritime* (later called *Compagnie générale transatlantique*) received the North Atlantic lines. From 1871 to 1914 the shipping company, now called *Compagnie des messageries maritimes*, saw its Golden Age.

61dba05c-1c18-5736-85f3-727803bfc389.name: *Housing in the Pierrefitte Chateau and Gardens* \[…\] *Payable in installments* \[…\] *\[Epargne Foncière Immobilière des Quinze - Vingts\]: open to visitors every day.*
61dba05c-1c18-5736-85f3-727803bfc389.short_description: Pierrefitte-sur-Seine was still a farming village in the mid 19th century. The construction of the Paris-Lille railway line in 1859 brought in rich Parisians in search of country air. The town was transformed again in the 20th century, thanks to the construction of factories in the Saint-Demis plains and the arrival of people looking for cheaper housing. The first tramway was also built in 1901. This poster advertises housing in an area outside the tramway's reach, which had remained wooded and rural, and was equipped with the most modern technologies available, such as gas and telephone.

61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.name: *The Port of Constanţa*
61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.short_description: The Black Sea port of Constanța underwent its first modernization while Dobruja, the province where it is situated, was under Ottoman control. In 1857, when the Ottoman government hired a British company to build a railway in Dobruja, the concluded contract also stipulated the reconstruction of the Constanța port. Completed in 1864, it was still a small harbor with a wooden dock, a dam and one cereals depot. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania, a law was issued in 1885 for the “improvement and augmentation” of the port. In 1896 its modernization was leased to a French enterprise but due to some disagreements, three years later the state took over the works, which were led by architect Anghel Saligny. Inaugurated in 1909, the new port had 3 dams, several docks, depots, silos, an oil basin, an electric plant.

61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.name: Traditional peasant attire
61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.short_description: Peasants and ordinary people's clothes did not change much over the centuries. It generally consisted of a shorter, narrower and darker coloured pair of baggy *shirwal* trousers for winter, and another pair in a lighter beige or khaki colour for the summer. This was paired with a cotton shirt or vest, called a *sudriye*, and a short embroidered *abaya*. A *keffiye*, a large scarf made of white cotton, was worn on the head with a *lebbede* or *'agal* on top.
61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
materials: The costumes were made of cotton and silk

6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.name: Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) / Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.short_description: Portrait of Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) on horseback/ Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen. He was elected Prince of Romania on the recommendation of Napoleon III in 1866. In 1881, after achieving formal independence from the Ottoman Empire, Carol declared himself King of Romania.

6345c672-a66e-5ec9-a903-e3ddfbdcb159.name: *Chiefs of nomadic Arab tribes in Syria visit the Abbot Desmazure, Latin father of the Saint-Sépulcre in the Convent of the Latin Fathers of Jerusalem, built on mount Gihon*
6345c672-a66e-5ec9-a903-e3ddfbdcb159.short_description: Syrian tribal leaders visited the Abbot Desmazure in 1827, in the Convent of the Latin Fathers of Jerusalem. He happily volunteered to show Jerusalem to visitors passing through the city, and tried hard to find diplomatic solutions to the religious tensions within the Christian community.

637e27e9-204e-5721-869e-ad4380dc0140.name: *The great celestial globe. 1900 Exposition Universelle.*
637e27e9-204e-5721-869e-ad4380dc0140.short_description: A great celestial globe, measuring 50 metres in diameter and located near the Champ de Mars, was one of the proposed attractions for the 1900 Paris World Fair. A restaurant sat beneath it, and popular science activities inside the globe allowed the visitors to learn about astronomy. Other than the globe's colossal dimensions, the poster also foresees great crowds of people visiting the exhibit.

63c94290-4824-5fcc-88ab-904bca42d8ca.name: Hussein Kamil, Sultan of Egypt (1853–1917)
63c94290-4824-5fcc-88ab-904bca42d8ca.short_description: Portrait of Hussein Kamil, Sultan of Egypt (1853–1917). On 18 December 1914 the British deposed the Khedive Abbas Hilmi II and declared Egypt to be a British Protectorate. They made the son of Ismail Pasha, Hussein Kamil, the Sultan of Egypt. Hussein Kamil died in 1917 and was succeeded by his brother Ahmed Fuad (King Fuad I).
keywords: Hussein Kamil, Sultan of Egypt; cartoon; caricature

63e03fb2-ff4b-5263-b342-f74d2b6bdf14.name: La Grande Gare du Hidjaz, Damas (The Grand Railway Station of Hijaz, Damascus)
63e03fb2-ff4b-5263-b342-f74d2b6bdf14.description: The Hijaz Railway Station building is one of several major public buildings established during the late Ottoman period under the rule of Sultan Abdülhamid II in Damascus. The construction was carried out under the supervision of Hüseyin Nazım Pasha, the Wali (Governor) of Damascus and chairman of the committee responsible for implementing the Hijaz Railway project. He oversaw the plan to construct the railway between Damascus and Medina from 1900 to 1908, mobilising conscripts and civilian labour to participate in its construction, while also benefiting from the expertise of German engineers and other foreign specialists who came to supervise the railway project.
63e03fb2-ff4b-5263-b342-f74d2b6bdf14.bibliography:

6466b53e-7366-59fb-b2d6-6c90c4bac6cd.name: Italian translation of the decree by the French Civil Affairs Superintendent (intendant civil) of Algeria, Louis-André Pichon, regulating coral fishing along the coasts of Algeria
6466b53e-7366-59fb-b2d6-6c90c4bac6cd.short_description: This decree imposed a heavy tax on foreign ships that fished corals near Algerian shores, while exempting French ships. The decree was translated into Italian in Livorno, an active coral fishing port town that was badly affected by this ruling. Coral fishing was an important economic activity in the Mediterranean. Algeria was the main fishing area for corals, especially after the depletion of Sardinian coral.
6466b53e-7366-59fb-b2d6-6c90c4bac6cd.author: Cristina Francioli

64c7bc97-7cc3-58be-9d17-18bd4395053c.name: Map of Beirut's water networks
64c7bc97-7cc3-58be-9d17-18bd4395053c.short_description: This map shows the water networks around Lebanon, set up by the Ottoman government.
64c7bc97-7cc3-58be-9d17-18bd4395053c.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem

6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.name: *The French Colonies. Book 26. M. de Brazza's Exploration 1875–79. His treaty with Makoko.*
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.short_description: In September 1880, the explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signed a treaty with Makoko, the Chief of the Bateke (Anziku Kingdom) laying out the new borders of the Congo. The French government ratified this treaty in 1882. Savorgnan de Brazza was henceforth put forward by Jules Ferry's government as the perfect example of non-violent victory, contrasting him with England's Henry Morton Stanley, his rival in this region. Savorgnan de Brazza's image as a "civiliser" became a central theme of colonial propaganda, as we can see from this image.
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.artist: Engraver: L. Geisler; artist; G. Dascher
keywords: Congo; France; colonies; Savorgnan de Brazza

65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.name: The Battle of the Nile fought on 1–2 August 1798 in Aboukir Bay (Egypt), where the British fleet, headed by Admiral Horatio Nelson, defeated the French fleet
65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.short_description: The battle of Nile of 1798 between the French and the British fleets entrenched Britain as the dominant naval power in the Mediterranean.
65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.author: Rossana Spadaccini

65da28a6-c1fa-5d24-a711-42488c8ec2ea.name: *The Recapture of Buda in 1686*
65da28a6-c1fa-5d24-a711-42488c8ec2ea.description:
In 1686, two years after the unsuccessful siege of Buda, a renewed campaign began to enter the Hungarian capital. This time, the Holy League's army was twice as large with over 74,000 men, including German, Hungarian, Croatian, Dutch, English, Spanish, Czech, Italian, French, Burgundian, Danish and Swedish soldiers, along with other Europeans as volunteers, artillerymen, and officers.  
By the middle of June 1686, the siege had begun. A Turkish relief army arrived at Buda in the middle of August, but Abdurrahman Abdi Paşa shrank from the large-scale attack against the siege army, and on 2 September 1686 came upon the resisting *Generalsturm* (General's Tower) at the fortress. The commanders in chief were Charles Duke V of Lorraine (1643–1690) and Maximilan II Emanuel Elector of Bavaria (1679–1726).  Prince Eugene of Savoy and his dragoons were not directly involved in entering the city, but secured the rear of their army against the Turkish relief army, which could not prevent the city from being entered after 145 years in Turkish possession.  
This engraving by Romeyn de Hooghe represents the great explosion of 22 July 1686, the dramatic and decisive event of the attack, showing a partly fictitious topography of the city. The commanders in chief with their army are represented in the foreground Pest-side, while besides them in Pest and in Buda, are their camps and attacking battle corps, with the city of Buda on fire and in ruins, and Gellért Hill on the far left.  
The print was published with German and Dutch inscriptions. The following is from the Dutch inscription seen at the top: “Belegering der sterke stad, Buda of Offen, door de keyserlyke en geallierde machten. 1686.” (The siege of the strong city of Buda – aka Offen – by the allied, imperial forces. 1686.) The print is signed in the middle at the bottom: “R. de Hooge jnv: et fecit. 1686.”
65da28a6-c1fa-5d24-a711-42488c8ec2ea.short_description: This print by Romeyn de Hooghe is the most famous of numerous representations of the recapture of Buda in 1686. It depicts a topographical, partly exact bird’s eye view, with a Baroque battle scene complete with representations of the commanders in chief in the foreground, and the castle and city of Buda on fire, in the background.
65da28a6-c1fa-5d24-a711-42488c8ec2ea.method_for_datation: On the basis of the signature
65da28a6-c1fa-5d24-a711-42488c8ec2ea.obtention: Transferred from the Capital’s collection in 1945.
