65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.name: Ferdinand I, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollen-Sigmaringen
65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.short_description: Street Scene with King Ferdinand of Romania in Vienna. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.

66663408-45e1-58b4-b0d6-376f5a5a1dbb.name: *The French Colonies: New Caledonia: Death of La Pérouse in Vanikoro*
66663408-45e1-58b4-b0d6-376f5a5a1dbb.short_description: History teaching in 19th century French primary schools focussed on heroic acts that marked historic events. The key dates and figures of colonialism were also taught in this way.

66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.name: *The Egyptian Magician holding a seance with members of the European community in Cairo*
66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.short_description: Although this is the roughest of drawings, a composition sketch, or simply on the spot note-taking, it is important because it actually shows an Egyptian Magician, Shaykh Abd al-Qadir al-Maghrabi, in action, possibly in Lewis’s house. A séance was held there on the 8th December 1841, according to Sir Gardner Wilkinson who was present. The Shayk is clearly visible in the centre, and the huddled form in front of him indicates the young lad kneeling and staring at the drop of ink in his palm, answering difficult questions put to him by the onlookers. Although they are in Eastern dress, they are identified on an old label as prominent members of the European community in Cairo, including Henry Abbott, Joseph Bonomi and Colonel Barnett, British Consul-General in Egypt.
66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.author: Victoria and Albert Museum

6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.name: *Comic Map of Seat of War with Entirely New Features* (London: Rock Brothers and Payne, 1854)
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.short_description:
In the annex to the map, the authors made explicit their view on the international situation and the political message that they intended to promote. They portrayed Russia as “the Great Bear of Europe”: a tyrannical power, epitome of despotism and oppression, which used the whip against her own subjects. “The claws of the Bear, improperly extended to the Black Sea, are undergoing the process of being clipped by our brave fellows”.  
Turkey, which was participating in the war on the side of Britain, was represented as a turkey. The authors argued that it was no longer the “sick bird of Europe”. With “head erect and again in good feather”, Turkey looked “its defiance to Russia”. England was described as “the old Lion of the World, majestic, strong and patient”.
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.author: Renata De Simone

67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.name: *The Algiers-Oran line*
67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.short_description: This illustration, from around 1860 in a local Oran publication in the west of Algeria, *L’Algérie Comique et Pittoresque*, comments on current affairs with a distinctively Mediterranean style and sense of humour. Salomon Assus, the father of the famous painter from the Algerian school Armand Assus, was one of the newspaper's first cartoonists.
67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.author: Dalila Orfali

67e5b11f-f92f-508e-b6d5-a9460fac4852.name: Asaf Khan Wearing a Portrait Miniature
67e5b11f-f92f-508e-b6d5-a9460fac4852.short_description: Asaf Khan (d. 1641) was an important individual at the Mughal court. His father was Jahangir’s *wakil* (prime minister); he was the brother of Jahangir’s favourite wife Nur Jahan; his daughter was Mumtaz Mahal, Shah Jahan’s favourite wife and the woman for whom he built the Taj Mahal; and he served as Shah Jahan’s *wakil*. Jahangir was fond of giving his nobles portrait miniatures of himself which they wore, as does Asaf Khan in this drawing, as a mark of his affection but also as a sign of their loyalty to him. The upper portion of the drawing is more highly finished than the rest of it in order to draw attention to the figure’s head, and for this same reason the white of the eye is the only bit of the drawing that has been coloured.

680c8cb0-7e03-52b8-988d-a7e74dbb89fa.name: *L'Égyptienne*, military operetta in three acts and 11 scenes.
680c8cb0-7e03-52b8-988d-a7e74dbb89fa.short_description: Egypt became the subject of choice across the theatrical arts as a symptom of "Egyptomania", a phenomenon which spanned the length of the 19th century. This military operetta, written by de Chivot, Nuitter and Beaumont (with music by Charles Lecocq) is set in Egypt during the arrival of the Napoleonic troops.

6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.name: Italian and Tunisian miners at work
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.short_description: According to the book where this photo was published, in 1906 the largest number of Italian miners in Tunisia worked in El Kef (2,000) and in Gafsa (1,200). The most important mineral resource in Tunisia were phosphates, but the country also had mines of copper, manganese, iron and lead. One could find Italian miners in all these mines.
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.author: Giulia Barrera

6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.name: *View Looking across the Hall of Columns, Karnak*
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.short_description: Roberts' viewpoint across the Great Hypostyle Hall, in the Precinct of Amon-Re, at the Temple Complex at Karnak, captures in great detail the physical features of the monument as it appeared in his day. At the same time, he used exaggerated proportions to convey the structure’s imposing scale, which impressed him deeply. In his diary he writes: ’Karnak is even more astonishing than Luxor. Its magnificence is unimaginable. Trying to describe rationally what I have seen would be ridiculous’. In the 19th century,, the Karnak temple complex became one of the most famous ancient Egyptian sites visted by artists and archaeologists. During his travels up and down the Nile, Roberts captured over 300 monuments and ruins in his unprecedentedly detailed and precise works, many of them before excavation or restoration.  In his work, Roberts also drew on the pioneering scholarship of scholars like Champollion. The final depictions subtlely contributed to the Orientalist discourse on Ancient Egypt, which Europe increasingly saw as their right to appropriate.
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis

686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.name: *Arab horseman*
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.short_description: This piece, drawn in 1846, is a study for the portrait of 'Ali bin Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. The portrait is currently held in the Musée de Versailles. The artist has concentrated on his posture rather than his face, which is sparse on details. The artist came to Constantine in May 1846 and said: "This is the only truly Arab city left in this country". In 1844 he was summoned by the Bey Ahmed, who he met in France, and was commissioned to paint his portrait on horseback surrounded by his beylical guard. The prints cabinet at the Musée National des Beaux-Arts contains the final sketch for this painting, which was exhibited at the Louvre in 2003.
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.author: Dalila Orfali

68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.name: Cartoon
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.short_description: Titled "Une maxime opportuniste", this cartoon by Alfred le Petit condemns the French invasion of Tunisia and points to business and French capital's blame. The poster shows a man bent over under the weight of a sack, full to the brim with silver, whilst a first quadrant on the right shows soldiers going to war, and another on the left shows a man depositing his money. Beneath, the striking line, "(Tunisia's) affairs are the money and blood of others".
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
keywords: French protectorate; resistance; occupation; cartoon; caricature

6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.name: Third-grade pupils of the Italian state-funded Giovanni Meli primary school in Tunis
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.short_description:
In 1831, siblings Pompeo and Ester Sulema, political refugees from Livorno, opened the first Italian school in Tunis. By the end of the 19th century, there were 21 Italian state schools in Tunisia: 13 in Tunis, three in La Goulette, three in Sousse and two in Sfax. Five of them were pre-schools, eleven were primary schools and five were secondary schools.  
The Italian State could run schools in Tunisia thanks to the treaty signed by Italy and Tunisia in 1868. In 1881, Tunisia became a French protectorate and in 1896 Italy and France signed a treaty over the status of Italians in Tunisia: the Italian state could continue to run schools in Tunisia but could not open new ones. So, classes became very crowded, as shown in this photo.
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.author: Giulia Barrera

699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.name: Author Tevfik Fikret and his book of poetry *Rübab-ı Şikeste*
699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.short_description: Tevfik Fikret, who published his first book of poetry *Rubab-ı Şikeste* (broken instrument), dealt with love, piety, nature and a worldview that was self-enclosed to the environment. His poems influenced other Turkish poets and he is considered a pioneer of contemporary Turkish poetry. His work also has some seeds of the social opposition of the future.

69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.name: In the Sicilian Sulphur Mines
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.short_description:
Sicilian sulphur mines at the end of the 19th century employed children as young as seven and eight years old to carry the crude ore up from the mines to the surface.  
In Italy, the first piece of law regarding children’s work dates back to 1886. It forbade employing children under the age of nine in factories and mines. It also dictated that children under the age of 12 could not work at night. Such provisions indicated the extremely hard situation of children workers at the time. Particularly appalling were the working conditions of children in the Sicilian sulphur mines. Their plight was highlighted by the Italian writer Giovanni Verga in his short story *Rosso Malpelo*, and by Nobel laureate Luigi Pirandello in his *Ciàula scopre la Luna*.
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.author: Giulia Barrera

6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.name: Street map of Beirut
6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.short_description: This map of Beirut was drawn in in 1902 under the reign of Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II. The table on the left contains a numbered list of shops and important landmarks, whereas the table on the right lists the name and location of Beirut's railway and maritime companies.
6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
keywords: Commerce; Map; Streets; Shops; Railway; Maritime

6b2642e7-7a75-5343-8798-9e4bf21929a4.name: Luca Petrovich (2nd half of the 19th century – 1900)
6b2642e7-7a75-5343-8798-9e4bf21929a4.short_description: Portrait of Luca Petrovic. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.name: Map of the different types of housing in East Beirut
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.short_description: This map indicates the different types of housing found in the East Beirut with a system of coloured dots.
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.holder: *Maisons traditionnelles de Beyrouth: Typologie, culture domestique, valeur patrimoniale. Le secteur de Rmeil-Médawwar* (Book)
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos

6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.name: Map of Beirut
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.short_description: This map dates to 1876 and was drawn by the acting Danish Consul, Julius Loytved for the Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II. Loytved was a map-maker, an archaeologist, and the director of various Anglo-Syrian schools. This detailed survey map includes 12 districts of Beirut: 1 - The Old City and the *suq*; 2 - Al-Zaytuna; 3 - Ras Beirut; 4 - Msaytbe; 5 - Mazraat al-Arab; 6 - Ras el-Naba'; 7 - Al-Bashura; 8 - Achrafieh; 9 - St. Dimitri; 10 - Mimas; 11 - Rmeil; 12 - Al-Saifi. The roads to Damascus, Saida and Tripoli are all clearly indicated by emphasis on the edge of the map. The map also indicates 47 other points of interest, including 91 consulates, military posts, government buildings, educational and health institutions, public parks, private gardens, cemeteries, archaeological sites, and sand and rock hills.
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.holder: American University of Beirut, Jafet Library, Archives and Special Collections Department
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
keywords: Expansion; Map; Districts; Consulates; Routes; City; Beirut

6b95b4dd-912b-59ba-93e0-00f63bedc323.name: SWP Geological Map
6b95b4dd-912b-59ba-93e0-00f63bedc323.short_description: This was the first ever geological map of Palestine, drawn up in the late 1880’s by Edward Hull. It enabled, for the first time, the accurate assessment of the geological resources of the country, and potentially their exploitation to the benefit of the local economy, as well as revealing the history and structure of the landscape.

6bbbfdcd-9af2-5577-92d7-ef4e14938379.name: *Description de l'Egypte*: frontispiece
6bbbfdcd-9af2-5577-92d7-ef4e14938379.short_description: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, containing all the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

6c0ec863-e0e7-5b08-9c07-4fe22fc9d7ae.name: *Oriental perfumes*
6c0ec863-e0e7-5b08-9c07-4fe22fc9d7ae.description: This advertisement shows that the influence of Orientalism was telegraphed to the public as a synonym for exotic places, buildings and dresses. This advertisement also could be related to the Russian ballets of Sergéi Diágilev.
6c0ec863-e0e7-5b08-9c07-4fe22fc9d7ae.author: Ana Cabrera

6c58855f-349e-59d4-b95b-645e69fbce46.name: Illustrations from *Voyage en Nubie et en Abyssinie entrepris pour découvrir les sources du Nil*
6c58855f-349e-59d4-b95b-645e69fbce46.short_description: People had been trying to find the source of the Nile since antiquity. However, interest in this increased significantly in the early 19th century, and lead to various new scientific observations. These observations were published and illustrated with engravings, which allowed Europeans to better understand the African continent.

6c6f6415-19dd-5136-9ef7-3e7a144c2f66.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
6c6f6415-19dd-5136-9ef7-3e7a144c2f66.short_description: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.

6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.name: Memo on the profits of the Suez Canal Company
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.short_description: An important memo on the profits of the Suez Canal. It shows that the increase in average load during the last 25 years is met with an increase in net profits which are estimated to be less than five Francs per ton, although the navigation fees were much more than that amount during the period stipulated in the document. This is due to the increase in company expenses, and the company’s decision to decrease navigation fees.
keywords: Suez Canal; Profits of the Suez Canal; Future of the Suez Canal

6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.name: *Clock tower, Beirut*
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.short_description: In the Ottoman provinces, clock towers became part of the urban space in the 19th century. These monuments allowed a certain control of time and symbolized "modernity". But they also functioned as imperial monuments. Beirut’s clock tower was for instance built near the Grand Serail to celebrate the anniversary of the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid’s [`Abd al-Hamid II]accession to the throne. So clock towers might be the most telling symbol of the presence of a new political order in the wake of the Tanzimat. Designed by Youssef Aftimus, the tower is 25 m tall, which made it the tallest piece of architecture in Beirut at the time of its completion.
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.author: Stefan Weber

6e13aca8-8a19-574f-8378-12aea190e022.name: File 3142/1903 'Hedjaz Railway'
6e13aca8-8a19-574f-8378-12aea190e022.description:
This volume contains copies of correspondence between British officials regarding the construction of the Hijaz Railway. The correspondence discusses a number of different aspects of the railway including its route, the progress of its construction and donations made towards its construction by members of the Muslim community in India.  
  
A limited amount of the correspondence in the volume is in French, including a copy of a letter sent by Paul Cambon, the French Ambassador in London, to Sir Edward Grey, the Foreign Secretary (folio 15).  
  
The volume contains a number of reports and related information about the railway. Of particular interest are the following:  
  
A report on the Hijaz Railway by Major Francis Richard Maunsell, dated July 1907 (ff 56-69)  
A memorandum respecting German influence on the Hijaz Railway by George Ambrose Lloyd, 1906 (ff 95-96)  
A list of the principal stations on the Hijaz Railway with approximate distances between Damascus and each station (f 100)  
A map of the Hijaz Railway with list of stations (f 106)  
A report by Mr Teofani Loiso, Vice-Consul at Mersina, based on information provided to him by his son who was employed as an engineer on the railway (ff 105-107)  
A report by Herr Otto von Kapp Kohlstein, a German engineer who inspected the Haifa-Damascus branch of the route and worked on the construction of the Damascus-Maan branch (ff 107-109).  
In addition, the volume contains cuttings (and translations) of press articles related to several aspects of the railway and its construction. Also included are two maps. The Turkish (Ottoman) language material consists of the second of these two maps.  
  
The volume includes a divider which gives the year that the subject file was opened, the subject heading, and a list of correspondence references contained in it arranged by year. This divider is placed at the front of the volume.
6e13aca8-8a19-574f-8378-12aea190e022.initial_owner: East India Company, the Board of Control, the India Office, or other British Government Department
6e13aca8-8a19-574f-8378-12aea190e022.provenance: British Library: India Office Records and Private Papers.

6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.name: *Tsar Nikolai II enters Paris, 6 October 1896*
6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.short_description: Tsar Nikolai II's visit to France in October 1896 was front page news. The French government, hoping to highlight the importance of this day, marked the occasion by giving students the day off, stopping all special train services, and meticulously preparing the path the imperial couple would take once arriving at Cherbourg Port. The true purpose of the trip was to preserve the precious Franco-Russian alliance signed in 1893 with Aleksandr III. Pictured in this image are the Tsar and his wife, accompanied by the President of the Republic Félix Faure, and greeted by a crowd of almost half a million on the Champs-Élysées. The popular imagery contributed to the success and immortalisation of the event.
keywords: Diplomacy; France; Russia; Nicholas II; Paris

6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.name: *Chechia maker*
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.short_description: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book *Tunis et ses Environs* shows a Tunisian artisan making a chechia. Before the competition of European industry arose in the 19th century, Tunisian artisans had been the main suppliers of the Middle East.
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar

6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.name: Organ Made in Tunis by the Italian Firm Cesare Trionfo and Exhibited in Milan
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.short_description:
Cesare Trionfo was a child when he migrated with his family to Tunisia from Livorno in 1855. He became a trader, and in 1886 he started trading musical instruments. In Tunis, he later also started a shop that made musical instruments such as this organ. Trionfo promoted the construction of the theatre Politeama Roissini, which he co-owned.  
This organ was exhibited in Milan for the 1906 international exhibition. The organ is a traditional Italian musical instrument. This one has decorative elements taken from Arab architecture.
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.author: Giulia Barrera

6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.name: *10 cents an issue. Le Télégraphe. Morning Newspaper. Special connections with the whole world.*
6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.short_description: Claude Chappe's invention of optical telegraphy was a turning point in the development of telecommunications. Built high up (e.g. on a hill or a roof), the mechanism consisted of a pole with movable arms, visible from a distance, which transmitted a code. Telegraphy became a very popular mode of communication during times of war, and was adopted by the National Convention of the First Republic in 1793. Even Napoléon I, who had shut down the French telegraph lines for fear of political troubles, had them reopened and extended to Europe in order to fight the anti-French Coalition. Telegraphy was an increasingly used mode of communication in the 19th century.

703206c7-1fe3-5807-91ec-e3c954824bfa.name: *Egypt. Plan of the remains of an existing circus, near Alexandria.*
703206c7-1fe3-5807-91ec-e3c954824bfa.short_description: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published between 1809 and 1826.

70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.name: *Turkish café, Smyrna, 9 November 1837*
70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.short_description: Denis-Auguste-Marie Raffet (1804–1860), sketcher and painter, travelled to Southern Russia, Crimea and Turkey with the Prince Demidoff in 1837. He brought back with him a few hundred illustrated pages, which were published in *Voyage en Crimée*. This image, depicting a café in Smyrna (Izmir), the "Little Paris" of the Ottoman Empire, is an excellent example of Orientalist drawing.

70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.name: *Theatre of Djemila, ancient Cuicul*
70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.short_description: In August 1840 and again in 1848 Delamare visited the ruins of Cuicul, an ancient Roman colony founded by Nerva and Trajan at the end of the first century. He brought a number of sketches back from these visits, with the most important of these currently kept at the Cabinet du Livre in the old library at the Sorbonne. This drawing, kept at the Musée des Beaux-Arts, accurately reproduces of the ruins of the theatre, built in the second century beyond the city walls.
70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.author: Hayet Touaibia

70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.name: Arabs listening to a story in their camp
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.short_description: Horace Vernet (1789–1863), the official painter of both Napoléon III and Louis-Philippe, was tasked with painting the "discovery" and conquest of Algeria. Various images of Algeria were published in the illustrated press in order to acquaint the French with Algeria and feed the narrative of a peaceful conquest. This idyllic painting of a group storytelling was very popular in the Salon des Beaux-Arts in 1834, and was reproduced by the engraver Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet in order to ensure its wider diffusion in the national press.
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.artist: Engraver: Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet; artist: Horace Vernet

70c03f94-1563-5fc4-9b32-84ea00fd8d52.name: A Letter from the State Bank of Morocco
70c03f94-1563-5fc4-9b32-84ea00fd8d52.description: Correspondence between the State Bank and Moroccan central government from the archive of Muhammad al-Muqri, the Grand Vizier of Finance under Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-Hafiz al-Hasan I.
keywords: Economy; finance; banking; French in Morocco; credit; protectorate

70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.name: Clothing, sheets and blankets distributed by the Students’ Benevolent Fund to destitute Italian children in Tunis
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.short_description: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies to promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children by providing free books and clothes.
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.author: Giulia Barrera

70df1938-c4b1-5bed-9f24-8054cc85bf48.name: Karl I, Emperor of Austria (1887–1922)
70df1938-c4b1-5bed-9f24-8054cc85bf48.short_description: Portrait of Karl I, the last Austrian Emperor. The Austrian and the Ottoman Empires disintegrated after World War I. Karl I had to flee from Austria and died in exile on the island of Madeira.

712ff58d-128f-55d5-aad2-b4bc62cf22ab.name: *Le Petit Tunisien. Voice for French interests and communities in Tunisia.*
712ff58d-128f-55d5-aad2-b4bc62cf22ab.short_description: Italian migration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. The French government had to bear in mind, however, that there remained significant population who had hoped Tunisia would become an Italian colony. Some French newspapers, such as *Le Petit Tunisien*, responded to this by emphasising their French-Italian links.

718961a1-beb1-58c3-8832-5f8a278c1682.name: The young ladies of the telephones: a view of a Parisian telephone exchange
718961a1-beb1-58c3-8832-5f8a278c1682.short_description: The French telephone network was not automated at the beginning of the 20th century. Young unmarried women were often employed to take paying members' calls, and connect them to their requested number.

71bafc31-de50-5515-8301-3411a7a0be01.name: *A market in Bucharest*
71bafc31-de50-5515-8301-3411a7a0be01.short_description: Wallachia and Moldavia's contacts with the Ottoman Empire also influenced the aspect of Romanian cities. For example, marketplaces, as known from 19th century paintings and lithographs, were similar to Turkish bazaars and represented, just like in the Ottoman Empire, the commercial centre of a city. The watercolor is part of an album with reproductions after 15 of Amedeo Preziosi’s paintings that depict scenes from Bucharest. Maltese painter Amedeo Preziosi met Carol of Hohenzollern, ruler of Romania, in Istanbul in 1866. Invited by the prince to come visit his country, Preziosi was in Romania between June-July 1868 and May-July 1869. He is the author of more than 250 works inspired by Romanian landscapes, cities and people.

71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.name: *The Grand Mosque in Constanţa*
71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.short_description: The Grand Mosque of Constanţa, the biggest in Romania, was built between 1910–1913 for the Muslim community of the city, on the initiative of king Carol I. It was erected on the place of a 19th century mosque, whose minbar (pulpit from where the imam delivers sermons) was preserved. The monument, a mixture of Byzantine-Egyptian and Romanian architectural elements, is the work of architect Victor Ştefănescu, who before designing it travelled to Istanbul to get acquainted with Islamic architecture. The mosque was inaugurated on 31 May 1913 in the presence of Romania’s king and queen and of Romanian and Ottoman officials. The envoy of sultan Abdul Hamid II brought a Persian rug for the mosque and awarded the orders of “Medjidie” and “Osmanieh” to Victor Ştefănescu and the city’s may.

71d76fc5-c9ad-524d-9391-c2dd24da5ac5.name: Chemin de fer, Postcard, Alep (Aleppo Railway Station)
71d76fc5-c9ad-524d-9391-c2dd24da5ac5.description: This composite postcard presents Aleppo’s earlier railway complex, generally identified as Damascus Station, together with a separate building labelled Pavillon militaire. Located in the Jamiliyeh district of Aleppo, the station served the French-operated railway Damas, Hama et Prolongements (D.H.P.), linking Aleppo southward through Hama and Homs with Damascus. The Hama–Aleppo extension entered service in 1906. The upper image shows a restrained two-storey masonry station with a long covered platform, regularly spaced windows and numerous chimneys, reflecting its combined passenger, administrative and possibly staff functions. The lower image records the military pavilion, with a raised entrance, deep tiled roofs and an ornamental timber porch distinguish it from the station building.
71d76fc5-c9ad-524d-9391-c2dd24da5ac5.bibliography:
Kurd Ali, Muhammad, *Khitat al-Sham*, Vol. 5, Damascus: al-Matbaʿah al-Hashimiyyah, 1925–1928.  
  
Digital Historical Documents House, “Aleppo’s Damascus Railway Station in 1902”, *Digital Historical Documents House*, February 4, 2020, Arabic. (The stated 1902 date should be treated cautiously because it conflicts with the documented 1906 opening of the Hama–Aleppo line.)

727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.name: *Interior of a Harem*
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.short_description: Preziosi probably used models to recreate this harem scene which as an infidel Frank he would not normally be allowed to witness. However, there is nothing in this decorous interior which is impossible or unlikely and it may be based on a visit to the house of one of his Turkish friends. The furniture and fittings show western European influence, particularly in the curious rococo wall bracket and the fringed sofa in place of the traditional raised wooden platform covered with carpets. By the middle of the 19th century French style in interior design was fashionable in Turkey, especially a degenerate form of the rococo. A version of this composition, dated 1852, is much less restrained, its details deliberately pandering to the popular western idea of a harem, based on Arabian Nights imagery.
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
keywords: costume; coffee; tobacco; rococo; Ottoman Baroque; Orientalism; women; Ottoman interior decoration; fashion

7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.name: Building a bridge near Haifa
7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.description: This album of 39 images documents the construction of the Hijaz Railway. It photographs two important stretches of the network: the route between Damascus and Maʿan, and the line connecting Daraʿa with Haifa. Its photographs record the remarkable engineering achievements required to negotiate difficult and varied terrain, while also illustrating the railway’s role in strengthening connections across the empire. Alongside tunnels, bridges and stations, the images capture the engineers, officials and labourers whose work made the project possible.
7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.holder: The Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Hajj and The Arts of Pilgrimage
7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.method_for_datation: The Hijaz Railway was constructed between 1900 and 1908.
7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.author: Qaisra Khan
materials: Photographic prints bound in an album

72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.name: *The Crisis in Egypt – Panoramic View of Cairo 1882*
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.short_description: This expansive, panoramic engraving focuses of the Citadel of Cairo with the majestic Ottoman-style mosque erected by Muhammad Ali Pasha in memory of his son Tusun at the centre. The view is taken from high up in the Moqattam range, allowing the viewer to appreciate a panorama that takes in the wide expanse of the city of Cairo beyond the fortress, all the way to the river Nile. In composing the image, dated to 1882 CE - the year of the Anglo-Egyptian war, the artist H. W. Brewer most probably drew on contemporary photographs. Little is known about this British illustrator who specialised in depictions of cities viewed from the air.The print was issued as a supplement to The Graphic 1882. The Graphic was a British weekly illustrated newspaper, first published on 4.12.1869 by William Luson Thomas’s company Illustrated Newspapers Limited. By 1882, it had over 1000 employees. The Graphic’s influence on the art word was considerable, its readers including Vincent van Gogh.
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis

72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.name: 'The War on Trial'
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.short_description:
This booklet describes an imaginary trial against Giovanni Giolitti, the Italian Prime Minister who directed the colonial conquest of Libya in 1911-12. The judge asks Giolitti:  
– ‘Why did you get into other people’s home?’  
– ‘In order to defend our interests.’  
– ‘Good! And what about the slaughtering of women and children, the massacre of elderly people, and the hanging of men?’  
– ‘You see, your excellence, we needed to uplift Italian prestige.’  
– ‘And what about the thefts, the burnings and the planes that bombed huts?’  
– ‘It was our civilising mission.’ "
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.author: Giulia Barrera

7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.name: *Ali Bey (Domingo Badia y Leblich), Traveller*
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.description: Ali Bey, a pseudonym used by Domingo Badia (1767–1818), was a Spanish explorer and spy. He travelled to the Ottoman Empire and North Africa under the identity of a Syrian prince. He published his experiences in different books. His travel descriptions had success in Europe and were translated into several languages. The descriptions reveal his admiration and respect for the Arab world.
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales
materials: Paper; ink; stipple engraving; pencil-manner engraving

736d9205-4e1c-5817-bc04-427dac8d02d2.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
736d9205-4e1c-5817-bc04-427dac8d02d2.short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

737d2ad8-e855-5e34-9a89-714f0aed6dff.name: The Stele of Mesha, Hebrew inscription from 896 BC. 1/16 of original size.
737d2ad8-e855-5e34-9a89-714f0aed6dff.short_description: Following the work of Champollion, decoding texts and archaeological discoveries became some of the main interests of popular science journals. Graphic items also begin to feature in the late 19th century, adding to the pedagogical side of these articles.

742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.name: *Monument commemorating the installation of the Hijaz-Damascus telegraph connection, Beirut*
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.short_description: This monument is a well-known benchmark, which remained the symbol of the municipal administration until a few years ago. The bronze column in the middle of the Merje Square was erected in commemoration of the Istanbul-Damascus-Mecca telegraph link. It was the line with the sultan’s Islamist policy, acting as a symbol of the Ottoman claim to leadership over Muslims. The monumental telegraph column is crowned by a model of the Istanbul Hamidiye Mosque, where every week the Sultan ‘Abdülhamid [`Abd al-Hamid II] had his visit to the mosque for Friday prayers celebrated with an imperial march-past- a demonstration of the concentrated political power of the Sultan.
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.author: Stefan Weber

74e93f42-b022-5056-9d51-bed2d2eb0ca5.name: *Map of Algeria's commercial routes to the "Pays des Noirs"* \[Guinea\]
74e93f42-b022-5056-9d51-bed2d2eb0ca5.short_description: Having conquered Algeria, France launched several expeditions in order to open up new trade routes from North Africa to Guinea. Europeans had great difficulty in using the internal trade routes, which were controlled by indigenous African kingdoms, so were instead limited to coastal routes.

7503191f-13bf-5090-a965-b30a2948d2bd.name: Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848)
7503191f-13bf-5090-a965-b30a2948d2bd.short_description: Portrait of Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848). As the best General under his father Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, he fought successfully against the Wahhabites, the Ottoman Army and the Greeks. In 1831 he conquered Syria and governed it until 1841. In 1848 he deposed his senile father and was declared Vice King of Egypt by Sultan Abdülmecid I.

750a06a9-2d0d-5ed4-96b6-1e5b28d3634e.name: Plan of the park Bibescu
750a06a9-2d0d-5ed4-96b6-1e5b28d3634e.short_description: In 1898, Nicolae Romanescu, the mayor of Craiova (a city in Wallachia), hired French landscape architect Edouard Redont to lay out two parks in Craiova. One of them, called park Bibescu, was completed in 1903. It was built on a terrain bought by the city hall of Craiova in 1853 from Iancu Bibescu, brother of Wallachian prince Gheorghe Bibescu. The park occupied a surface of 100 ha, among which 4 were represented by water. Some of the attractions of the park included: a luxuriant vegetation, two lakes, a waterfall river, several springs, a replica of a medieval castle, a suspended bridge, a zoo. There also existed restaurants and cafes, a library, an exhibition hall, a ceremony hall, a hippodrome, a velodrome and a pier. In 1900 the plan of park Bibescu was awarded a gold medal at the universal exposition of Paris.

75891604-fdb8-540e-af25-a6509a9103f7.name: *Cairo: houses and gardens in the French quarter.* Flaubert in the foreground.
75891604-fdb8-540e-af25-a6509a9103f7.short_description: The writer Gustave Flaubert lived in Egypt for three years from 1849 to 1851 with his friend Maxime Du Camp. He saw and experienced many new things during this time, travelling to Egypt, Beirut, Jerusalem and Damascus. Although Gustave Flaubert did not like being photographed, Maxime du Camp was able to take this snap of him in Cairo.

76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.name: Photograph of the Old Railway Station in Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.short_description: The first railroad in Macedonia was the track running from Thessalonica via Skopje to Belgrade. Its construction was financed with foreign investments and began in 1871. The track to Skopje was finished in 1873. The Skopje-Mitrovica railway line was completed in 1878. In 1888, it was connected to Serbian railways at the border crossing Zibevche near Vranje.
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.holder: Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.author: Zoja Bogdanovska, historian, Museum of the City of Skopje

author.lastname: Bogdanovska, historian, Museum of the City of Skopje

keywords: Railroad; railway; railway station; Ottoman Balkans

76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.name: Advertisement from the International Exhibition in Rome 1911
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.short_description: During the International Exhibition of Fine Arts in 1911, in a green area near the Tiber river within Rome’s boundaries, exhibitions of regions and ethnography were staged. This show was meant to celebrate ethnography as a new science and, at the same time, to highlight the habits and customs of the different regions of Italy, especially on the occasion of the 50th anniversary celebrations of the unification of the Italian state. A consequence of the exhibition was an enlargement of the city of Rom and massive urban growth. At the same time, upon the Rassegna Illustrata dell’Esposizione commercial pavilions were destined to later become restaurants, shops and pubs. All of them were clearly inspired by the popularity of orientalism.
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.holder: Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions

7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.name: *Partium Regni Sclavoniae et Croatiae*
7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.alternate_name: Geographical-historical map of the northwest region of Croatia in 1673
7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.description:
A map depicting the northwest region of Croatia with inscriptions and dates that detail the most important battles against the Ottoman Turks in the 15th, 16th and 17th centuries.  
There is a letterpress dedication to Martin Borković, Bishop of Zagreb from 1647 until 1667, and to Count Nikola Erdödy. A signature on the bottom right in a cartouche reads “*per R.P. STEPHANVM GLAVACH” and* “*NOVA hactenus ... SCLAVONIAE et CROATIAE ... Confiniumque Descriptio ... Professorem 1673”.*  
The map is an announcement of the Croatian Counter-Reformation and the beginning of the Baroque style. Made by the Jesuit, Stjepan Glavač the first teacher of logic at Zagreb Jesuit Academy and professor of philosophy, exegesis and controversy at Graz University, its production was the incentive of the Bishop of Zagreb Martin Borković, and the Croatian *ban* (viceroy) Nikola Erdödy.  
The map shows the “remnants of the remnants” of the former Kingdom of Croatia after Ottoman expansion ended. Drawings, made by Glavač while he travelled throughout Croatia accompanied by soldiers and Krajina officers as consultants, decorate the map. The map presents a rare example of decoration in the spirit of the Society of Jesus, shown particularly in the drawings of Mars in armour and the female figures of *Fidelitate constanti* and *Catholica Fide*.
7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.short_description: A geographical-historical map of northwest Croatia in 1673, it was drawn by the Jesuit Stjepan Glavač, a teacher at the Zagreb Jesuit Academy and at Graz University. Glavač spent several years travelling through dangerous and inaccessible regions of Croatia accompanied by soldiers and Krajina officers who acted as consultants. The map, showing the “remnants of the remnants” of the former Kingdom of Croatia, and decorated solely with Glavač's drawings, is a rare example of decoration in the spirit of the Society of Jesus.
7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.holder: Metropolitan Library, Valvasor Collection of prints and drawings
7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.provenance: From the Johann Weichard Valvasor Collection
7756c7b9-3b65-5af3-92f0-bce2be93d3c9.obtention: Purchased in 1690 from Johann Weichard Valvasor by the Archdiocese of Zagreb Baron J. W. Valvasor, a Slovenian polymath and collector, had a museum in his mansion in Bogenšperg. Towards the end of his life, due to financial difficulties, he sold some of his exceptionally valuable holdings. In 1690, the Bishop of Zagreb, Aleksandar Mikulić, purchased Valvasor’s collection of prints and his library.

Pelc, M., *Iconotheca Valvasoriana, VII. svezak*, Janez Vajkard Valvasor Foundation, Zagreb Archdiocese, Ljubljana, 2004.

7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.name: The Promotional Exhibition of the Alsace and Lorraine Society in the Algerian Section [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.short_description: Paris, International Exhibition, 1878. In one of the streets in the Trocadero Pavilion buildings were constructed based on those built in Algeria after the French-Prussian war (1870–71) by the Society Protecting Alsatian and Lorenese People for refugees coming from France. The interior shows all the territories donated to the Protecting Society and in the lower part the villages of Hanssonvillers and Bacckhalfa.

779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.name: *Interior of a school, Cairo*
779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.short_description: In this scene depicted by Lewis, the Hoja or teacher is listening to his assistant rhythmically reciting the Quran (while beating time), as some children pay attention and others not. Some commentators have regarded the presence of a young girl as inauthentic, but young girls were able to attend Quran schools, according to the artist Charles de Tournemine, the scholar Edward Lane and the translator Richard Burton. Certainly not all women were illiterate, and some female descendants of the prophet were noted for their ability to read and recite the scriptures.
779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
keywords: education; school; teaching; children; childhood; kuttab

77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.name: Algerian Pavilion in the Trocadéro Park [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.short_description: At the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, the Algerian Pavilion was designed by the architect M. Wable, who was appointed by General Chanzy. The building represents one of the greatest proofs of French colonisation policy. The front-door, four metres wide, is a copy from the ‘Ubbad Mosque of Sidi Bumadyan in Tlemcen, and is richly decorated with enamelled majolica and arabesque decorations. The decorations of the minaret echo the tower in ruins from the mosque of Mansoura, 1,200 square metres wide. The pavilion was meant to show the productive potential of the colony to the French capitalists.

78482946-b8d7-5fca-913f-fd0e2dc38b4a.description: A 19th-century map of the Moroccan Empire and the states of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli. Its toponyms are written in French. As the original was monochrome, evidently the *Atlas*’s original owner manually embellished the borders between countries and administrative boundaries.

794483b6-f573-5ea4-9de3-b7a65c779566.name: Coronation of His Majesty King Charles X, in Rheims,  29 May 1825
794483b6-f573-5ea4-9de3-b7a65c779566.short_description: Charles X was Louis XVI's younger brother. During the revolution, Charles (then the Count of Artois) emigrated in search of support from other European royal courts. He disapproved of Louis XVIII's pragmatism, and following his death advocated a return to the Ancien Régime. He had himself crowned in Reims, like his ancestors, although the cost of this grandiose ceremony was the subject of great controversy.

79791fd6-4a63-5950-8b88-e5b802feebd3.name: Research on the location of Carthage (with 15 illustrated pages)
79791fd6-4a63-5950-8b88-e5b802feebd3.short_description: Christian Théodore Falbe, captain of a Danish ship and explorer, was the Tunisian consul before becoming  delegate for the Société pour l'Exploration de Carthage. Fable dedicated himself to developing a new map of Tunis, which required the use of newly developed techniques. He had to use his cunning to be able to draw these plans, as he had aroused the suspicion of the Tunisian population, and ended up doing many of them from the roofs of neighbouring consulates. His pioneering work on Carthage should be seen as part of a greater international movement which had recently taken great interest in this destroyed and long-forgotten city.

7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.name: *Map to illustrate the Route of David Roberts Esq. R. A. in the Holy Land, Petrea and Syria*
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.short_description: This map shows the areas visited by the Scottish artist David Roberts (1796-1864) during the 11 months he spent travelling between Egypt, the Sinai, Jordan and Palestine in 1838/39. Roberts subsequently became famous for his meticulous lithographs of Egypt, the 'Holy Land' and other Near Eastern regions, hardly touched as yet by British artists at the time. Maps like this one were provided with each complete set of his lithographs later to help trace the locations Roberts visited and sketched.Roberts' depictions were to become extremely important tools in popularising the ‘Holy Land’ in 19th century British imagination, thus encouraging ever more people to visit, map and survey it. His work also helped to underpin the aspirations and objectives of the Palestinian Exploration Fund, founded in 1865.

7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.short_description: This map of Lombardy-Venetia from 1827 shows postal routes and information concerning the costs of travelling with the post coaches.

7a9b5caa-c0ca-5b9c-a54b-4f65a9d0be8e.name: *Palais de l'Industrie. July to November 1890. International Exhibition of the Industrial Arts and Sciences*
7a9b5caa-c0ca-5b9c-a54b-4f65a9d0be8e.short_description: The Palais de l'Industrie et des Beaux-Arts was built in Paris in 1855 with the purpose of hosting the first French Exposition Universelle (world fair). Its great glass and metal structure, the "galerie des machines", was a symbol of industrial progress. This building, unlike others of its kind, was used for the same purpose right up until 1896, when it was destroyed to make space for the Grand Palais and the Petit Palais for the Exposition Universelle of 1900. For 40 years it hosted a variety of exhibits, all aimed at promoting recent technological innovations.

7ab5bd97-3948-5e4a-9db2-309afc5b078e.name: A lithographed postcard showing Sharif Makka al-kabir Aun ar-Rafiq (ʿAwn al-Rafiq, Grand Sharif of Mecca)
7ab5bd97-3948-5e4a-9db2-309afc5b078e.description: The figure is Sharif ʿAwn al-Rafiq Pasha, who served as Sharif and Emir of Mecca from 1882 until his death in 1905. Institutional catalogues of his surviving portrait consistently identify him by this name and term of office. The title, “Sharif of Mecca”, referred to the Hasanid descendants of the Prophet Muhammad who governed Mecca. Sharifian government in the city developed from the tenth century and remained one of the most important institutions of western Hijaz politics for centuries. As a member of the Hashemite ʿAwn household, he governed the holy city, exercised authority connected with the Hajj, and negotiated his position with the Ottoman administration, whose recognition remained essential to the sharifate. The Arabic heading was intended to identify him as "Sharif Makka al-kabir Aun ar-Rafiq"(ʿAwn al-Rafiq, Grand Sharif of Mecca), but the name is irregularly and inaccurately written on the card as "Sharif al-Makka al-kabir Aun ar-Rabay".

7b582bf3-4e6a-5626-8f57-513177ccb1d0.name: *St. Andrew*
7b582bf3-4e6a-5626-8f57-513177ccb1d0.description:
Figure type and a diagonal X-shaped cross identify the subject of the work as St. Andrew, a fisherman from Galilee and Christ's first disciple. The elongated figure, with an S-shaped body and one foot forward, is sketched in light outline. The artist's attention is dedicated to the modelling of body volumes and the rendering of a system of draperies in an elaborate network of parallel and crossing lines of varying density and intensity.  
Josef Winterhalder Sr. came from a family of sculptors in Schwarzwald. After studying at the Vienna Academy he settled in Moravia, in Olomouc and Znojmo. At the beginning of the 1740s, shortly after a trip to Dresden, where he studied sculptures by Balthasar Permoser, he obtained a large commission in Náměšt nad Oslavou. Between 1740 and1744 he created a series of 20 larger-than-life statues of saints and angels in shell limestone for the Náměšt Bridge, one of three of the kind surviving in the Czech Republic. Winterhalder invited the sculptor Alexander Jelínek, member of a renowned family of sculptors from Velké Meziříčí, to collaborate with him. Winterhalder produced several drawings associated with the commission, three of which are preserved in the graphic art collection at the Moravian Gallery. The drawings represent St. Joachim, St. Andrew and St. Michael. Brilliant specimens of Baroque drawings for sculpture they demonstrate the essential part the artist Paul Troger played in shaping Winterhalder's drawing style. Similar drawings have also survived for the decoration of the Dominican Church in Brno.  
The drawings of Josef Winterhalder Sr. significantly contributed to the further dissemination of Paul Troger's influence among artists active in Moravia. Winterhalder employed his drawings, for example, in the training of his nephew, the future painter Josef Winterhalder Jr. Winterhalder's drawings were also used by other artists, such as Johann Lucas Kracker.
7b582bf3-4e6a-5626-8f57-513177ccb1d0.short_description: The drawing refers to the decoration of the bridge in Náměšť nad Oslavou, one of the few of its kind to survive. Josef Winterhalder came from a family of sculptors in Schwarzwald. After studies at the Vienna Academy he settled in Moravia, first in Olomouc and later in Znojmo.
7b582bf3-4e6a-5626-8f57-513177ccb1d0.method_for_datation: The drawing probably comes directly from the estate of Josef Winterhalder Sr. Its style corresponds with the sculptor’s manner of work.
7b582bf3-4e6a-5626-8f57-513177ccb1d0.obtention: The drawing, acquired as early as 1863, is part of a series possibly passed directly from the estates of Josef Winterhalder Sr. and his nephew, painter Josef Winterhalder Jr. In all probability, the series later came into the property of the sculptor Andreas Schweigl and later the archivist Jan Petr Cerroni, Moritz Wilhelm Trapp and Emil Kořistka, all of whom were curators at the Brno museum.

7b607aac-e5db-517f-aaf5-04ce4eb5e62c.short_description: This project for a park with fountain, covered, possibly, with tiles decorated in Neo-Mudéjar style. The Neo-Mudéjar style was selected by the architects for important buildings such as theatres or bull rings or urban spaces as the International exhibition of Barcelona 1888. One of the characteristics of this style is use of brick and tile decoration in the buildings’ interiors and façades.

7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.name: *The Laboratories of the Istituto delle Scienze of Bologna*
7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.alternate_name: *The Visit of Frederick Christian of Poland to the Istituto delle Scienze of Bologna*
7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.description: The *Insignia degli Anziani Consoli*, housed in the Archivio di Stato, of Bologna, are documents on parchment commissioned every two months, from 1530 to 1796. These bound 16 volumes celebrate the eight Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere di Giustizia, a group of ruling magistrates. From the end of the sixteenth-century the names of the magistrates were written flanked by their coats of arms and a depiction of a significant event that took place during the bimester of their charge. These manuscripts provide an extraordinary visual chronicle illustrating more than two centuries of the city's history with six pictures a year. This picture, refers to the last bimester of 1739, shows the inside of the Istituto delle Scienze of Bologna during the visit of prince Frederick Christian of Poland. The prince is sitting examining a fortress plan. In the background are visible from the left: the anatomy room, the school of the nude, and the Institute library. On the top is the coat of arms of the eight Anziani Consoli and in the middle, that of the Gonfaloniere di Giustizia.
7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.short_description: This illumination shows the Istituto delle Scienze of Bologna during the visit of Prince Frederick Christian of Poland. In the middle of the scene, the prince is examining a fortress plan; in the background it is possible to see the rooms of the Istituto.
7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.initial_owner: Anziani Consoli of the town of Bologna
7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.method_for_datation: The date of the illumination (1739, last bimester), the subject depicted and the patronage (the Anziani Consoli of Bologna) are inscribed in the caption, below the picture.
7b6c2e8c-8a34-50a4-8b04-8c9aeafdbdd9.obtention: This illumination, like the whole series, has always been housed in the archive of the Bolognese senate, inside the municipal palace. It was transferred to the Archivio di Stato in 1874, when it was created.

7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.name: *Rysul Khyma from the SW and the situation of the Troops at ½ past 2 pm, November 13th, 1809*
7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.short_description: In this image, the artist - a soldier with the British forces attacking and devastating Qawasim strongholds in 1809/10, records the wholescale devastation of Ras al Khaimah on the afternoon of November 13th, 1809. Looking at the town from the southwest, he records in graphic detail the inferno British troups visited on both the town and the Qawasim's majestic dhows. Both are seen being consumed by a firewall of flames, the smoke billowing densely above. A large contingent of inactive British troops is seen standing along the perimeters of the town, unconcerned by the devastation behind them. In the foreground on the left, a group of workers is instructed by British officers to remove  things from a burning builiding, which - interestingly - is marked with a large cross on its side wall. Eye witnesses to this event record that the town was cannonaded since the day before, while troops stormed strategic positions. By 4 pm on the 13th, all the Qawasim's vessels were burning, together with their naval stores and houses, most of which were looted by the British forces.

Unfortunately Champollion died in 1831 (he was only 41 years old) and Rosellini had to carry on the huge project on his own, publishing the texts and also the atlas plates in folio. The original materials for the publication are preserved today at the University Library of Pisa.

7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.name: *The Battle of Abukir 1799*
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.short_description: During the French occupation of Egypt, in fact three battles centered on the area around Abukir (Abu Qir), a town on the Mediterranean northeast of Alexandria. The first, in 1798, was a naval battle in which the French were defeated devastatingly by the British navy under the command of Rear Admiral Horatio Nelson. The second battle – shown here – marked a decisive confrontation between Ottoman troops under the command of Sayyid Mustapha Pasha, shipped to Egypt by the British navy, and the occupying French forces led by Napoleon Bonaparte. On the 14th of July 1799, the Ottomans stormed Abukir’s harbor and briefly took control of the city, only to be rebuffed and decisively defeated by the French eleven days later. The scene here appears to mark the moment of surrender. Napoleon Bonaparte, seated on a white horse and surrounded by his officers  is supplicated by Ottoman figures, while fighting still goes on and the smoke of battle continues to billow all around. At sea lie the ships of the British navy – unable to intervene.  The last battle fought near Abukir in 1801 between the French and British helped to prepare the ground for France’s final expulsion from Egypt.

He is widely considered as one of the most important artists in Saudi Arabia and is notable for his particular interest in the development of Mecca.

7ef4da57-b989-5c8a-b7bd-e74673870ad0.name: Aqueducts around Jericho No.7
7ef4da57-b989-5c8a-b7bd-e74673870ad0.description: An original plan from the survey of Western Palestine showing the aqueducts bringing water from the wadies Fara, Kelt and Nuwayimeh into the Jericho oasis. These aqueducts date from the Hellenistic era onwards, and were used and added to for centuries well into the Islamic era. Note in particular how they feed into the Umayyad period Khirbet al Mafjar, a huge agricultural estate and palace, and the Mamluk period sugar mill, Tawaheen es Sukkar.

7f3328c0-a8f7-54b7-800a-d0938adac602.name: Pop-up view of the Masjid al-Haram
7f3328c0-a8f7-54b7-800a-d0938adac602.short_description: This pop-up view of Mecca was illustrated by Vojtěch Kubašta and published by Artia in Prague. Vojtěch Kubašta was born in Vienna in 1914 and spent much of his life working as an illustrator, creating children’s books and cards. Having studied architecture but unable to practice during the war, his knowledge of structure is evident particularly in this pop-up view of Mecca. The view made in 1955 illustrates the haram with pilgrims and the Kaˋba at its centre, surrounded by buildings which were removed after the 1960s, for example, the Bani Shayba gate and the building which dispensed Zamzam water. The depiction is very accurate, which suggests that it was likely to have been copied from a photograph. The gateways into the mosque are all labelled and small details such as the roof of the Kaˋba have not been left out. The cover illustrates a man with his hand on the Black Stone and six views on the back include photographs of the main sites of Hajj (e.g. Mina, the Jamarat and Muzdalifa). Artia also published a series of Kubašta’s works in Farsi for the Iranian market.

80bf7d8a-befa-587f-8452-207110b874a9.name: Map of the Sykes–Picot Agreement and Historical Note
80bf7d8a-befa-587f-8452-207110b874a9.description: The lines drawn on the map and the lines drawn in the portrait bear the marks of the same authority: both the border and the identity are shaped by the tip of the pen. During the First World War, Britain and France secretly agreed, with Russia’s approval, to divide the Ottoman Middle East. With a few strokes of the pen, new frontiers were drawn across the lands once linked by the Hijaz Railway. These lines silenced local voices, fragmented communities and reshaped territories. Decisions made behind closed doors by imperial powers set the political, social and cultural course of the region for generations to come.

81c828fc-8155-513b-b95f-cf8966747f0a.name: *The Romanian pavilion at the world exhibition of 1867*
81c828fc-8155-513b-b95f-cf8966747f0a.short_description: In 1865, the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia were invited by France to participate in the universal exhibition of 1867, that was to take place in Paris. The Romanian government appointed Alexandru Odobescu to negotiate with the Imperial Commission for the Organization of the Exposition the location of the Romanian pavilion. Although the Principalities were under Ottoman sovereignty, the Commission agreed to offer the Principalities their own pavilion next to that of the Ottoman Empire. Odobescu hired French architect Ambroise Baudry, who had been to Romania in 1864 for an archeological mission, to build the Romanian pavilion, which was a combination of architectural elements characteristic of famous Romanian monuments (e.g.: the Stavropoleos Church in Bucharest, the Curtea de Argeș monastery).

823a405a-b8cf-5eeb-af76-1bb8e28081d7.name: First issue of *Al-Ahram*
823a405a-b8cf-5eeb-af76-1bb8e28081d7.short_description:
*Al-Ahram* was founded in Alexandria in 1875 by two Lebanese brothers, Bishara Takla and Salim Takla. It began as a weekly newspaper published every Saturday. Its first issue appeared on 5 August 1876. The paper was relaunched as a daily newspaper in January 1881.  
Its headquarters was in Alexandria until November 1899 when it was moved to Cairo. The newspaper was distributed in Egypt and the Levant. The religious innovators Muhammad Abduh and Jamal al-Din al-Afghani were early writers of the newspaper. Upon the death of Bishara Takla, Dawud Barakat, a Lebanese journalist, was named editor of the daily in 1901.

825ea881-372b-5499-bcbe-096246ecd917.name: Import/export activities between Egypt and Venice in 1868 and the first six months of 1869
825ea881-372b-5499-bcbe-096246ecd917.short_description: The items imported from Egypt were cotton, natron (a hydrous native sodium carbonate, used in chemical industry; Egypt had a rich deposit of it in Wadi el-Natrun), coffee, hides, fruit, copper and tamarind roots. The items exported to Egypt included wood and pieces of furniture, fruits and vegetables, butter, bricks and tiles, glass beads, lime, wine, cloth, medicaments, books, and various other products.
825ea881-372b-5499-bcbe-096246ecd917.author: Andrea Pelizza

82a512d3-aced-55a2-b8b4-370dfafb5ffc.name: *Théâtre de l'Opéra. "Aida". The banks of the Nile (act 3). Set by Jean-Louis Chéret*
82a512d3-aced-55a2-b8b4-370dfafb5ffc.short_description: Commissioned by Isma'il Pasha for the inauguration of the Suez Canal, Verdi's opera *Aida* was performed for the first time in Cairo in 1871, with great success. It recreated life at the time of the pharaohs, with the details and the plot developed by the archaeologist Mariette. *Aida* was performed in Paris from 1876, with a grand and successful performance at the Opéra Garnier in 1880.
82a512d3-aced-55a2-b8b4-370dfafb5ffc.artist: Engraver: Auguste Lepère; artists: Henry Scott, Jean-Louis Chéret

82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.name: The horses presented by the Sultan of Morocco to the King of Italy on the occasion of the official visit to Italy by a Moroccan delegation
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.short_description:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an Ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station, he was received by the Mayor or Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamond box, and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

82f533fb-66d6-5753-8d34-97a1b983f107.short_description: Lecture by George Scharf at what was to become Queen’s College, London. He made large drawings of important objects for the purpose.

83ca2754-e506-5404-be99-4dd9fa3be1e5.name: Information for Passengers: Beirut, Tripoli, Alexandretta
83ca2754-e506-5404-be99-4dd9fa3be1e5.description: This advertisement for the Nairn Transport Company, founded in the 1920s, promotes its six-wheeled Pullman buses crossing the desert between Damascus and Baghdad. With timetables linking Haifa, Beirut and Iraq, the service carried both mail and passengers. More than transport, it symbolised modern mobility under the Mandate system, replacing older caravan and railway routes while reflecting new borders and colonial influence in the Middle East.

8452667b-dc79-566c-8b23-9d0b6af62bc0.name: An illustrated album of architecture, including views of Mecca and Medina
8452667b-dc79-566c-8b23-9d0b6af62bc0.short_description:
This large-format volume, entiled *Entwurf einer historischen Architectur in Abbildung unterschiedener beruehmten Gebaeude des Alterthums* (Project for a History of Architecture through pictures of various important buildings from antiquity and foreign people), by Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656–1723) was published in 1725, a few years after his death. Fischer was an Austrian architect and in 1705 he was appointed imperial court architect for Joseph I.  
The book is considered one of the first to attempt an architectural history of the world. It includes nine Islamic buildings amongst its listing of thirteen ‘*foreign*’ buildings. The line drawings of the Iranian and Ottoman buildings are known to have been sourced from illustrated travellers’ accounts, but the addition of the View of Medina and the View of Mecca are remarkable for their originality. Underneath each picture is engraved explanatory text in German and French and they may be the first representations of Mecca and Medina in a European work.  
The plan of Mecca contains some of the known buildings in the *haram*, which are identified by a key, but there is still much confusion about what they are, and although the general plan must have been taken from Ottoman images available at the time, there is much which is incorrect perhaps in an attempt to exoticise the drawings. The view of Medina on the other hand is almost entirely inaccurate and may have been compiled from oral accounts.

84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.name: Traditional dress for a *shaykh* or *shaykha*
84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.short_description: Featured here is the traditional dress for the *shaykh* and *shaykha* of the Keserwan district. The *kubran* is an embroidered jacket (with or without sleeves) made of silk or velvet. The *gumbaz* is a long dress or coat embroidered with gold or silver and sometimes adorned with semi-precious jewels. It consisted of three panels and was split on either side of the body, beginning from the hip area. Other components of this traditional attire were a *mentiene* (blouse), the *shirwal* baggy trousers, a velvet or satin cape with gold or silver embroidery, and a long belt called a *shamle* or *zunnar* made of silk or cashmere depending on the season, and which was wrapped around the waist or hips.
84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
materials: The original were made of silk, velvet, gemstones, cashmere, satin, gold, silver

84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.name: *Entrance to Damascus*
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.short_description: This coloured engraving by W. H. McFarlane shows the entrance to Damascus by the new French-built road through the Merj, or meadow, west of the city. Most probably this is the carriage road that had been established between Beirut and Damascus in 1863, at a time when most other connecting arterties were mere mule paths. French firms also built railways and ports in Syria during the later 19th century. The Ottoman style building in the background on the right is the Tekkiye Mosque Complex, built on the banks of the Barada river at the orders of Suleiman the Magnificent between 1554-1560 and incorporating a mosque, accomodation, a soup kitchen and a hospice.

863f2655-60dd-5322-acff-d958595ed2e2.name: *Società d'Esplorazione Commerciale in Africa*
863f2655-60dd-5322-acff-d958595ed2e2.short_description: This map shows Italian commercial expeditions in Africa, particularly in Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, between the years 1881 and 1882. 868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.name: *Panoramic view of the Isthmus of the Suez, tracing the canal between the two seas*
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.short_description: Between 1859 and 1869, the Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez built a canal joining the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, thus opening up a strategic trade route towards the Indian subcontinent. This panoramic image was drawn by Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer fascinated with Egypt who played a key role, alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps, in the planning and construction of the Suez Canal.
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds
keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps

868e1d9c-d782-5ab4-a356-d8e849b96e6c.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
868e1d9c-d782-5ab4-a356-d8e849b96e6c.short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

86f5889a-6b8e-56da-8202-c0ca7f73045b.name: Algerian Corkmaker [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
86f5889a-6b8e-56da-8202-c0ca7f73045b.short_description: At the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion, as part of the reconstruction of a hypothetical typical neighbourhood. The making of cork-taps was moved from Europe to Algeria to take advantage from the numerous Algerian forests. Taps were both made by hand and by machines and were brought to Europe from Trocadero.

870e10a2-491d-5ec7-881d-703d19098570.short_description: Print after Edwin Long’s famous painting. Well informed by archaeological discoveries, but based on a story in Herodotus of Mesopotamian life, laced with Orientalist fantasies.

87e70362-8746-56dc-8457-3ebaaa0bc58a.name: Ottoman map of the Romanian countries
87e70362-8746-56dc-8457-3ebaaa0bc58a.short_description: This is a map of Moldavia and Wallachia dating from after 1812, when following the Russian-Ottoman war of 1806-1812 Russia annexed the Eastern part of Moldavia, thereafter called Bessarabia (which used to be the name by which southern Moldavia was known). The red line marks the new border that the peace treaty of Bucharest (1812) established between the Ottoman Empire and Russia. The light blue line marks the border between Moldavia and Wallachia, the yellow one that between Austria and the Ottoman Empire and the thick blue line represents the border between Bulgaria and Wallachia. The green line marks the frontiers of the Ottoman Empire.

88e039ef-da59-59a2-bb4a-56259bea2878.name: *French conquest of Tunisia - the battle of Jebel Hadada. 26 avril 1881*
88e039ef-da59-59a2-bb4a-56259bea2878.short_description: Published in a colonial newspaper, this image was intended to highlight the strength of the French army in the face of the Tunisian resistance, which seems unable to hold them back. 88f4e317-6501-5591-b5b3-41a03b3515d2.name: *Strike fund*
88f4e317-6501-5591-b5b3-41a03b3515d2.short_description: "Strike funds" were established during strikes, collecting money which they received from donations and subscription fees. These funds are able to financially support strikers, who no longer received their salaries and therefore had no means of survival. This drawing emphasises the anxiety on the faces of the workers and their families, who relied wholly on this solidarity for their food and lodgings. It also mocks the role of the Minister of the Interior, who was sending in military troops instead of funds. Indeed, many strikes were interrupted by the arrival of military forces between 1899 and 1901.

890b6eec-1fed-550a-92ce-3942e2797947.name: Calligraphic Panel (*Levha*)
890b6eec-1fed-550a-92ce-3942e2797947.short_description:
From the 16th century, calligraphic panels were highly popular in the Ottoman Empire. This one was written by Hüsni in 1877. The style of writing used is *celi sülüs*, or *thuluth*. This style was widely used for inscriptions on buildings and other objects, and a number of individual sheets and large calligraphic panels were also written using this style. Beautifully illuminated religious quotations, written on large panels, were used to decorate mosques. Some of these panels were intended to be painted on tile and were first drafts before the designs were recreated on the tiles.  
The manuscript is inside a golden frame decorated with flowers, which help balance the composition. In Arabic, it reads, "surrender to the command and desire of God and submit to the fate determined by him."
