898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.name: *Head of the Great Sphinx, Pyramids of Geezeh July 17th, 1839*
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.short_description: Roberts depicted the Sphinx some twenty years after Giovanni Battista Caviglia had excavated at Giza in 1817 and had cleared masses of sand away from the monument, which up to that point had been buried right up to its neck. Subsequently, he succeeded in clearing the whole front of the Sphinx. At the point of Roberts’ visit, the sphinx was visible from the top of the head to the floor of the temple between its paws. After its initial discovery, the Sphinx soon became one of the foremost fascinations for early European Egyptologists, including Auguste Mariette, the founder and first director of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, Gaston Maspero, who conducted a survey  of it in 1886, and the British scholar E. A. Wallis Budge.It also proved fascinating for Orientalist artists and artisans all over Europe. In Roberts' artwork, the stone-cut monument is rendered in great detail, carefully recording also the far-reaching damage to the Sphinx’s face, the cause of which had already given rise to much discussion and speculation at the time. The Pyramids in this view are that of Cheops, or the Great Pyramid, seen on the right, and on the left, that of Cephren, also known as the Second Pyramid.

89a137fb-7ff4-50b4-b635-4fb544d4dd2a.name: *Winters in Algeria*
89a137fb-7ff4-50b4-b635-4fb544d4dd2a.short_description: Between 1872 and 1873, the famous American Orientalist painter Frederick Arthur Bridgman went on a long trip around North Africa, travelling from Tangier to Algiers, via Tlemcen, Oran, Constantine and Biskra. This trip was the inspiration for his book *Winters in Algeria*, which contains many of his works depicting Algerians' daily lives in the late 19th century.
89a137fb-7ff4-50b4-b635-4fb544d4dd2a.author: Leila Zeghmi

89f4e566-e82c-56e3-b94a-d8bd68a1f680.short_description: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc. *Tercüman*, the interpreter of a diplomatic mission.

8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.name: Letter from Father Joseph Yazbek to the Maronite Patriarch Yuhanna el-Hajj
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.short_description: A small but growing Maronite community settled in the Chinatown area of Boston in the 1890s. In 1893, the Archbishop of Boston, John Williams, assigned F. Gabriel Korkemaz as the first Maronite priest. He was succeeded by his cousin, F. Stephan Korkemaz, two years later, and shortly afterwards by F. Joseph Yazbek. At the time, the hundred-or-so families that formed Boston's Maronite community worshiped at the St. James' Church on Harrison Avenue. Father Yazbek later bought a four-storey building on Tyler Street, which he remodelled to include a chapel, social hall, and priest's residence. This letter is a copy of a letter sent by Father Yazbek to the Maronite Patriarch Yuhanna el-Hajj, inviting him to the ceremony dedicating the Syro-Maronite chapel to Our Lady of the Cedars of Lebanon.
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

8a229227-3cb6-53ea-978a-a63f9f557d11.name: Patent for the invention of the fountain pen with a replaceable ink cartridge
8a229227-3cb6-53ea-978a-a63f9f557d11.short_description: Pedagogue, engineer and mathematician Petrache Poenaru was the first Romanian inventor to obtain a patent. After 1821 he studied in Germany and then in France. While in Paris, he invented the fountain pen with a replaceable ink cartridge, a pen devised to ensure a constant flow of ink, preventing ink leaks, and to allow the replacement of some of the component parts. On 27 May 1827 the Manufactures Bureau within the French Ministry of Internal Affairs granted him for this invention a patent with a validity of five years. Although his invention did not become known at the time and was not commercially exploited, Poenaru is considered to be the first inventor to receive a patent for a fountain pen.

8a58f4f9-1644-5ff0-8f2d-9e17a9b86098.name: Bills from the Beirut Tramway and Electricity company
8a58f4f9-1644-5ff0-8f2d-9e17a9b86098.short_description: Two bills from the Beirut Tramway Company. The first is for the value of 22 Ottoman pounds, and is dated to 1 February 1896. The second is for the value of 11 Ottoman pounds and is dated to 1 November 1990.

8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.name: ‘Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918)
8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.short_description: Portrait of 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918). He was born in 1842 in Istanbul. In 1876 he became Sultan and after the lost war with Russia in 1877, he was forced to agree to the 1878 Congress of Berlin. The signatory powers of the congress allowed Austria to occupy Bosnia-Herzegovina, which belonged to the territory of the Ottoman Empire. In 1888 he had to accept the occupation of Tunisia by France. He tried to modernize the Ottoman Empire with the help of Germany, but in 1908 a revolution of Turkish officers forced him to abdicate. He died in 1918 in Istanbul.
keywords: 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina; Tunisia

8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.name: *Théâtre Impérial du Châtelet. Aladdin and the magnificent lamp; the genies of the lamp (ballet).*
8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.short_description: The tale of Aladdin became very popular following the rise of Orientalism in the 1820s, and became the subject of multiple adaptations for opera and for theatre. In 1863 Adolphe d'Ennery and Hector Crémieux also transformed it into a "féerie" (fairy play). This féerie, a genre which chose great legends as its subject and spanned many different mediums (ballet, on-stage special effects) was extremely popular in 1860s France.
8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.artist: Engraver: Auguste Tricon; artist: Auguste Belin

8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.name: *Rusul Khyma with the attack of the Honorable Company's cruisers on the evening of 11 November 1809*
8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.short_description: This image records one of the many battles between the fleet of the Qawasim rulers of the lower Gulf and the British, who were determined to end their economic and political hegemony in much of the region and gain overall control of the Gulf as a vital corridor between India, the Middle and Near East, and ultimately Britain.This composition shows the Qawasim stronghold of Ras al-Khaimah with the Hajjar mountains in the background, as seen from the sea by the artist, a soldier participating in the British attack on the town. A small number of British ships are positioned along the coast, and billowing smoke in the background on the right evokes an atmosphere of menace and impending major conflict. The British sent a squadron of frigates to Ras al Khaimah to attack and rout out the enemy. Troups disembarked in the afternoon, and despite all attempts by the Qasimi forces - their bravery and skillfullness even acknowledged by the British - by 10 o'clock the town was in ashes, the powerful fleet of the Qawasim, comprising more than 50 very large dhows, destroyed.
8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.name: *Pulpit on the Platform of the Mosque of Omar*
8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.short_description: This image, etched after having been originally drawn by Samuel Prout after a sketch made on the spot by F. Catherwood, shows the ‘Minbar al-Saif’ of the Al-Aqsa mosque precinct, on the southern side of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, right next to the south gateway to its raised platform.  Originally built by Saladin in the 12th century, it was later restored in the 14th century by Burhan al-Din, whose name is also used to refer to the structure.  It forms an important part of the Haram al-Sharif revered by Muslims. The third-most sacred site in Islam, it marks Islam’s first qibla and the spot from which the Prophet undertook his night journey to heaven. The image was first published in 'Landscape Illustrations of the Bible', consisting of Views of the most remarkable places mentioned in the Old and New Testaments. From original sketches taken on the spot and engraved by W. And E. Finden. With descriptiions by the Rev. Rhomas Hartwell Horne, B.D. In 2 Vols, Vol 1, John Murray and Charles Tilt, London 1836.

8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.name: Lithographed Qur’an, originally written by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.short_description: This Qur'an, originally caligraphed by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Shukr Zadeh is the first Qur'an to be printed in an Islamic country by way of lithograpy. It was produced around 1850 AD.While printing had begun in Europe many centuries ago, the Islamic world continued to favour handwritten books, and most certainly as regards copies of the Holy Qur’an. In 1834, the first edition of Gustav Fluegel’s printed Qur’an was published, while in the Ottoman Empire, the printing of Qur’ans began only in the second half of the 19th century, both in Egypt and in Istanbul. Most were lithographed, as they had the look and feel of manuscripts. Most importantly, all the required recitational signs could be rendered accurately.

8b73574b-b242-5496-8220-49ca7d6386ab.name: *The Arrival of the Holy Crown at Buda*
8b73574b-b242-5496-8220-49ca7d6386ab.description: The history of the Holy Crown goes back a long way and tells a story full of dramatic event. During the reign of Queen Maria Theresia, the Holy Crown was preserved in Vienna. In 1780, when the Holy Roman Emperor Joseph II (1765–1790), son of Maria Theresia, ascended to the Hungarian throne, the Holy Crown was kept in Vienna but Joseph II refused to be crowned with it or take the coronation oath. For this reason he was named *Pál Ányos*, and this is why his nickname “king of Hut” was widespread all over in Hungary. Following his death, the Holy Crown was returned to Buda in a ceremonial procession to the Royal Castle. On the occasion the diet was summoned there, which had last happened in 1530. The engraving represents the ceremonial procession, and is well known as the first and only example of such a festive event in Hungary.
8b73574b-b242-5496-8220-49ca7d6386ab.short_description: An engraved representation of the return of the Holy Crown of Hungary from Vienna to Buda in 1790.
8b73574b-b242-5496-8220-49ca7d6386ab.method_for_datation: On the basis of the object itself
8b73574b-b242-5496-8220-49ca7d6386ab.obtention: Purchased from an art dealer between the two world wars in Budapest.

8b73574b-b242-5496-8220-49ca7d6386ab.author: Beatrix Basics

8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.short_description: Roger Broders was a French illustrator and artist best known for his travel posters promoting tourism destinations in France. Broders' illustrations were distinctive for their simple lines and bold, flat areas of colour, combined with noticeable graphical perspective showing the featured mountains and seascapes in the background. Broders' illustrations depicting people show active, elongated figures wearing elegant, contemporary clothes. His posters were simply and boldly lettered identifying the destination, and were supplemented with a brief slogan.

8bca273e-4101-56b4-9c21-1783781d5f11.name: *The future kingdom*
8bca273e-4101-56b4-9c21-1783781d5f11.short_description: The Franco-Prussian war (1870–71) led to the production of a great number of cartoons, in an attempt to lift morale and stay strong during the difficult conditions of Paris under siege. This cartoon mocks Bismarck and the Prussian soldiers.

8c28d282-9632-5ae4-81b1-ed79c1035940.name: Poem
8c28d282-9632-5ae4-81b1-ed79c1035940.short_description: This poem was written by Antonio Cappelletti in honour of Emperor Franz Joseph's visit to Cairo on 20 November 1869.

8c2abbac-16e2-5805-a239-068b6318e25d.name: *Hüdavendigar* Newspaper
8c2abbac-16e2-5805-a239-068b6318e25d.short_description: After the *Tanzimat* (reforms), newspapers in Arabic, Persian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Albanian, Kurdish, English, French, Italian and German began appearing in the Ottoman Empire. Some of them were bilingual as Turkish-Greek, Turkish-Armenian and Turkish-Arabic. *Hüdavendigar* was a provincial newspaper of Bursa and it was first published on 19 February 1869. The same year, starting with the 80th issue, the back page was printed in Armenian. The paper was published twice (Wednesday and Saturday) and then four times a week. It was 50 x 25cm. Subscription for a year was 100 kuruş, for six months was 50 kuruş and one issue was 20 para (1/2 kuruş). It continued to be published until 1953 under different names.

8c948912-a36b-5142-9ff7-26c982ac3b28.name: *The opening of the exhibition, by Blass. M. Carnot and his entourage, pass under the Eiffel tower*
8c948912-a36b-5142-9ff7-26c982ac3b28.short_description: The Eiffel tower was opened in March 1889 by the President of the Republic, Sadi Carnot, in the presence of several foreign rulers. This inauguration, taking place at a moment of great political tensions, gave rise to many sarcastic comments mocking how the government was using the Exposition Universelle (world fair) for its own gain.

8cbe678a-dcda-57dc-87ce-36a2c9a08898.name: *The Tent of the Arabs Sent by the Governor General of Algeria to Guard the Algerian Pavillion at the Trocadero* \[Paris Exhibition, 1878\]
8cbe678a-dcda-57dc-87ce-36a2c9a08898.short_description: Paris, International Exhibition, 1878. The text of the magazine describes a big tent built in the garden of the Algerian Pavilion with camel fur, fixed with ropes of the same material and strong bamboo canes. Some Arabian men stayed there, sent by the general Algerian governor, and dressed in the typical light-blue uniform of the "Turkish people", or with a red blanket, typical of the region. The Algerian Pavilion was meant to represent the colony through the reproduction of the Campo Marte and Trocadero buildings and also in the garden.

8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.name: *The Sultan receives the prince Ioan I at his palace in Dolmabahce, Istanbul*
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.short_description: In May 1864, prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza dissolved the Parliament and announced his intention of imposing a new constitution (in fact, a modified version of the 1858 Paris Convention, which granted him greater executive powers). Since the Principalities were under Ottoman sovereignty, it was necessary to obtain the sultan’s approval. Therefore, Cuza travelled to Istanbul, where he had several meetings with sultan Abdul Aziz, who eventually recognized the act. Cuza’s visit to Istanbul and its successful outcome were described in an article published on 30 July in the French journal *L'illustration*. The article, written by P. Paget, the journal’s correspondent in Wallachia, was accompanied by a drawing made by Cuza’s court painter, Carol Popp de Szathmar, who depicted one of Cuza’s meetings with the sultan.
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.type: Drawing (after a sketch by Carol Popp de Szathmari)

8f8640bd-04ac-5181-ba28-bef663422bf2.name: *Panoramic View of Makkah - Arabia (West Asia). Panoramic View of Makkah during the Celebration of the Pilgrimage of the Muslims to the Kaaba, where the religious treasure is guarded*
8f8640bd-04ac-5181-ba28-bef663422bf2.short_description: This coloured print, perhaps from a late 19th-century, Spanish newspaper or magazine, shows a birds-eye view of the city of Makkah with the Holy Mosque and Ka'bah at the centre. The view was recorded from one of the rugged mountains surrounding the city. Hundreds of pilgrims are seen to approach from afar and converge on the city gates. that lead to the sanctuary. The print shows close compositional similarities to an early 19th century drawing by the English officer and artist Charles Hamilton Smith (1776-1859). Smith, although not known to have visited the Arabian peninsula, produced an album of drawings - possibly in turn taken from older engravings - with views from Syria, Persia and Arabia sometime between 1818 and 1846.

90753f8b-1041-579e-af7d-41a335a9669a.name: Black Sea: Sevastopol port
90753f8b-1041-579e-af7d-41a335a9669a.short_description: Founded by Yekaterina II (Catherine the Great) in 1783, Sevastopol became a very active military and commercial port following the Russian annexation of the Crimea. The siege of Sevastopol from 1854 to 1855 was the one of the most critical points of the Crimean War.

90898679-94a2-5a74-9442-dce1eaec5acf.name: *Shepherd with his sheep*
90898679-94a2-5a74-9442-dce1eaec5acf.short_description: Sheep husbandry has always been a traditional agricultural occupation in the Romanian lands. Shepherds spent summers in mountainous regions, where they found pastures for their flocks, and descended into lower valleys for the winter. Transhumance is still practiced in Romania. During the Ottoman sovereignty, one of Moldavia and Wallachia's economical obligations towards the Porte was to send sheep, but also sheep wool, cheese, meat and tallow in the Ottoman Empire.

9161faa0-4fe2-54c4-a25b-05a4938ccfd9.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
9161faa0-4fe2-54c4-a25b-05a4938ccfd9.short_description: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.

919aef03-f815-592e-ab38-dd26eb510ac9.name: *Tughra* (imperial monogram).
919aef03-f815-592e-ab38-dd26eb510ac9.description: Written in pen and illuminated in gouache, this is the *tughra* (imperial monogram) of Suleyman the Magnificent (r. AH 926–73 / AD 1520–66). *Tughra*s were used on documents, or firmans (commands) which were issued by the Diwan (Council of State). This example bears the Sultan’s name, Suleyman Shah, and that of his father, Selim, and the phrase ‘the one who is always victorious’. Within the widest loop, formed by the Han (Title), is an intricate illuminated design. Painted in black and gold are fine floral spirals set against a ground of minute cloud-scrolls. The inner loop is filled with split-palmette scrolls and florets. Further floral- and cloud-scrolls fill the space between the ascending parts of the letters. The spiral design is also found on underglaze painted ceramics. The practice of illuminating the *tughra* was established by the ruler Bayazid II (d. AH 917/ AD 1512), under Suleyman they became ever more elaborate. The subject of the document to which this *tughra* was attached is not known.
919aef03-f815-592e-ab38-dd26eb510ac9.short_description: This copy of the *tughra*, or imperial monogram, of Süleyman the Magnificent is written in black pen. Contained within the curves and lines of the letters are delicate illuminated designs of floral spirals in black and gold.
919aef03-f815-592e-ab38-dd26eb510ac9.method_for_datation: This is the *tughra* of Suleyman the Magnificent (r. 926–73 / 1520–66). Due to the type of illumination employed this particular example probably dates to about 956 / 1550.
919aef03-f815-592e-ab38-dd26eb510ac9.method_for_provenance: The *tughra* would have been inscribed and illuminated at the imperial court of Suleyman the Magnificent in Istanbul, Turkey.

91b66b55-0c91-5d46-b3bc-af6121a29639.name: Portrait of Mihai Suţu
91b66b55-0c91-5d46-b3bc-af6121a29639.short_description: Mihai Suţu was the last Greek prince of Moldova. The Sublime Porte imposed Greek rulers in Wallachia and Moldavia (called “Phanariotes” because they came from Fanar, the Greek neighborhood of Istanbul) at the beginning of the 18th century and maintained them until 1821. During this period some modernizing reforms, influenced by the ideology of the Occidental Enlightenment, were introduced in the Romanian countries. The drawing was made by French artist Louis Dupré, who visited Greece, Istanbul, the Balkan Peninsula and the Near East in 1819 –1820. In the summer of 1819 he arrived in Bucharest together with Mihail Şuţu, whom he had met in Istanbul. He painted Şuţu laying on a red divan, wearing Oriental clothes.

91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.name: *Asia. Athalide*
91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.description: In this lithography, Asia is represented as a woman dressed in Turkish style. She is Athalide, the lover of Bayaceto, in a 1762 play by Jean Racine. She wears Circassian clothes. Orientalist painting usually represents Circassian women in the seraglios or harems.
91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales

91e561d2-6530-5965-bd21-e1a70b9ef590.name: Air France Brochure
91e561d2-6530-5965-bd21-e1a70b9ef590.description: This folding brochure, illustrated by an artist signing as Mariner, advertised Air France services to the Orient and the Far East for the summer of 1939. On its cover, the route runs from London and Paris to Marseille, divides as it crosses the Mediterranean and meets again in the Levant, before continuing to Baghdad and onwards to India, Southeast Asia and Hong Kong, a journey of eight days and more than 15,000 kilometres. A Dewoitine D-338 airliner, cut open to reveal its passengers, crew and cargo, promises comfort as well as speed. At the European end of the route stands a woman in an evening gown, while at the far eastern end another woman appears in East Asian dress. Inside, timetables, fares, visa regulations and currency tables guide the traveller across a map divided by colonial and mandate rule. Before the summer season was over, the outbreak of the Second World War disrupted this network of long-distance civilian air travel.
keywords: Advertisment; Travel; Flight; Art Deco; Holidays

9438f959-d105-5cd5-890f-56a9cdcc3715.name: *Josef Freiherr Philippovich-Philippsberg (1818–1889)*
9438f959-d105-5cd5-890f-56a9cdcc3715.short_description: Portrait of Josef Freiherr Philippovich-Philippsberg (1818–1889). In 1836 Philippovich-Philippsberg joined the Austrian Army. In 1878 he became commander of the Austrian invading forces for the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On 17 August 1878, Austrian troops occupied Sarajevo. Philippovich commanded Austrian forces in Bosnia until 1880.

94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.name: Stalactites
94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.short_description: The artist and architect Jules Bourgoin travelled to Egypt many times. Between 1880 and 1884 he took part in a French archaeological campaign to Cairo, directed by Gaston Maspéro, from which he brought back a number of drawings of Egyptian monuments and Arab architecture.

949e75ce-78cf-577e-95d9-461cc0734d07.name: *On the omnibus (or inside a tramway passing over a bridge)*
949e75ce-78cf-577e-95d9-461cc0734d07.short_description: The question of multi-passenger transport emerged first in capital cities. In the 17th century, Blaise Pascal had the idea of creating transport lines in Paris with scheduled itineraries for horse-drawn carriages seating 8 people. This type of transport saw increasing success in the 19th century as did, on the other hand, the use of cabs with specific destinations. In 1855, all Parisian omnibus companies were merged into the "Compagnie Générale des Omnibus" at the request of the Chief Commissioner of the Seine, in a desire to prioritise the movement of tourists visiting the Exposition Universelle (world fair). Steam or fuel-powered tramways were also introduced in the 1870s. This drawing does not accurately reproduce the atmosphere of those overcrowded omnibuses, however, as Mary Cassat chose to foreground a mother who, lost in her thoughts, does not notice the nanny playing affectionately with her daughter.

94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.name: Design for book cover: *Tres morillas me enamoran*
94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.description: The influence of the Spanish Muslim art can be seen in this design that references the illuminated books of Alfonso X, King of Castile (1252–1284). The arches, the dresses and the general decoration recall the illuminated pages of the 13th century illuminated books preserved in the Royal Collection and Library.
94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.author: Ana Cabrera

94ef618f-769f-5a52-9aa5-25aac10e2373.name: London-Baghdad in 8 Days by Simplon-Orient-Express & Taurus-Express
94ef618f-769f-5a52-9aa5-25aac10e2373.description: Travel poster depicting the Arch of Ctesiphon (Taq Kasra) and advertising the passenger train route connecting London to Baghdad, operated by the "Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits" (International Sleeping-Car Company). The journey combined two rail routes: the Simplon Orient Express from London to Istanbul, and the Taurus Express from Istanbul to Aleppo and Baghdad. Until 1935, the Syrian section terminated at Tel Kotchek, from where motor vehicles transferred passengers to Kirkuk; the final leg to Baghdad was by metre-gauge railway. The poster was issued by the French Paris-Lyon-Méditerranée (PLM) railway company and designed by French illustrator Roger Broders (1883–1953), best known for his Art Deco travel posters commissioned by the PLM, characterised by simple lines and bold, flat areas of colour.
94ef618f-769f-5a52-9aa5-25aac10e2373.author: Giulia Martini

94f28839-f709-5cc7-bf4c-84a06693c6fe.name: Dust jacket; template for the edition of Heinrich Böll: *Ansichten eines Clowns*. Roman. dtv No. 400. Original drawing affixed to a pre-printed cover showing the title and publisher’s device
94f28839-f709-5cc7-bf4c-84a06693c6fe.description: Celestino Piatti (1922–2007) was one of the best-known graphic artists in Europe in the last third of the twentieth century. From 1961 to 1992, he designed the look of the Deutscher Taschenbuch Verlag (dtv). A whole generation of readers in German-speaking Europe associates works of world literature with the covers he designed for them. Piatti read all the books whose cover he designed, and confidently translated their key scenes into memorable images. The Swiss National Museum was able to acquire from the artist’s estate over 1,000 print templates, trial proofs, and cover designs produced for dtv.
keywords: Celestino Piatti; Dust Jacket; Print Template; Heinrich Böll; Ansichten eines Clowns; Duggingen; Basel-Landschaft; Graphic Design

957ca713-c1c0-5491-8542-164f00239bf4.name: *Aladdin, or The Magnificent Lamp: sketch of the set for act 1 or act 2*
957ca713-c1c0-5491-8542-164f00239bf4.short_description: The tale of Aladdin and his lamp was very popular in the theatre and the opera following the rise of Orientalism in the 1820s. Its first performance as an opera in 1822 was so successful that gas was used for the first time ever at the Opéra de Paris, to light up the lamp on stage.

962e3954-6b7a-5ffb-a881-c31a4aa6530a.name: The Benefits of Hygiene. Hydrotherapy
962e3954-6b7a-5ffb-a881-c31a4aa6530a.short_description:
In Italy, the first law that introduced compulsory education (the so-called “Coppino law”) dates back to 1877. Only the first three years of elementary school were compulsory. In 1911, the law extended compulsory education up to the age of 12.  
During the 19th century, illiteracy in Italy was very high: in 1867, almost 70 per cent of spouses who could not sign their marriage certificate because were unable to write; in 1901, there were still about 39 per cent of spouses who could not sign their marriage certificate.
962e3954-6b7a-5ffb-a881-c31a4aa6530a.holder: Archivio unico regionale di deposito – Solomeo di Corciano
962e3954-6b7a-5ffb-a881-c31a4aa6530a.author: Giulia Barrera

96fe1797-6dfb-529b-ad9e-f9a5fe80e499.name: Page from an Album made for Jahangir
96fe1797-6dfb-529b-ad9e-f9a5fe80e499.short_description:
This is a two-sided painting with elaborate bordered illustration on one side (verso) and bordered calligraphy on the other (recto). The verso illustration has brilliantly colored scene delineating six human figures and two birds. The whole composition can be divided into three grounds. All the human figures occupy places in the foreground and a youth (central figure sitting on a raised pedestal) is shown in explanatory posture with left hand pointing upwards. He is wearing an orange top (*Jama*) belted on the waist, blue trousers and long boots. On his right an old man wearing a light yellow *jama* and a blue hat is drawn engaged in an argument with the young man. Three other male figures, including a reclining man bent on a club, are standing on the left side of the youth. The reclining man is draped in a yellow top and is juxtaposed in astonishment. The sixth figure, a female attendant, is shown peeping surreptitiously on this dramatic event. A light blue wine vessel can be seen on the grassy (with some flowers) ground.  
The middle ground of the composition is comprised of a brown arched architecture with a rectangular inscription, distant dark trees and mountains. The upper ground holds a bright blue sky and large birds of greenish and bluish hues. The entire composition is surrounded by several borders with the middle golden one being the most prominent. It consists of flowers and creepers which enhance the beauty of the whole composition. The entire verso illustration is then surrounded by an elaborate border consisting of many animals and birds in movement. These figures include leopards, lions, deer, rabbits, eagle etc. The broad border is replete with plants and flowers. These are all drawn in gold with touches of colors.  
The recto side of the page shows diagonally inscribed calligraphy in Persian within decorative borders. Broad outer border has a scene of falcon hunt and feast shown in gold with sublime treatment of different hues.
96fe1797-6dfb-529b-ad9e-f9a5fe80e499.dates:
Recto calligraphy: Hegira first half 10th century / AD first half 16th century;  
Verso image: Hegira c. 998 / AD c. 1590; album: Hegira c. 1017-1028 / AD c. 1608–19
96fe1797-6dfb-529b-ad9e-f9a5fe80e499.dimensions: Image: Length: 21.6cm x Width: 12.2cm; Sheet: Length: 42.2cm x Width: 26.5cm
96fe1797-6dfb-529b-ad9e-f9a5fe80e499.method_for_provenance: This painting was made by the Hindu court artist Kesu Dâs, who worked for the Mughal emperor Akbar (1542–1605).The composition is adapted from a 1544 engraving by the German artist Georg Pencz (c.1500–1550) entitled, "Joseph Telling His Dream to His Father," which Jesuit missionaries disseminated in India during the mid-16th century. The scene is on the back of a sumptuously illustrated page with a poem by Mir Ali, who was famous throughout the Persian-speaking world as a calligrapher. Both painting and calligraphy were collected by Akbar’s son and successor, Jahangir (1569–1627). He ordered the pages to be assembled in a special album and given elaborate borders of scenes from a hunt by an unknown but highly skilled court artist.
96fe1797-6dfb-529b-ad9e-f9a5fe80e499.bibliography:
Bailey, Gauvin Alexander, *The Jesuits and the Grand Mogul: Renaissance Art at the Imperial Court of India, 1580 – 1630*, Washington, D.C.: Freer Gallery of Art, Arthur M. Sackler Gallery, Smithsonian Institute, 1998.  
Brand, Michael and Lowry, Glen D., *Akbar’s India: Art from the Mughal City of Victory*, New York: The Asia Society Galleries, 1985.  
Renard, John (ed), *Windows on the House of Islam: Muslim Sources on Spirituality and Religious Life*, Berkely: University of California Press, 1998.  
Ziad, Zeenut, *The Magnificent Mughals*, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2002.
keywords: Page; Album; Jahangir; Drawing; Watercolor; Gold; Ink; Paper; India; Asia; Pencz; German; watercolour
materials: Ink, opaque watercolor, gold on paper

9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.name: *Egyptian village scene*
9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.short_description: Egyptian men and women are seen here in a town or village on the Nile. In the shade of an overhanging tree a market stall displays its wares, including paper lanterns and bread. At the stall behind, sugar cane is for sale. In the background is a mosque with a white minaret, though not distinctive enough to establish the scene's locality. Pilleau had visited Egypt in the winter of 1842-43 with Lieutenant Colonel George Everest (after whom Mount Everest was named) and two other companions, on their way home from India. On his return to England he published a set of twelve coloured lithographs, Sketches in Egypt (1845), which, like the better-known publications of Wilkie, Roberts and Owen Jones in the same decade, fuelled popular interest in Egypt and the Holy Land.
9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
keywords: Economy; Market; sugar cane; Egypt; local product; rural life; eating; paintings
materials: Water- and bodycolour over pencil, heightened with white, on blue/grey paper

9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.name: Gold to the country from the [Italian] colony in Tunisia
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.short_description:
This receipt certified that Leone Moreno (Tunis, 1852-1940) “donated gold to the country” in order to support Italy’s war effort during WWI. Leone was the grandchild of Mosè Moreno, a Jew from Livorno who migrated to Tunis around 1830. In Tunisia, the Morenos became successful in business. Leone’s father and brothers were traders and bankers, while Leone was an agricultural entrepreneur.  
He was a nationalist and was one of the Italians who actively resisted the French policy of assimilating the Italians in Tunisia. He employed only Italian workers on his estate and supported the Società Dante Alighieri, a society aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad. Leone Moreno also generously supported the Italian hospital Giuseppe Garibaldi and the Italian orphanage “Principe di Piemonte”.
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.author: Massimo Sanacore

9b3b7415-4847-52e1-a035-b476f65ee03e.name: Viaduct on the Haifa–Dar‘a line
9b3b7415-4847-52e1-a035-b476f65ee03e.description: This postcard depicts a viaduct on the Haifa–Dar'a section of the Hijaz Railway, identified on the image as the "Chemin de fer Hamidié du Hidjaz (Caifa–Deraa)". Published by the Société Lumière of Lyon, it presents the railway’s substantial engineering works within the landscape of Palestine. The postcard was circulated through the Levant, bearing French Levant postage stamps postmarked Beirut, Syria, on 11 October 1905 and Smyrna, Ottoman Turkey, on 17 October 1905.
9b3b7415-4847-52e1-a035-b476f65ee03e.holder: The Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Hajj and The Arts of Pilgrimage

9ba9df9d-f2a1-5166-9182-6b24185296d6.name: Map (*Africa magna*)
9ba9df9d-f2a1-5166-9182-6b24185296d6.description: An 18th-century map of Africa (*Africa magna*), its toponyms are written in Latin.

9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.name: A battle between Algerian ships and ships of the Naples Royal Navy, which chased the Algerian ships and ultimately destroyed them by firing cannon shots on 17 May 1792
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.short_description: In the 18th century the Kingdom of Naples and the Regency of Algiers were among the countries that competed for the control of trading routes in the Mediterranean and that participated in privateering. Only in 1856, by the Declaration of Paris, did Great Britain and most of other major European countries (with the exception of Spain) declare privateering illegal. By the time, Algeria had already become a French colony. The French military occupation of Algeria had in fact started in 1830.
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.author: Rossana Spadaccini, Giulia Barrera

9c9255a5-9a88-5f13-953c-48f2830112c9.name: Ottoman official document containing the *Tughra*
9c9255a5-9a88-5f13-953c-48f2830112c9.short_description: The Ottoman Sultan's certificate presents an expressive, secular form of calligraphy. It is crowned by the ornate, triangular seal of the Sultan, the *tughra*. Here, it is the *tughra* of Sultan Mahmud I (1730-1754). The lines are written narrowly in gold, black and, red ink and each one is written in an upward curve to prevent the possibility of forgery. Official, ornamentally decorated documents, such as this one, would hang in offices or private houses and served as status symbols.
9c9255a5-9a88-5f13-953c-48f2830112c9.method_for_datation: Inscription mentions Sultan Mahmud I (1730-1754) and date Hegira 1150 / AD 1737.

9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.name: Newspaper *al-Wataniyya*
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.short_description: This issue of *al-Wataniyya*, only part of which is shown here, dates to 1 February 1901. *Al-Wataniyya* was a bi-monthly newspaper founded by N. A. Mokarzel and written, edited and printed in Philadelphia, USA. It was distributed internationally.
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.name: The Students’ Benevolent Fund of the Società Dante Alighieri
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.short_description: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies into promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children, by providing free books and clothes.
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.author: Giulia Barrera

9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.name: *Plan of the Suez Canal*
9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.short_description: This map was printed four years before the opening of the Suez Canal, in a book published in Algiers by the local Chamber of Commerce. It is evidence of the interest that the opening of the Canal aroused in North African countries other than Egypt, because of the business opportunities that it created.
9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.author: Chiara Artico

a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.name: Mico Liubibratic (1839–1889)
a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.short_description: Portrait of Mico Liubibratic. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.
keywords: Mico Liubibratic; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina

a12c9928-1d6f-5b1e-814c-74692d5b8de6.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911)
a12c9928-1d6f-5b1e-814c-74692d5b8de6.short_description: Portrait of minister Sayed Ahmed Pasha Arabi (Urabi). In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.name: *A Mamluk Resting with his Horse*
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.description: The Mamluks were excellent horsemen and aroused the attention of artists like Carle Vernet and Sebastian of Bourbon, a member of the Spanish Royal family. Artists did not need to have journeyed to the Near East or Arabia to be labelled Orientalists. This is a good example, because the authors did not travel to the Near East.
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.artist: Original: Carle Vernet; copyist and lithographer: Sebastián María Gabriel Borbón y Braganza
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales

a3bc9b66-ff10-54b0-b271-4ef2ef26a367.name: *King Solomon’s Mines*
a3bc9b66-ff10-54b0-b271-4ef2ef26a367.short_description: The book is a narrative of an expedition to East Africa, in search of gold - the King Solomon's mines; a pretext for an imaginary trip to a part of the world that at the end of the 19th century attracted travellers, scientific explorers, adventurers and travellers: the delta of the Nile in Africa.
a3bc9b66-ff10-54b0-b271-4ef2ef26a367.holder: National Library of Portugal, Digital Library
a3bc9b66-ff10-54b0-b271-4ef2ef26a367.artist: Author: Ryder Haggard; translator and editor: José Maria Eça de Queirós
a3bc9b66-ff10-54b0-b271-4ef2ef26a367.author: DGPC

a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.name: Photograph of Bab Idris street
a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.description: Pictured here is Bab Idris street, leading to Bab Idris, the city's western gate and the entrance to the old town. By the time of Ahmad Bey al-Jazzar's reign (1777–1804), the city had four main gates: Bab al-Dirka to the south, Bab al-Santiya to the west, Bab al-Dabbagha to the north, and Bab al-Saraya to the east. Jazzar Pasha built fortifications between these four main gates, which was not a fortified gate. Other city gates included Bab Yaqub, also in the east, Bab Abu Nasr at Burj square, and Bab Idris. These non-military gates are reflections of the city's rapid expansion, particularly due to an increase in trade.
a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki

a3cbcd9b-cf11-5b68-9f33-19a8c46c9df8.name: Map of the Ottoman province (vilayet) of Damascus marking the Hijaz Railway line in red.
a3cbcd9b-cf11-5b68-9f33-19a8c46c9df8.description: The map is part of the Pocket Atlas of the Ottoman Lands: The Geographical and Statistical Conditions of the Ottoman State. It depicts the territories extending from the Hama region in the north through Damascus, the Hauran, and Jordan to the northern Hijaz. A red line begins at Hama and continues southward, representing the Hijaz Railway. A western branch extends toward the Mediterranean coast, corresponding to the railway connection between the main line and Haifa. The principal heading reads سوريه ولايتى, Vilayet of Syria. The vilayet was the principal provincial administrative unit established under the Ottoman provincial reforms of the nineteenth century. Vilayets were divided into sanjaks, and beneath the title the map identifies the four sanjaks of Damascus, Hama, Hauran, and Karak.
a3cbcd9b-cf11-5b68-9f33-19a8c46c9df8.bibliography: Masters, Bruce, *The Arabs of the Ottoman Empire, 1516–1918: A Social and Cultural History*, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2013.

a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.name: *Panorama of the Compagnie Transatlantique* (French Line). *The "La Ville de Rome" steamer leaving the port of Algiers via Montenard*
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.short_description: The emergence of steam boats in the 19th century allowed important maritime trade relationships to develop. In 1855, the Pereire brothers adopted this new method of transport and founded the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique (The French Line). The first line built served New York. In the 1880s the company then established an important line from Marseille to North Africa, which consisted of a 12-steamer strong fleet, the "sister ships" of the "Ville de Rome", which was first put into use in 1881. In March 1889, the "Ville de Rome" was run aground and washed up on the shores of Menorca. The passengers were evacuated in time, but the storm caused the wreck of the ship to break in two.
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.artist: Photographer: Neurdein Frères; artist: Frédéric Montenard

a434b4ec-9d28-510b-baac-35beab8f46ee.name: A map of the area around the 'Turkish graveyard' in the town of Livorno (Tuscany). The graveyard is represented as a small green rectangle
a434b4ec-9d28-510b-baac-35beab8f46ee.short_description: In 1762, Muslims living in Livorno were granted a plot of land outside the city walls, near the beach, to build a graveyard (highlighted in green in the map). The graveyard remained in use until the second half of the 19th century. A Muslim graveyard existed in Livorno even before the 18th century. A significant Muslim community lived in the town. Its first members were captives taken to Italy as slaves. Muslim traders settled in town as well. In 1856, the graveyard was enlarged and surrounded by walls. In 1872 it was demolished to build a road and some of the graves were moved to the city graveyard.
a434b4ec-9d28-510b-baac-35beab8f46ee.author: Daniela Tazzi

a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.name: *Inside a Jewish household*
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.short_description: This copy of a beautiful watercolour by Charles Lallemand shows the inside of a bourgeois Jewish household. This snapshot of daily life reveals a great deal of similarity between Jewish and Muslim traditional dress and interiors.
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar

a508bec6-1ea4-51c9-b5d8-a70ddc2a7baf.name: *Dans le harem: Divertissement Arabe.* For piano.
a508bec6-1ea4-51c9-b5d8-a70ddc2a7baf.short_description: Musical composers' fascination with the "Orient" manifested itself in their music and their titles. The sphinx, for example, was a recurring symbol of "Egyptomania".

a532878c-9737-5402-a686-e8febd96a222.name: *Klemens Wenzel Lother of Metternich-Winneburg (1773–1859)*
a532878c-9737-5402-a686-e8febd96a222.short_description: Klemens Wenzel Lothar of Metternich was the leading diplomat at the Congress of Vienna (1815) who organized the balance of power between the European states. The core of Metternich's policy was supporting Austrian hegemony in Italy and preventing Russian hegemony in Germany. In the German Confederation, there existed an equilibrium between Austria and Prussian influences. Metternich's so-called "balance of power" politics ensured peace in Central Europe for a generation.

a541b832-d774-57c4-adb6-f83fd670fffc.name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico “L. Pigorini” (National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography), Exhibition Room
a541b832-d774-57c4-adb6-f83fd670fffc.short_description: The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus. This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered together by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a central museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by palethnologists in Italy.

a553f0d5-43fe-535b-9d07-0aff49e30b7f.name: *Portrait of Father António Vieira*
a553f0d5-43fe-535b-9d07-0aff49e30b7f.description:
In this engraving Arnold van Westerhout represents the humanist, António Vieira, as a man of knowledge and a father of the Society of Jesus. His gaze extends beyond the horizon: whether towards Brazil where he grew up or to Lisbon, the home he always defended with the staunchness he employed to preach the Christian faith. The Flemish artist concentrates on António Vieira's facial expression to heighten his altruistic character which is shown in constant reflection about the human condition and his own experience of it.  
This painting celebrates António Vieira's exemplary life dedicated to the defence of human rights, whether to those of Brazil's indigenous peoples or the Jews persecuted by the Inquisition.  
Born in Lisbon in 1608, António Vieira departed to S. Salvador da Bahia with his parents at the age of six. He entered the Society of Jesus in 1623 and become a priest 12 years later. He played a fundamental role in the relationship between Jesuits, coloniser and the indigenous peoples of Brazil, exhibiting in his sermons an anxiety about the socio-political conditions that would characterise his missionary activity. With knowledge of the languages and costumes of the Brazilian Indians he was a missionary and a preacher with a humanistic vision.  
Following independence from Spanish domination, Vieira returned to Lisbon where he became an important figure in the court of King João IV. He rapidly became a key player in state decisions and helped re-establish the Portuguese Empire's economic, political, diplomatic and religious profile in Lisbon and in the most important colony at the time, Brazil. In the latter, and at Vieira's advice, the Commercial Company of Brazil was instituted with two intentions: to resist Dutch invasion and to foment the recovery of local sugar production with the objective of export to Europe.  
In Lisbon he proposed economic reforms that would force a change in the doctrine of the Inquisition. He terminated the distinction between 'new-Christians' and 'old Christians' in order to attract the investments of Jews who had fled the Kingdom. The idea generated a conflict with the Society of Jesus and the Dominicans, which resulted in António Vieira being persecuted by the Inquisition.  
Later in his life he was one again accused of heresy. This was as a result of a letter he sent to the Bishop of Japan in which he outlined his *Theory of the Fifth Empire*. Here he predicted that Portugal was predestined to be the next grand empire following the Assyrian, Greek, Persian and Roman.
a553f0d5-43fe-535b-9d07-0aff49e30b7f.short_description: An engraving by Arnold van Westerhout of António Vieira, a Portuguese Jesuit Priest, writer and preacher. As a senior diplomat as well as a missionary in Brazil, he became both an influential figure in Portuguese culture and in the defence of human rights of indigenous peoples.

a565ef0e-9407-5de9-8ab2-05297761a4c9.name: *Amphitheatre at El Jem*
a565ef0e-9407-5de9-8ab2-05297761a4c9.short_description: This drawing is by Sir Grenville Temple. The Amphitheatre of El Jem is seen as a symbol Roman Tunisia. Sometimes called the Colosseum of Ancient Thysdrus (El Jem), this amphiteatre is the only in the world, other than the colosseum of Rome, to have preserved all three of its tiers. Considered the most beautiful monument of ancient Africa, the Amphitheatre of El Jem was listed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO on 26 October 1979.

a63d4087-1cd4-5ec4-b4ee-b445f990556b.name: *Chargeurs réunis. French steam-travel company (with destinations in South America)*
a63d4087-1cd4-5ec4-b4ee-b445f990556b.short_description: At the end of the 19th century, France tried to catch up with its counterparts in the arms trade, as it had begun to fall behind England, Germany and others in recent decades. Commercial interests also played a part. In 1872, the Compagnie des Chargeurs Réunis established a maritime relationship between France and South America for the movement of passengers and merchandise. As this poster shows, they put great emphasis on the different services passengers were provided aboard these steamers.

a7135e6b-1b7e-5ddf-9568-b2daa5ac8d45.name: Louis Pasteur's work on silkworm illnesses. *Healthy Worms*
a7135e6b-1b7e-5ddf-9568-b2daa5ac8d45.short_description: Silkworm farming developed in both France and Italy from the 15th century. Over-intensive farming caused the spread of various silkworm-based illnesses in the mid-19th century. Louis Pasteur, the famous scientist known for his work on the rabies vaccine amongst other things, was called on to find a cure. In 1870 he published *Une Étude sur la Maladie des Vers à Soie*, in which he proposed the use of various preventive methods, which proved effective. Pictured here is an illustration of silkworms immune to illness.

a73e56c5-c169-5488-aff8-8af1170f4be3.name: “The conqueror of Europe”
a73e56c5-c169-5488-aff8-8af1170f4be3.short_description:
In Italy, the pandemic of influenza of 1918, known as “Spanish flu,” caused about 600,000 deaths out of a population of about 40 million. Around the world, it caused around 20 million deaths.  
The name derived from the fact that Spain – which did not participate in WWI – unlike other Western countries did not have press censorship, and so the news regarding the epidemic made headlines on newspapers. However, the epidemic did not start in Spain, but in China, then spread to the USA and arrived in Europe involuntarily carried by the US soldiers dispatched overseas.  
It hit particularly hard because the population was weakened by the hardships caused by the war and many medical doctors had been drafted, leaving civilians with insufficient medical assistance.
a73e56c5-c169-5488-aff8-8af1170f4be3.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
a73e56c5-c169-5488-aff8-8af1170f4be3.author: Giulia Barrera

a7580d59-2cc3-599d-bd19-8d4d84fa37af.description: Designed by Jean Olivier in 1929, this Art Deco poster for Air Union's Lignes d'Orient announced a weekly seaplane mail service from Marseille to the Eastern Mediterranean. A simple silhouette of a seaplane hovers over bands of blue and sprayed white that suggest sky, cloud and sea at once. Below, the timetable promises that a letter posted on Saturday morning would reach Naples the same afternoon, Athens on Sunday and Beirut on Monday. An arrow beyond Beirut points further east, towards the routes the company would soon open.

a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.name: Süleymaniye waterway map.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.description:
The Süleymaniye waterway map is handmade on unfinished paper. The waterway was designed to supply water to the entire complex of the mosque, including its *imaret* (soup-kitchen), *maristan* (hospital), *maktab* (school) and public fountains. Fed by the Aypah (Kirazlı) and çınar springs, the highest-capacity branches of the Halkalı water supply system, this waterway supplied the Süleymaniye Complex as well as 80 other points in Istanbul. The map shows the waterway in detail from its source all the way to its end, including the places where it is joined by other waterways, the points where it enters the city through the walls, and especially the water-distribution centres and aqueducts.  
  
The map was prepared without a scale and has a schematic style. Therefore, many structures and neighbourhoods cannot be precisely placed. At the far end of the map there is the drawing of the Süleymaniye Complex.  
  
Such waterway maps tell the story of water from springs being conveyed via pipes, crossing valleys in aqueducts, its pressure adjusted at certain points, being sent off in various directions at distribution centres and reaching public fountains. These maps also provide information about the urban structure; how people lived, and the infrastructure and buildings in a given quarter. For example, the Roman Aqueduct of Valens (AD 375), known as Bozdoğan Aqueduct in Turkish is introduced as 'the big aqueduct in the Horse Market'. The names of the people and the structures receiving water from this aqueduct are also given. The water of the Halkalı network could be distributed to private estates only on the written permission of the sultan. For instance, we find the house of Süleyman the Magnificent's dentist, Moshe Hamon, (AH 899–962 / AD 1490–1554) listed as 'House of Hamudoğlu'.  
  
From the Süleymaniye Complex waterway map, we learn not only how the water was brought to the city but also about the quarters where the courtiers and dignitaries resided. Therefore, the waterway maps are important for describing the social topography of the city.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.short_description: Istanbul has always suffered from water shortage due to a lack of sufficient springs nearby and its demand was met by conveying water via aqueducts from afar. Waterway maps provide information about the routes from the springs to the city, monuments on the way and the social structure of the city.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.dates: Hegira second half of the 12th century / AD 18th century.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.method_for_datation: Although the map does not have a date it is clear from the names of people and structures therein that this is an 18th-century document. For example, it is known that water was supplied to Taygun Palace in 1161 / 1748, a building shown on this map; therefore, this map must have been prepared after 1161 / 1748.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.method_for_provenance: The map does not bear any date. However, that our copy is an 18th copy is clear from the names of people and structures given therein. For example, it is known that water was supplied to Taygun Palace in 1161 / 1748, a building shown on our map; therefore, this map must have been prepared after 1161 / 1748. Public services such as the water supply were under the supervision of the state and due to this fact the waterway would have been designed and constructed by the official architects of the Topkapı Palace.
a7ce0231-54e8-5757-928a-48c3c0b66585.obtention: The map was transferred to the museum in 1923 from the Directorate of Supplies for Pious Foundations.

a9007630-d81f-5724-87ad-6fc202c954e3.name: Gufas (Quffas) on the Tigris at Baghdad
a9007630-d81f-5724-87ad-6fc202c954e3.short_description: This stereoview by the Keystone company (a reprint from an older negative) was part of a popular box-set of images about Mesopotamia. They were sold across Europe. The text on the reverse contains description of the geography, architecture (explanation of minarets, lament at the absence of fine buildings through devastation of the city by fire, habit of wealthy to live in unpretentious houses to avoid the attention of the Turkish taxman) and history, plus brief caption in half a dozen languages.

a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.name: *Athenian Bride*
a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.short_description: Louis Dupré (1789–1837) visited Greece in 1819. He exhibited Greek subjects at the Salons of 1827, 1831, 1833 and 1855. In 1825 he published a set of colored lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyages à Athènes et Constantinople*. Dupré recorded his experiences of travel in the Levant in 1819 mainly through portraits of the people he met. In addition to the lithographs in this book, Dupré also produced loose broadsheet lithographed plates. Many of these are in the possession of the Cabinet des Estampes of the Bibliothèque Nationale. Much has been written on Dupré. *Athenian Bride* depicts the preparations of an Athenian wedding. The bride patiently waits as the groom is ritually shaved.
a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.author: Tsigakou, The Rediscovery of Greece, p.191

a98c40f6-a4df-55c5-b720-2e843d2d4af6.name: General view of the excavations in the crypt of the Saint-Geneviève monastery, in 1807.
a98c40f6-a4df-55c5-b720-2e843d2d4af6.short_description: Although only the library remains today, in the 18th century there used to be a great monasterial complex - the Abbey of Sainte-Geneviève - next to the Church of Saint-Etienne du Mont in Paris. The monastery was destroyed to make space for the construction of the Panthéon and Rue Clovis. The architect Bourla, who was tasked with its demolition, made a great number of sketches and organized many excavations in the crypt, where a number of sarcophagi were discovered. His son Alexandre, who had helped out on the site as a child, worked on the drawings that illustrated the archaeological reports.

ac179872-390d-5c7a-ab3a-2c5e56a1e7df.short_description: This collecting card commemorates the 1889 Exhibition in Paris. Visitors were able to satisfy their relentless curiosity about other cultures through exploring recreations of houses from foreign and past cultures.

ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.name: *The Gate of the Roman*
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.short_description: Since King Otto (1833–1863) made efforts to transform immediately ruinous Athens into a European capital worthy of its erstwhile glory, around the mid-nineteenth century spectacular changes were made in the urban planning structure and morphology of the city. A reliable image of Athens at this time is given by Du Moncel in his book *Vues pittoresques des monuments d’Athenes*. This particular representation of Athens is the Roman Agora (Forum Romanum), natural continuation of the ancient Agora, was built c.10BC, the Gate of Athena Archegetis, which is depicted here. In Ottoman times this Roman gate was known as the Pazaroporta (Bazaar Gate), because it was used as the entrance to the bazaar, the commercial centre of Athens, which occupied the area between the Roman Agora and the Library of Hadrian.
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.artist: Théodore Achille Louis, Vicomte du Moncel

ac642d3b-bbff-52e1-97f4-243c52c3dde5.short_description: When Italy became a nation state in 1861, the illiteracy rate in the country was 78 per cent. Illiteracy was particularly high in the countryside. In 1877, the “Coppino Law”, made three years of elementary school mandatory and free of charge.

acfa76a9-edd6-5f50-bcf6-fef161aa398e.short_description: Despite the abolition of the slave trade in 1848, slavery continued to exist in 19th century Congo in other forms. Missionaries went to Congo with the aim of freeing these slaves, partly for ethical reasons but partly also in the hope of converting them, and often by buying them first with their own special funds.

ae99c07a-63eb-5689-9082-49c9d484164e.name: *Suq al-Hamidiyya, Damascus*
ae99c07a-63eb-5689-9082-49c9d484164e.short_description: The Suq al-Hamidiyya, built in 1886 and 1894, is by far the biggest and most famous suq in Damascus. This bazaar street also links the two most important historic buildings, the Umayyad Mosque and the Citadel. It was built along its western section by incorporating earlier structures, whereas the eastern part of the street was a completely new construction cutting through the existing buildings. The commercial thoroughfare is 450 metres long and 8.70 to 9.90 metres wide, its enormous size and the high standard of its execution accentuate new design principles. So in various respects, this suq is a very interesting example of structural change in a traditional commercial centre.
ae99c07a-63eb-5689-9082-49c9d484164e.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

af6de1c1-aac3-5b48-9d6c-1e99228574c4.name: Military personnel records
af6de1c1-aac3-5b48-9d6c-1e99228574c4.description:
The information sheets are part of the medical examination prior to the training of the new recruits. The newly enrolled were destined for the Protectorate which, due to the pressure of public opinion, refused the presence of Spaniards in that area.  
The records, along with a pair of photographs, gathered information on individuals’ social and professional backgrounds, as well as descriptive data and anthropometric values. Those values were used by the Medical Corps to determine the minimum size permitted to enter in the Army, but they were also important according to the existing racial theories in Spain.  
The sheets refer to these soldiers as “Moors” in a generic way, a colloquial and sometimes pejorative term of Latin etymology, which alludes to the population of the Maghreb with no regard to their origin, ethnicity or beliefs.

b0efd48f-c5dd-580f-97dd-0300a02b3fc2.name: *La Tunisie martyre*
b0efd48f-c5dd-580f-97dd-0300a02b3fc2.short_description: *La Tunisie Martyre: Ses Revendications* (better known by its abbreviated title, *La Tunisie Martyre*) is a Tunisian book written in French and published in Paris in January 1920, attributed to Abdelaziz Thâalbi (Abdelaziz al-Thalibi). Having arrived in Paris on 10 July 1919, Thâalbi started writing a book by the title *Tounes al-Shahida* (Tunisia the Martyr). Although the published book does not bear his name, Thâalbi admitted to having written it in Arabic, as can be seen from the reports sent from Tunis by the future leaders of the Destour party. As he was not able to write in French, he asked his friend Ahmed Sakka, a lawyer living in Paris, to translate the book into French. A few months after the publication of *La Tunisie Martyre*, an arrest warrant was issued for Abdelaziz Thâalbi. He was arrested on 28 July 1920 in Paris, and transferred, by escort, to Tunis, where he was taken to the military prison and charged with jeopardizing national security.

b111e780-75c2-51e3-bb5c-dda0ea9e3015.short_description: Pictured here are three Tunisian men sentenced to death and a photograph of a public execution using a guillotine brought over especially from Algeria. These two young men, barely 20 years old, were implicated in the events of the 7 November 1911, known as the Jellaz Affair. The memory of this execution is still alive today in Tunisia.

b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.name: *Temple and fountain of Zaghwan*
b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.short_description: This drawing of the temples and fountains of Zaghwan was drawn by Sir Grenville Temple in the mid-19th century. The triumphal arc and the nymphaeum are carved with two important tales from the city's ancient history. This water temple, located at the feet of Mount Zaghwan, contains a 30 metre long semicircle nymphaeum, bordered on the inside by arched galleries fitted with various niches. At its feet lies a pool, flowing with water which is then carried all the way to Carthage.

b3ad190f-fed9-546e-924a-e3b7f2699f23.short_description: Émile Prisse d'Avennes (1807–1879) drew this plan of the Ka'aba in Mecca, a detailed view of the place of pilgrimage which had so fascinated Europeans.

b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.name: *Cairo, from the Gate of Citizenib, looking towards the Desert of Suez*
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.short_description: Although entitled 'Cairo from the Gate of Citizenib, looking towards the Desert of Suez', this view actually shows Cairo as seen from Tel Zaynum, situated to the south of the city. The monuments depicted include the tombs of Fatimah Khatun and Sultan Khalil on the left and the mosque of Sayidah Nafisah on the right. In the background, one can discern both the Cairo citadel on the right and the Madrasah of Sultan Hassan on the left. Notwithstanding the incorrect identification of this area of Cairo, the scenes gives a good impression of one of its quarters with its traditional urban architecture and historical monuments before major urban development projects were undertaken under the Khedive Ismail (1863-1879), who was determined to turn Cairo into a modern, international city  on a par with European capitals.

b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.name: *Djouni. The residence of Lady Hester Stanhope*
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.short_description: William Henry Bartlett was a prolific topographical artist who travelled extensively in search of new and interesting subjects for his drawings. He visited North Africa and the Middle East seven times and made several other trips in Britain and Europe, as well as North America. Popular demand for travel books was high during the 1830s and 1840s and Bartlett contributed illustrations to several of them including about a dozen written by himself. His aim as he described it was 'to give lively impressions of actual sights'. Bartlett visited the celebrated Lady Hester Stanhope, a British adventurer and traveller, at her residence in Joun in the Lebanon in June or July of 1834 and produced this watercolour during his visit.
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.author: Victoria and Albert Museum

b5237ac5-6bde-593f-8bf3-56257cd8a060.name: Tunisian Coffee Shop at the Trocadero [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
b5237ac5-6bde-593f-8bf3-56257cd8a060.short_description: A half circular hall arranged as an Oriental coffee shop with a Tunisian orchestra of four musicians playing typical instruments. The instruments played are a lute, a type of violin used in the Middle Ages, a little drum decorated like a cymbal and a derbuka, which is a terracotta drum shaped like a particular vase.

b532b295-4380-5ea9-951e-1e3a7150eff2.name: The Central Asian railway. Proposal for a direct line from Europe to India.
b532b295-4380-5ea9-951e-1e3a7150eff2.short_description: Charles Cotard was an engineer and graduate of the famous École Polytechnique who dedicated his life to developing new transports. As the engineer-in-chief during the digging of the Suez Canal, he offered Ferdinand de Lesseps a partnership, with the goal of creating a railway line from Europe to India. The biggest obstacle to his plan was the number of hilly or mountainous regions which needed to be crossed. However, Charles Cotard saw many diplomatic and economic opportunities (such as closer relations between England and Russia) in this venture. The map's caption shows the new route's predicted cost and time for passengers compared to the current available routes.

b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.name: *Entrance to a Private Mansion, Cairo*
b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.short_description: The Scottish artist David Roberts spent six weeks in Cairo. In his times, Arab architecture was much less known in Europe than that of ancient pharaonic temples, and Roberts' images of ancient and modern Islamic architecture in Cairo were the first window into this ‘exotic’ world for many Europeans. This image shows the monumental, two tiered, marble entrance portal to a Cairo mansio.Although the entire building is not shown, the composition evokes some of its most characteristic aspects: the walls are high and windowless, protecting the inhabitants' privacy. At the same time, a delicately carved, openwork alcove or mashrabiya projects above the entrance portal to allow air and light into the room behind and to provide those within the chance to observe life outside without being seen themselves. With the arrival of major urban development in Cairo from the mid 13th/ 19th century onwards, many traditional buildings were either erased or modified to reflect the new European-style tastes of the urban elite. In the process, the traditional courtyard-style layout of Cairene houses was was often replaced by European-style designs, and traditional architectural elements like mashrabiyas made way for the latest in European technology, including glass pane windows.
b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

b5f42e1e-ecb3-55b6-8189-981be88d8626.name: National loan 1920. *Banque National d'Escompte de Paris… National loan, 1920, 6%... Sign up for a loan and save in the future…*
b5f42e1e-ecb3-55b6-8189-981be88d8626.short_description: As the First World War was proving longer and more costly than predicted, the French government took out two loans in 1915 and in 1918 to fund weaponry and other wartime expenses. After the war, more loans were taken out to rebuild the country. Posters with simple messages were used to persuade the population that these loans were beneficial to the country, and would have huge returns. We can see on this poster, for example, a French cockerel standing on a horn, a symbol of abundance, from which money is overflowing.

b64a1bbb-e3ff-5209-9c78-7304ea9b3d7d.name: Water Well
b64a1bbb-e3ff-5209-9c78-7304ea9b3d7d.description:
This powerful and emotional drawing reflects everyday life, community and endurance. The artist uses a limited colour palette of dark, soft tones to create a haunting atmosphere. At the centre, a group of women stand close together around a dark well, while a solitary figure stands apart, carrying heavy containers. The scene is both quiet and heavy, conveying the physical and emotional weight of their daily labour.  
The well itself becomes more than just a source of water; it also symbolises life, connection and memory. The women's bent figures and joined forms suggest unity and cooperation, as if they rely on one another for strength and survival. Their faces are not clearly visible, giving the image a universal quality and turning the women into symbols of resilience and shared struggle rather than individuals.  
The artist’s use of shading and blurred lines gives the drawing a dreamlike and timeless quality, as if the moment exists in both the past and the present. The open space and faint background add to the sense of isolation and endurance in a harsh environment.  
Overall, *Water Well* powerfully and poetically captures the intersection of women’s labour, community and survival. The simple composition and muted tones draw attention to the emotional depth of the scene, reflecting not only daily life in rural Jordan, but also providing a broader commentary on strength and perseverance.
b64a1bbb-e3ff-5209-9c78-7304ea9b3d7d.holder: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts

b7235782-b04a-58a3-83e1-28d83ed8c19d.name: *Plan for the House of the Invalids in Pest*
b7235782-b04a-58a3-83e1-28d83ed8c19d.description:
The engraving and etching was made after the original drawing by the imperial architect, Anton Erhard Martinelli (1684–1747), for the largest Baroque building, the House of the Invalids in Pest. The building, which was never finished following Martinelli's original plans, is today the City Hall of Budapest.  
The building, which was originally used as a military hospital, has three gates, the central one leading to the former chapel where there are allegorical figures of *War* and *Peace* with a statue of *Atlas* above. The façade is decorated with reliefs commemorating Emperor Charles III and Eugene of Savoy. The foundation stone was laid in 1716, and the main façade was finished in 1731. With the death of the architect, Martinelli, construction of the building stopped in 1741. During the reign of King Joseph II it became a casern named after the founder, Charles III. It became the City Hall in 1894 and was transformed for the purposes of the central office by the architect Ármin Hegedűs.
b7235782-b04a-58a3-83e1-28d83ed8c19d.short_description: A printed *veduta* using a mixed technique showing the plan of the largest Baroque building in Budapest – the House of the Invalids in Pest – designed by Anton Erhard Martinelli (1684–1747). The building, which was never finished following Martinelli's original plans, was rebuilt at the end of the 19th century as the City Hall of Budapest, for which use it is still inhabited today.
b7235782-b04a-58a3-83e1-28d83ed8c19d.method_for_datation: On the basis of the signature
b7235782-b04a-58a3-83e1-28d83ed8c19d.obtention: Transferred from the Capital’s collection in 1945

b7235782-b04a-58a3-83e1-28d83ed8c19d.author: Beatrix Basics

b7682ec7-12af-5614-9211-58be3ac85cee.name: *On sale everywhere. The 1900 Paris Exposition Universelle, an illustrated publication with around 2000 engravings…*
b7682ec7-12af-5614-9211-58be3ac85cee.short_description: The 1900 Exposition Universelle (world fair) saw the publication of many related articles, guides and other works. This poster is advertising a booklet, featuring illustrations by various famous artists. These booklets were later collected and bound together to make an Encylopaedia.

b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.name: *The Progress of Steam: A View in White Chapel Road, 1830*
b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.short_description: Steam engines carried a great variety of goods in the 1830s. This English cartoon imagines the chaos the widespread use of collective and individual carbon-fuelled transport systems would bring (pollution, noise, cumbersome, etc.) to one of London's great arteries, Whitechapel Road. These vehicles provided fashionable services such as on-board coffee.

b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.name: *The Emperor of Austria ascending the Great Pyramid*
b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.short_description: William Simpson wrote in his autobiography: "I went out one day and saw the Emperor of Austria lugged to the top of the Great Pyramid by two Arabs as if he had been only an overland passenger". Many visitors were unceremoniously hauled to the top of the monument by local inhabitants, helping unfit and often overweight tourists to clamber up the huge blocks. Emperor Franz Joseph was one of many European dignitaries in Egypt in November 1869 for the opening of the Suez Canal. Simpson was employed by the Illustrated London News as their "Special Artist". Photography would soon replace such drawings.

b84ae82c-3c44-5a73-ae00-06a543d2035b.name: Dr Béchir Denguezli, doctoral thesis in medicine
b84ae82c-3c44-5a73-ae00-06a543d2035b.short_description: Pictured here is the cover of a doctoral thesis in medicine, written by Béchir Denguezli at l’Université de Bordeaux in 1897. Dr Béchir Denguezli was the first Tunisian doctor to study at a French university, and his thesis was on the subject of smallpox.

b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.short_description: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.short_description: Alfredo Melani, teacher and then director at the school of applied arts in Milan, was one of the main exponents of oriental decorative motifs in Italy. During the 1880s he published a series of works and texts discussing eastern art, often in the form of handbooks and essays. Subsequently, toward the end of the century Camillo Boito pioneered courses in the history of styles at the Accademia of Brera. Dell’ornamento nell’architettura written by Melani, includes a whole chapter about Muslim decorations, from which the drawing showing wooden grills from mosques is taken.
