e76f2cd3-86ac-51b9-b076-e4ec90a04fbc.name: *Illustrations of the One Thousand and One Nights, vol. 1*
e76f2cd3-86ac-51b9-b076-e4ec90a04fbc.short_description: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. Galland was its first French translator, translating with much liberty what he had been able to understand in the early 18th century. The translated *One Thousand and One Nights* were extremely successful, and became the subject of a variety of art forms, both allowing Europeans to become better acquainted with the Arab world, but also forming the basis for lasting stereotypes.

e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.name: *Interior of the Great Temple at Baalbec*
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.short_description: This view into the interior of the Temple of Bacchus at Baalbek, Lebanon originally formed appeared in 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c', illustrated views printed in 3 series over 2 volumes (37 plates, 37 plates, and 48 plates for each series respectively) including maps and title pages. The publication resulted from the 1836-1838 collaboration between the painter William Henry Bartlett, the engraver Ebenezer Challis and the Publishers Fisher, Son and Co. The architectural and artistic details they recorded subsequently inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam, who based one of the ceilings at Osterley House on the ceiling of the Temple of Bacchus and the portico of St George's, Bloomsbury on its portico. Since the 1860s, many tourists visited the site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulous, illustrated publication that further popularised the site.
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis

e794e773-3653-5861-a65a-803eb3349875.name: The trademark for the Italian company Smalto Tripoline, manufacturer of paints and varnishes
e794e773-3653-5861-a65a-803eb3349875.short_description: The trademark of the company “Smalto Tripoline” (a factory producing enamels and paintings), based in Verona (Veneto, the same region as Venice).
e794e773-3653-5861-a65a-803eb3349875.author: Margherita Martelli

e87a28c8-480d-590e-ba3c-b84ef6e8d476.name: Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861)
e87a28c8-480d-590e-ba3c-b84ef6e8d476.short_description: Portrait of Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861), riding a horse. When he came to power in 1839, he tried to re-occupy lands lost to Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, the ruler of Egypt. In this effort he was supported by Britain and Austria. In 1840 a combined British-Austrian fleet cut off the supply lines of the Egyptian army and forced the Egyptians to sign the 1840 Convention of Alexandria. Abdul-Mejid was able to win back Syria and Palestine. In 1849 he granted the Hungarian refugees exile. In 1861 he died and left his throne to his brother Abdülaziz.
keywords: Abdul-Mejid, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Syria, Palestine; Hungarian refugees

e89aa553-0859-53ef-ad91-bdaddb8ac231.name: *Hüdavendigar* Paper in Armenian
e89aa553-0859-53ef-ad91-bdaddb8ac231.short_description: After the *Tanzimat* (reforms), newspapers in Arabic, Persian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Albanian, Kurdish, English, French, Italian and German began appearing in the Ottoman Empire. Some of them were bilingual as Turkish-Greek, Turkish-Armenian and Turkish-Arabic. *Hüdavendigar* was a provincial newspaper of Bursa and it was first published on 19 February 1869. The same year, starting with the 80th issue, the back page was printed in Armenian. The paper was published twice (Wednesday and Saturday) and then four times a week. It was 50 x 25 cm. Subscription for a year was 100 kuruş, for six months was 50 kuruş and one issue was 20 para (1/2 kuruş). It continued to be published until 1953 under different names.

e93e2356-ce89-5c16-b735-40f476c4b07d.name: Gustave Eiffel. The Eiffel Tower in 1889.
e93e2356-ce89-5c16-b735-40f476c4b07d.short_description: Today, the Eiffel Tower is one of the great symbols of Paris and of France. This metal structure, a huge technological achievement in and of itself, was constructed by Gustave Eiffel (1823–1923) for the Exposition Universelle (world fair) of 1889, which celebrated the centenary of the French revolution. Many of his contemporaries, such as Guy de Maupassant, considered the structure hideous and called for its demolition. This drawing recalls the tower's function as a symbol of the vitality of French industry, highlighting its exceptional size and its proximity to the great Palais de l'Industrie, which housed the Dôme Central, the first building to use electricity on a large-scale.

e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.name: Receipt for a subscription among the Italians in Tunisia to buy Italy a plane
e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.short_description:
We do not know whether the Italians living in Tunisia who collected money to buy Italy a plane were aware that Italy would use planes to bomb civilians in Libya. To be sure, they supported Italian expansionist policy.  
This receipt bears the signature of the treasurer of the committee that was collecting funding to buy Italy a plane, Giuseppe Di Vittorio, the owner of a successful construction company. The donor, Ugo Moreno, was another “big man” of the Italian community in Tunisia: a lawyer, he established a bank (Banca Italiana di Credito), in 1901 started an oil company (Societé du Pétrole) and in 1919 became town councillor in Tunis.
e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.author: Massimo Sanacore

e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.name: Chorographical plan of the attack waged by Lord Exmouth against Algiers on 27 August 1816
e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.short_description: In the spring 1816, a large Anglo-Dutch fleet headed by Admiral Lord Exmouth forced the three Ottoman regencies of the so-called “Barbary Coast” (the coastline of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli; “Barbary” comes from “Berber”, the name given to the original people and culture of North-West Africa) to release Christian captives and to sign agreements over the abolition of corsairing, or privateering, and the enslavement of captives. In August, the Anglo-Dutch fleet returned to Algiers and made additional demands to the Turkish regent, who refused to comply. Lord Exmouth then ordered a heavy bombardment that destroyed the Algerian navy and part of the city of Algiers.
e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.author: Edoardo Garis, Giulia Barrera

e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.name: Tekke panel
e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.short_description: *Hüsn-i Hat* is a type of calligraphy. Turks probably started to get interested in calligraphy after their arrival to Anatolia. The brightest period was during the Ottoman era. Calligraphy developed well beyond its functional role; it almost played a similar role to the paintings in Western art in terms of the level of its aesthetics. The script *"Ya Hazreti Şeyh Sultan Yusuf Sümbül Sinan Kaddes Allahu sırrahu"* (religious text, untranslatable) is written on a black background with *Zerendud* (gilded) calligraphy and designed as the *sikke* (tall felt hat) of the Sünbüli order. It stands over a small table in Rococo style and there are hyacinth flowers on either corner of the upper part. The sides of the plate are surrounded by two borders that are Rococo in design.
e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.name: *The Citadel of Cairo, the Residence of the Pasha*
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.short_description: The citadel of Cairo, here captured by the Scottish artist David Roberts in the 1830s, was undergoing major changes under Muhammad Ali Pasha (1769-1849). Having overcome the Mamluks of Egypt in 1805, Muhammad Ali erased all traces of their rule, including remaining palace and administrative structures. He rebuilt most of the walls, erected four new palaces - his own royal residence in the northern enclosure, a courthouse, an expansive terrace and state-of-the-art accomodation for his army. At the heart of the citadel complex, Mohammad Pasha ordered a memorial mosque for his son Tusun in the Ottoman style. Building work on the mosque lasted from 1828 to 1848. Roberts incorporates the new structures existing in his time, like the palace on the right, cresting the hill - the ongoing building works on the mosque are concealed by the Mamluk structure in the foreground on the right.
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.name: An example of Italian colonial propaganda: 'Italy takes up the sword of ancient Rome. To the Italian sailors who are fighting in Tripolitania'
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.short_description:
Italian sailors fighting in Libya are portrayed as the heirs of Roman soldiers. On the ground, one can see the personal military equipment of an ancient Roman soldier. The modern sailor holds in his right hand the Roman soldier’s sword and in his left hand an Italian flag.  
Italian colonial rhetoric looked at the Roman Empire as a justification for Italy’s colonial conquests of Libya. The current territory of Libya was for centuries part of the Roman empire.

eb38e940-7f0e-59a0-8e60-897613089325.short_description: Within the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion. Working activities were part of the project of the reconstruction of a hypothetical neighbourhood. The picturesque recreation of the Algerian surroundings includes a drinkseller offering lemonade kept fresh inside "*alcarazas*” made by red earth.

ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.name: The Gallery of Machines – Section of French Telegraphic Machines, Marinoni's Continuous Paper Model [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.short_description: Two of the most important inventions of the 19th century, the rotary and four-colour printing (quadrachrome), are attributed to Augusto Ippolito Marinoni. The new machines changed the printing of journals, achieving up to 18,000 to 20,000 copies per hour. Marinoni had extraordinary success in Paris, where his factory produced 4000 samples of machines which also sold in London, Berlin and Vienna. In Italy at the time, only the journal *Il Secolo* had a "Marinoni".

ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.name: *Histoire de la Princesse Boudour (Conte des mille et une nuits)*, Translation by J.C. Mardrus of *The Story of the Princess Boudour: Tales of a Thousand and One Nights*
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.description: François-Louis Schmied (1873–1941) and Jean Dunand (1877–1942) worked together on *Histoire de la Princess Boudour*, the French translation of one of the tales from *The Arabian Nights* by J.-C- Mardrus. The painter, illustrator, engraver, bookbinder and publisher François-Louis Schmied was primarily responsible for producing the graphic design and handling of the text, the illustrations and their wood interpretations. Dunand produced a lacquered metal plaque that transmitted the eroticism and voluptuousness revealed throughout the text. Using warm colours, Princess Boudour is portrayed on a red ground sprinkled with gold, and appears as a very elongated, tubular figure holding a flower with both hands. It’s a limited edition, just twenty copies, it’s a extremely rare Art Deco book.

ecc37fb3-5606-5413-bfb4-48ac62d9c763.name: Turkey. Inside view of the Scutari Hospital during the Crimean war.
ecc37fb3-5606-5413-bfb4-48ac62d9c763.short_description: Florence Nightingale (1820–1910), a British nurse famous for her commitment to and improvement of the health service, was sent to on a humanitarian mission to Scutari in the middle of the Crimean war. With a team of about 30 nurses, she cleaned the hospital and reorganised the wards in order to prevent the outbreak of epidemics. In this image she is pictured in the sick ward, taking various measures to improve its hygiene.

ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.name: *Ruins of Troy: general excavation plan by Mr Schliemann*
ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.short_description: Heinrich Schliemann (1822–1890) was a German businessman who discovered his passion for archaeology whilst travelling. In 1870 he decided to direct an archaeological campaign in Turkey where he discovered the ruins of Troy. Various scandals (stolen objects, scientific errors) quickly destroyed his reputation, and today he is credited only with having created sites which led to important advances in the field. However, this plan of Troy is evidence for Schliemann's efforts to direct the excavations in a rigorous scientific manner.
keywords: Greek antiquities; archaeological excavations; Schliemann; Turkey; plans

edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.name: The Moroccan Embassy in Rome
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.short_description:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered him a gala dinner.  
In this picture one can see Morocco’s Ambassador, his interpreter, two Moroccan dignitaries who travelled with him, an Italian diplomat and another Italian high official.
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

ee0cbe27-f7a7-56db-b5c5-18038a38b0c8.name: Omar Pasha (1806–1871)
ee0cbe27-f7a7-56db-b5c5-18038a38b0c8.short_description: Portrait of Omar Pasha. He was born in Croatia in 1806 near the Turkish-Hungarian border. In 1828 he deserted from the Austrian army and joined the Ottoman administration in Bosnia. After a long career in the Ottoman army, he became the military governor of Bucharest and commanded the Ottoman forces at the siege of Sevastopol in Crimea. In 1862 he suppressed an uprising in Herzogovina and led a victorious campaign against Montenegro. In 1868 he became War Minister and died in 1871 in Istanbul.
keywords: Omar Pasha; Croatia; Bosnia; Ottoman empire; Herzegovina

efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.name: Europeans leaving Alexandria (Egypt) during the antiforeign rioting in June 1882
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.short_description:
Ahmed Urabi, an army colonel of peasant origins, led a protest movement in 1881 against European domination of Egypt’s affairs and in favour of placing constitutional limits on the Khedive’s power. In 1882 Urabi was appointed minister of war and started working for the creation of a national assembly.  
In May 1882, Britain and France, concerned about access to the Suez Canal and intending to protect their financial interests in Egypt, sent a fleet to Alexandria, hoping to weaken Urabi’s nationalist movement. The presence of the fleet only worsened tensions. In June, anti-foreign rioting erupted in Alexandria and left several hundreds dead, including about 50 foreigners.  
18,665 Italians were living in Egypt at the time, mostly in Alexandria and Cairo.
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.author: Giulia Barrera

efe60dc6-7155-5eb3-a180-d0bfbd548106.name: Revenue stamp
efe60dc6-7155-5eb3-a180-d0bfbd548106.short_description: A revenue stamp issued in 1888 during the reign of Khedive Muhammad Tawfiq with the value of one dime. Written at the top is “Egypt Post” in Arabic with its French translation below it. To the left is the value of the dime in French, and in the centre is an image of one of the Giza pyramids and the Sphinx. The first postal stamp was issued in England in 1840. It bore the portrait of Queen Victoria, as suggested by Sir Roland Hill. This stamp was issued twice, in red and in blue. The United States of America was the second country in the world to use stamps, and the first Egyptian stamp was issued in 1866 by order of Khedive Ismail.

f0020c49-694c-556a-855c-e631e86ab20b.name: Survey of Western Palestine
f0020c49-694c-556a-855c-e631e86ab20b.short_description: Field sheet showing a week’s work mapping the environs of Gaza for the Survey of Western Palestine, dated 29th April, 1875. The SWP was the first detailed and fully accurate map ever made of Palestine, at 1 inch to the mile, for the Palestine Exploration Fund. The Survey Party was commanded by Lieut. Claude R. Conder, R.E., and his assistant, Lieut. H.H. Kitchener.

f1166cb3-b783-5cbf-98fd-cd4d924c210b.short_description: The drawing shows the main entrance of the Hotel Excelsior on the beach of the Lido sandbar which separates the Venice lagoon from the sea. Two small towers crowned by domes with decorations stand aside the portal. Particularly interesting is the use of arches in Moorish style, for the main portal and for the loggias in the side wings.

f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.name: *Tunis 2*
f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.short_description:
Designed by Joseph Nash, this is one of the set of views published with accompanying text as Dickinson's Comprehensive Pictures of the Great Exhibition. The prints used the newly available technique of colour lithography to record scenes from the popular 1851 Exhibition. This particular scene shows the Tunisian exhibit, Tunisia being one of few African countries represented at the Exhibition. Exhibits were selected by the bey, Mushir Basha, and included a Bedouin tent. The wealth of material displayed and the charisma of the exhibitors, Hamda Elmkadden and his assistant Saido Belais, ensured that the exhibit proved ‘one of the most remarkable features’ of the Exhibition.  
Following the Exhibition, a government grant was awarded to a committee headed by Henry Cole to purchase items from the Exhibition to form the basis of a Museum of Manufactures (later the V&A).
f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum

f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.name: *The Great Khan of Damascus*
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.short_description: Damascus had long been a major commercial hub in the Middle East, with trading caravans converging on its numerous souqs from all over the Islamic world. Commercial complexes had already flourished in the 18th century and were an integral part of Ottoman modernisation projects in the 19th century. This image gives a wonderful impression of the activities within a traditional Near Eastern khan or market complex in the 19th century. Under high vaulted domes, man and beast are engaged in various activities. Pack animals bring wares or are being unloaded, traders discuss their wares, rest or ponder their accounts. A fountain in the centre provides respite and coolness. On the second floor, figures are visible at the balconies, overlooking the activities below. The print was originally published in Volume I, p. 49, of 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor &c', printed in 3 series over 2 volumes, drawn by William Henry Bartlett and William Purser, engraved by W. Kelsall, with descriptive text by John Carne. Published by Fisher and Son, with series I and II bound together.

f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.name: *Fête Égyptienne: Divertissement de Concert pour Piano: op. 3*
f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.short_description: French "Egyptomania", which began with the campaign in Egypt and lasted the whole 19th century, saw a period of particular intensity during the construction of the Suez Canal. The illustrator of this score, responding to the music's supposedly Egyptian inspiration, focused his illustrations on stereotypical Egyptian images (pyramids, sphinx, palm trees), but notably failed to include images of Egyptian people or daily life.

f23c34bf-814d-5e9e-8baf-ebe84ce157b4.name: *Folies Rambuteau. New quartet from the Auvergne.*
f23c34bf-814d-5e9e-8baf-ebe84ce157b4.short_description: The 19th century saw mass rural to urban migration, particularly to Paris, for largely economic reasons. These migrants often settled with people from their region, who offered them work in specific fields. Thus, those from the Savoy region became specialised in chimney-sweeping, those from the Auvergne were water-carriers or coal-merchants, those from Brittany were domestic workers, and so on. Regional solidarity therefore ensured the survival of regional culture. In this image, for example, a quartet from the Auvergne are advertising their performance in a *café-concert* in traditional dress. Music from the Auvergne was the origin of the Parisian *bal-musette* (a dance accompanied by accordion music).

f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.name: *Interview with Mehemet Ali in his Palace at Alexandria 1839*
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.short_description: This scene shows Muhammad Ali Pasha, comfortably seated on a diwan with sword and waterpipe by his side, receiving a British Delegation at his palace in Alexandria on May 12th, 1839 - an event at which the artist David Roberts himself was present after receiving an invitation from the British Consul General in Alexandria, Colonel Patrick Campbell, to accompany him to the meeting at the city's Arsenal. On entering the audience room, Roberts noticed the magnificent view of the harbour from the window, and he eternalises this impression at the centre of his composition, accentuating at the same time the separation of the Egyptian ruler and his entourage on the left and the six-strong, British delegation on the right. Campbell is seated closest to the ruler, followed by Thomas Waghorn and David Roberts, eagerly leaning forward to listen and observe. Other identifiable individuals include Bogosh Bey, the Armenian chief minister, standing left of the seated Pasha, Dr Tattam, a Coptic scholar commissioned by the British Museum and Mr Pell. Campbell  was soon to be recalled due to his attempts to influence British politics towards Mehmet Ali, whom he greatly admired.

f2797aad-043c-51e6-ba00-d9f4afd964a3.short_description: The illustrated publication *Recherches sur l' origine du Blason et en particulier sur la Fleur de Lis* is a study on emblems with references to Mamluk blasons. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.name: *A Turkish Coffee-House, Constantinople*
f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.short_description: Preziosi was of noble Maltese birth, but against the wishes of his family rejected their chosen profession of the law to become an artist. From 1842, until his death forty years later, he lived and worked in Istanbul, renowned for his vibrant and evocative images of all the different races and cultures of that most cosmopolitan of cities. He became for a time well-known in Western Europe because many travellers, (including in 1869 the Prince of Wales) took his pictures home as souvenirs of their visit. Demand for his work prompted the publication in Paris in 1858 of a series of lithographs, Stamboul Recollections of Eastern Life.This is a fine example of Preziosi’s keen observation of contemporary Ottoman life, rapidly sketched yet full of accurately depicted detail.
f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.author: Victoria and Albert Museum

f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.name: *London-Paris-Constantinople* \[…\] *Orient Express. Paris-Munich-Vienna-Budapest-Belgrade & Constantinople: fast and direct service, without your car and without your passport* \[…\] *Winter 1888–89 ...*
f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.short_description: Founded in 1872, the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-lits was originally a Belgian company. Its founder (Georges Nagelmackers) had the idea of creating a luxury train line, without the need for changes at each border, in order to allow wealthier tourists a more comfortable journey. The opening of the famous Orient Express between Paris and Constantinople in 1883 was an extremely successful example of this.

f32db4ad-178e-583f-be68-731a20b86a1a.name: Map of the Hijaz Railway. Designation in Ottoman Turkish and Arabic
f32db4ad-178e-583f-be68-731a20b86a1a.description: The map is part of the Pocket Atlas of the Ottoman Lands: The Geographical and Statistical Conditions of the Ottoman State. It represents territories extending from Egypt and the eastern Mediterranean in the west to the Euphrates River in the east, and from Damascus in the north to the Hijaz region in the south. The map identifies regions, towns, ports, deserts, mountain ranges and maritime routes in Ottoman Turkish written in Arabic script. A route beginning in Damascus and continuing through Darʿa and Maʿan toward Medina corresponds to the Hijaz Railway. The map table heading is given first in Ottoman Turkish and immediately below in Arabic, reading: "Map of the Hijaz Railway", with a list of stations underneath. Each location is accompanied by a numerical value expressed in kilometres, indicating cumulative distances measured from Damascus.

f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892)
f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.short_description: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.
keywords: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha; Egypt; Arabi (Urabi) revolution; Great Britain

f3e4d209-2bec-5851-8ab2-7247da1e8c09.name: *Sepolcro del Giovedì Santo*
f3e4d209-2bec-5851-8ab2-7247da1e8c09.description: This etching documents the main installation created by the sculptors Angelo and Domenico Piò in the church of the Holy Saviour in Bologna. Antonio Cartolari drew the engines, Petronio Nanni built them, Angelo Sarti was the painter and Marco Montanari the scenographer. It was a tradition to keep a drawn memory of ephemera built during the Holy Week in one of the three churches chosen each year among the 60 selected in the diocese of Bologna for this celebration This was a practice created by cardinal Gabriele Paleotti, that took shape in the eighteenth-century, with sumptuous and solemn liturgies. On the Holy Thursday the Catholic Church celebrated the institution of the Eucharist with the Last supper. The host was taken from the tabernacle and put in the Repository, called the Sepulchre, to commemorate the death of Christ. The repository was an installation built to emphasise the tabernacle holding the holy Eucharist. This etching was part of a booklet, helping the faithful to meditate over the Passion and Resurrection of Christ. The analytical description of the sumptuous installation involving the whole church was made in order to preserve the memory of a work created to last only few days.  The work was made to touch the faithful hearts and at the same time to instruct them about the core of the Catholic faith, thus helping them to follow in the right behaviour preached by the Church. On the altar stand the allegories of Holy Grace, Religion, Faith and Fortitude, defeating the devil. On the cartouche we read the words of St. Paul: “Gratia Dei Salvatoris nostri” “Thanks to the Lord our Saviour” (Tit. II. 11). The rest of the church was uniform, thanks to six installations like this one. All the figures were painted in white to convey the idea of marble, while the architectural details, standing inside niches covered with red and gold material, were made to look like travertine. The spirit animating the whole installation reflected the rhetoric and the ostentation of the age.
f3e4d209-2bec-5851-8ab2-7247da1e8c09.short_description: Among the most significant documented ephemera built in the baroque age are the so-called sepolcri (“sepulchres”). This is an effective example. A group of sculptors, scenographers, sceneshifters, architects and painters erected them in churches during the three days before Easter.

f441f874-4d85-5d61-a241-aca16296bfa2.name: Programme card for the Exposition Universelle of 1900. Phono-Cinéma-Théâtre.
f441f874-4d85-5d61-a241-aca16296bfa2.short_description: World fairs were an opportunity to discover new inventions, and to make them known worldwide. The "cinematograph" was present, in various forms, at the 1900 Exposition Universelle in Paris. The invention of the "Phono-Cinéma-Théâtre" brought sound and image together for the first time, and Henri Lioret and Clément-Maurice Gratioulet used a phonograph to combine the voices and images of famous actors such as Sarah Bernhardt.

f4c22e70-95b9-576e-af85-4267539e8ace.name: Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial
f4c22e70-95b9-576e-af85-4267539e8ace.short_description: This illustration, taken from the Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial  had didactic objectives. It attempted to show the inhuman treatment slaves were subjected to (yoke, chains, whipping) by traders. In this image, a mother is begging King Charles X of France to spare her son this dark fate and abolish slavery. However, even though the National Convention did abolish slavery in 1794, Napoléon Bonaparte then reintroduced it to most of the territories under French control.

f4ee2a86-2553-5a0f-a698-a195e71a3ffd.name: Treaty of the French Protectorate, 12 May 1881
f4ee2a86-2553-5a0f-a698-a195e71a3ffd.short_description: This drawing shows an important moment in modern Tunisian history: the signing of the treaty of the French Protectorate over the Tunisian regency, at the Palais Kassar Saïd, in Bardo, on 12 May 1881. The main players are featured in this drawing, namely Sadok Bey who ruled Tunisia from 1859 to 1882, with his hand resting on the table, and to his right the general Jules Aimé Bréart, the leader of the invading French troops.

f5bf8d60-ea7d-51ea-b865-00084437d439.short_description: Women were very active in trade unions. In 1906, a woman, Argentina Altobelli, became secretary general of the National Federation of Agricultural Workers (Federazione nazionale dei lavoratori della terra).

f6ba7168-fb9b-59f4-96f4-181869aa5b52.name: *The Battle on Dealu Spirii*
f6ba7168-fb9b-59f4-96f4-181869aa5b52.short_description: In June 1848 revolution broke out in Wallachia. In terms of relations with the Ottoman Empire, Wallachia’s suzerain, revolutionaries claimed the administrative and legislative independence of the country. In the autumn, as negotiations with the revolutionaries proved unsuccessful, the Sublime Porte decided to intervene militarily. On the 13th of September, Bucharest was attacked. The battle that took place on Dealu Spirii between the Ottoman army and the Romanian soldiers helped by a company of firefighters was won by the former. Afterwards, the Ottoman sovereignty over the Romanian countries was re-imposed. The lithograph is entitled *The fight of the Romanian soldiers with the numerous column of the Ottoman army* and below the drawing a short text describes the battle.

f6ce25ef-e196-51ea-878e-f582be55dc3a.name: Petrie and typology
f6ce25ef-e196-51ea-878e-f582be55dc3a.short_description: In 1890 Petrie carried out a six-week season of excavations at Tell el-Hesy (as he transliterated it), which he identified, wrongly, as the ancient city of Lachish.  This was the first proper archaeological excavation ever carried out in Palestine, and in the course of this single season Petrie established the principle of dating strata by the pottery which they contained, thus establishing the outlines of the archaeological sequence, which continues to be refined to this day. This section drawing was made by Frederick Jones Bliss, who continued Petrie’s excavations from 1892–1894.

f6f098bc-4e9c-5171-b766-ca9c47aabe50.name: New maps
f6f098bc-4e9c-5171-b766-ca9c47aabe50.short_description: Sgt. George Armstrong, R.E., who was a key member of the Survey Party, later made a 3D ‘Raised Contour Map’ of Palestine from the 2D maps originally produced. This was shown all over the western world, and won him a medal at the St. Louis World’s Fair in 1903. It was the first such map ever constructed of Palestine, and served to introduce scholars and the public to the nature of the landscape in a way that no previous maps had done.

f7cee5d1-1e01-5071-9419-091425349403.name: Dictionary of Three Languages
f7cee5d1-1e01-5071-9419-091425349403.short_description: The *Dictionary of Three Languages* by Gjorgji Pullevski (1822–1893) shows the political context and coexistence of Macedonians, Albanians and Turks in the territory of Macedonia. It also provides evidence of the awakening of the national spirit of Macedonian people. The dictionary has 190 pages in paperback. It gives words in Macedonian, Albanian and Turkish in three columns. Despite its orthographic errors, the dictionary provides a valuable source for studying of the evolution of the Macedonian language.
f7cee5d1-1e01-5071-9419-091425349403.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)

f939b530-8866-5fba-afa5-e436e2211419.name: Rich drawing
f939b530-8866-5fba-afa5-e436e2211419.short_description: Portrait of a standing male Yezidi from Sinjar. Claudius Rich made observations and drawings not only of sites but also of people. Early travellers often studied the customs and costumes of local peoples, as well as drawing landscapes or mapping territories. There was no such thing as a professional archaeologist yet.

f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.name: *Arabs of the Desert*
f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.short_description: The constant movement of large Bedouin confederations regularly impacted on the history of the Middle East, in particular when it affected settled societies and cities.This print provides much interesting detail about the dress of the Bedouin at the time David Roberts visited the Near East in 1838/9. The individual in the foreground wears a white turban and short gown with belt, a dark red jacket and a voluminous, all-enveloping blue cloak. His legs remain uncovered, and he wears simple leather sandals on his feet. A formidable dagger or khanjar in its sheath is secured in his belt, and he carries a long slender gun through a sling. The bullets for the gun appear to be secured in an ammunition belt strapped diagonally across his chest. In the background, four male figures wearing striped headscarfs and cloaks as well as short white gowns and holdings lances appear on the right. On the left, a bedouin leads his camels away. The inscription states: *Arabs of the tribe of Benisaid, Feb. 17th 1839*.

f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.name: *Théâtre du Châtelet. Germinal*
f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.short_description: The thirteenth novel in the *Rougon-Macquart* series, *Germinal* (1885), is the most well-known and the most discussed of Zola's works. This naturalist writer took a new approach to depicting workers' lives, shedding light on miners' terrible working conditions and the violence and difficulty of strikes. Fearing that the adaptation of this novel for stage would trigger social unrest, the play was initially banned. It was finally performed for the first time in 1888 at the Théâtre du Châtelet. This poster highlights the most important themes of the novel - life in the mine, strikes, etc.

fa167dcd-aecd-50c2-9f06-7fb3d8cf9248.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
fa167dcd-aecd-50c2-9f06-7fb3d8cf9248.short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

fb2abd3f-4014-5c92-a525-a24db70c968b.name: Map of the 1877–1878 war
fb2abd3f-4014-5c92-a525-a24db70c968b.short_description: This map shows the theatre of operations during the Russian-Ottoman war of 1877–1878, which for Romania represents her independence war. In April 1877, Romania signed a secret military convention with Russia, who was on the eve of a new war with the Ottoman Empire, allowing her troops to cross the Romanian territory in order to get south of the Danube. Because in May the Ottomans bombed some Romanian ports on the Danube without a previous war declaration, the Parliament proclaimed Romania’s independence and decided the country’s entrance in the war. By the beginning of 1878, the Russo-Romanian army was victorious. At the peace Congress of Berlin (June-July 1878) Romania’s independence was recognized, but she had to cede Russia the south of Bessarabia in exchange for a part of Dobruja.

fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.name: *The Storming of a large Storehouse near Rus al-Khyma where Capt Dancey of H. M. 65th Regt was killed. Nov. 13th 1809*
fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.short_description: This dramatic scene was recorded by a British soldier participating in the siege and destruction of Ras al-Khaimah, the main stronghold of the Qawasim empire in the lower Gulf. It shows a British contingent, armed with musket guns attacking a large, fortress-like building, surrounded by small dwellings, traditionally built of palm fronds and known as areesh. A soldier in the foreground is taking aim at a local fighter on the roof of the building, while he in turn is defending himself by launching a sharpened log in the attacker's direction. The actual subject of the image, however, is the striken soldier with a headwound, Captain M.M. Dansey, hit by a spear according to eye witnesses and attended to by his comrades in the centre. Nevertheless, after the attacks, the British prided themselves in their 'trifling losses' while estimating that 'from seventy to eighty' of the Qawasim Arabs were killed, and 'many must have fallen in the previous bombardment'.

fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.name: *The railway*
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.short_description: Epinal prints take their name from the eponymous town in the Vosges region of France. These stencil-coloured lithographies with simple designs became very popular during the 19th century, thanks to their modest price and popular themes. This particular print is aimed at explaining the new railway system to rural communities, by illustrating the different jobs related to this mode of transport (station master, porter), and the types of people interested in faster transportation (soldiers, tourists, merchants). The different classes (from first to third) and their varying levels of comfort are also shown. This helped dispel and ridicule the fear transport had evoked.

fbde1ba4-0cc0-547e-9260-e7d47c092d47.name: Picture postcard, *Greetings from Pirot*
fbde1ba4-0cc0-547e-9260-e7d47c092d47.description: A picture postcard with the Cyrillic inscription *Pozdrav iz Pirota* (*Greetings from Pirot*) shows a woman from Pirot weaving a kilim, with a child standing by her side. Pirot, a town in south-eastern Serbia, was an important centre of kilim weaving in the Balkans. Pirot kilims were woven on vertical looms (as the one shown in the picture) with a slit weave technique (*klečanje*), which renders both front and back of a weave even and identical. It took one to ten weavers to weave a kilim, depending on its dimensions. The kilims were made of fine, thinly and evenly spun wool which, until 1880’s, was exclusively processed at homes. One of their major characteristics are the studied coloristic effects, achieved by choice and distribution of colours. Natural herb dyes were replaced by the aniline ones at the beginning of the 20th century.
fbde1ba4-0cc0-547e-9260-e7d47c092d47.method_for_datation: Ref. Perać, J., *Razglednice u Srbiji 1895–1914 = Postcards in Serbia 1895–1914*, Belgrade: Museum of Applied Art, 2009.

fc0202a4-85ca-5193-af7d-ee6857a9426b.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911), Colonel Ali Fahmi Bey, Colonel Abdellal Hilmi Bey
fc0202a4-85ca-5193-af7d-ee6857a9426b.short_description: Portrait of minister Arabi (Urabi) together with two officers. In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.name: The villa of Paul Draneht in Oggebbio (Verbania, Italy)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.short_description:
In 1872, Paul Draneht Bey bought a Villa on the Lago Maggiore (Italy), which he remodelled, mixing oriental and European architectural styles. From this postcard, one can see a tower with an Arabic flavour.  
In the interior, there was an “Egyptian hall”, modelled according to the style of an ancient Upper-Egypt temple. The furniture was made by one of the shops in Paris that was making the scenes for the opera *Aida*.

fd4f4f6c-55c9-53ba-b261-f3fda9387dc4.name: The Chapel of the Mihrab at the Oratory of the Cathedral of Cordoba Reproduced by Mr Giuseppe Botana with Pieces of Mother-of-pearl and Shells [Paris Exhibition 1878]

The Chapel of the Mihrab is a faithful reconstruction of the Mihrab in the beautiful mosque built in Cordoba by the Amir Abd al Rahman I above the previous Christian church. The decoration was created by Giuseppe Botana, who specialised in mother-of-pearl works, and by Zuloaga's, a mosaics' maker.

fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.name: The Empress visits the Orient
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.short_description: The Empress Eugénie (Napoléon III's wife) stopped off in Istanbul on her way to Suez, where she was representing France at the inauguration of the Suez Canal. This visit marked the beginning of improving relations between France and Turkey. Eugénie was received with great respect and visited all the great monuments of the city. A fervent Catholic, she could not resist stopping off at the Hagia Sophia mosque, which had once been an Orthodox cathedral.

feb66ca9-ced9-518b-8f58-1ac129aebdd4.name: Lazar Sozich (2nd half of the 19th century – 1900)
feb66ca9-ced9-518b-8f58-1ac129aebdd4.short_description: Portrait of Lazar Sozich. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.name: *Navis nundinaria* (The trading ship)
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.alternate_name: A ship-shaped theatre for the roast pork feast of 1657
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.description:
The *Insignia degli Anziani Consoli*, bound in 16 volumes and housed in the Archivio di Stato Bologna, are documents on parchment. They were made every two months, from 1530 to 1796, to celebrate the eight Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere di Giustizia, a group of magistrates ruling the city. From the end of the sixteenth-century, the names of the magistrates were depicted flanked by their coats of arms and a significant event that had taken place during the two months of their charge: an extraordinary visual chronicle illustrating more than two centuries of the city's history with six pictures a year.  
This picture (IV bimester of 1657) shows the stage for the roast pork feast. Celebrated every year on the 24th of August, a special installation was ssembled on the main square to host the feast of St. Bartholomew. In 1657 the theatre was shaped as a ship and was occupying nearly all the square, between the palace of the Podestà on the left and the stairs of the basilica of St. Petronius on the right. Along the sides of the ship were the stalls for the feast of the Assumption (from 15th to 24th August) that were going to become on the 24th boxes for the paying audience watching a theatrical representation and taking part in the traditional distribution of roast pork. On the mast waves the flag of the Municipality, under it a standard shows the coats of arms of Pope Alexander VII among those of the cardinal legate and of the archbishop of Bologna. On the aft deck a tent hosts the nine coats of arms of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere of the bimester July-August 1657. On top right a Latin inscription in golden ink describes the picture and bears the names of the Anziani Consoli.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.short_description: This illumination represents a theatre in the shape of a ship that was built on the Main Square of Bologna for the feast of the roast pork in August 1657. This was an event that attracted a great number of people every year. The ship sails are the coats of arms of the nine families of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere, who ruled Bologna in the bi-mester July-August 1657. On the left side of the ship, is the portico of the Palazzo del Podesta. In the background is the Pavaglione and the Palazzo dei Banchi.  The stairs on the right lead to the church of San Petronio.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.initial_owner: The Anziani Consoli of the town of Bologna
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.method_for_datation: The date and the names of the magistrates are inscribed on the top right of the picture.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.obtention: This illumination, like the whole series, has always been housed in the archive of the Bolognese senate, inside the municipal palace. It was transferred to the Archivio di Stato in 1874, when it was created.

ff28cb9b-b4cd-5d7f-8616-1983d1ba7e9b.name: *The last day of the Commune, Paris 1871*
ff28cb9b-b4cd-5d7f-8616-1983d1ba7e9b.short_description: The Parisians, who had spent many long months under siege, did not accept the armistice signed with Prussia in 1871. They rose up in revolt in March, as the government was hiding in Versailles. The "Commune" of Paris, which organised the city socially and politically, was thus created. Versailles fought the "communards" for two months. After a "bloody week" and the loss of thousands of lives and many deportations, the government finally regained control of the city, which continued until a general amnesty was reached in 1880. From this point onwards, the period - which had become a taboo - gradually began to be discussed. This poster from 1883 is advertising a play which enacted Paris' takeover by the Versaillais.
